_about: Generated by scripts/generate.js. Do not edit.

schema.title: SubjectRef
schema.description: The one cross-platform reference to an actor. Issued by OpenVibe.Network. Never a service-local integer id.

oneOf.description: UserSubject
GuestSubject
AppSubject
ModSubject
PrincipalSubject
AgentSubject: an agent (OpenVibe.Actor, or a developer app's agent) acting under grants its owner delegated (roadmap WS-Z2). In an event envelope, on_behalf_of names the owner.

schema.title: LegacyIdentityMapEntry
schema.description: One row of identity_legacy_map: links a service-local id to its canonical subject. Kept alongside legacy ids, never replacing them.

source_system.description: live, media, games, network, rs-companion, hobo, ...

schema.title: ServiceTokenClaims
schema.description: Claims of a short-lived RS256 client-credentials token issued by OpenVibe.Network to a service, app, mod, node or agent principal. Replaces X-Internal-Key. App tokens (actor_type app) also carry project_id and env; receivers refuse env=sandbox unless they opted in. Agent tokens (actor_type agent, sub agent:agt_<ULID>) are minted for the agent's host and also carry project_id, env and on_behalf_of (the owner), and optionally cap_confirm and act.

iss.description: Issuer; https://openvibe.network in production. Receivers pass the issuer they expect to verifyServiceToken().

cap.description: Granted capability ids; a trailing .* grants a family.

cap_confirm.description: Agent tokens: capabilities the agent holds in confirm mode. Each use needs an approved network.confirmation-request@1, presented as OpenVibe-Confirmation: cnf_<ULID> and consumed by the owning service. Never also in cap, so a receiver that does not know agents refuses those actions.

ns.description: Namespace constraints, e.g. live.* or mod.example.*. A developer app token carries its project_id (the whole project, as issued before namespaces were rows) and app.<project_id>.*: on Media, app.<project_id> and app.<project_id>.sandbox are the project's production and sandbox namespaces, with children below them.

project_id.description: Developer project of an app or agent principal (ADR-014). Services key tenancy by it. Absent on first-party service tokens.

env.description: Environment of an app or agent principal. A receiver MUST refuse env=sandbox (401 token.sandbox_refused) unless it opted in to sandbox tokens. Absent on first-party service tokens, which are production.

on_behalf_of.description: The person who authorized an app through the authorization-code flow, or the owner an agent acts for (always present on agent tokens). Absent on client_credentials tokens.

act.description: Agent tokens: the host that runs the agent and the token was minted for (RFC 8693 actor claim), a service or an app.

schema.title: RealtimeTicketClaims
schema.description: Claims of a realtime ticket (ADR-005 amendment 2; roadmap WS-E task 3, WS-F task 1): a two-minute RS256 JWT that OpenVibe.Network signs for the signed-in person (POST /api/v1/realtime/ticket) so a browser on any OpenVibe site can open Events' /realtime/stream?ticket=... as that person. A browser cannot put a header on an EventSource, and the ov_token cookie of openvibe.events is third-party on every other site, so the ticket travels in the URL; that is why it is short-lived, single-purpose and single-use. It is never a session token, by three independent rules: its issuer is Network's issuer followed by /realtime (every service checks the issuer of a session token), it carries typ (services refuse a session token that has one, as for FedCM assertions), and its only audience is openvibe.events. Events accepts it only as ?ticket= on /realtime/stream, verifies the signature with Network's key, iss, aud, typ, purpose and expiry (lifetime at most 300 s), refuses a jti it has already seen while the ticket is valid, and never logs it. The connection then sees what the person's session would: public events and subject events addressed to `sub`.

iss.description: Network's issuer followed by /realtime (https://openvibe.network/realtime in production): not the issuer of a session.

sub.description: The person's subject id; subject-visibility events for this subject reach the connection.

typ.description: Token class. A service that finds typ on a Network token does not treat it as a session.

purpose.description: Single purpose: opening one realtime stream.

exp.description: iat + 120 as Network mints it; Events refuses a lifetime over 300 s.

jti.description: Unique per ticket; Events accepts each once.

schema.title: IdentityResolveRequest
schema.description: identity.resolve-request@1: the request of identity.subject.resolve on OpenVibe.Network. GET /internal/identity/resolve?subject_id= or ?system=&id=[&type=user] takes no body. POST /internal/identity/resolve-batch: { subject_ids } or { system, type?, ids } (at most 500; 413 beyond).

schema.title: IdentityResolveResult
schema.description: identity.resolve-result@1: answers of identity.subject.resolve on OpenVibe.Network. GET /internal/identity/resolve → one identity.subject-projection@1 (404 identity.subject_not_found when nothing matches); POST /internal/identity/resolve-batch → { results } keyed by each id asked, null for an id that resolves to nothing.

schema.title: IdentitySubjectProjection
schema.description: identity.subject-projection@1: what OpenVibe.Network's identity resolver answers about a subject (server/identity/subjects.js resolve): the SubjectRef, the Network account behind it, its display fields, whether it is banned, and every legacy id mapped to it.

schema.title: EntityRef
schema.description: Typed reference to another service's entity. Store this instead of a foreign key; resolve a display projection from the owner.

schema.title: Problem
schema.description: RFC 9457 problem details (application/problem+json) with a stable OpenVibe error code and trace identifiers. The legacy 'error' string is allowed during migration so existing clients keep working.

error.description: Deprecated compatibility field: same text as title/detail for clients that read {error}.

schema.title: ServiceManifest
schema.description: What a service is, where it lives and what it offers. The ecosystem registry is built from these, not from hard-coded route maps.

internalOrigin.description: Where the service answers on its host (loopback only): the address the registry polls health and readiness from. A host inventory or an OV_<ID>_INTERNAL_URL loopback override may replace it; a service with nothing to run has none.

exposure.description: Where the service can actually be reached today, which is separate from its maturity (status): live (its public domain serves it), internal (loopback only; the domain, if any, still serves a placeholder), library (a released package), repository (code with CI, nothing released or run), placeholder (charter only) or retired. When a service goes public, this changes in the same release that points its domain at it.

publicSite.description: What the public domain answers today: the service itself, a placeholder page, or nothing (no public domain).

package.description: For a library: the npm package name.

repo.description: For a library: the OpenVibers repository its release tags live in.

site.description: How the network presents the service as a site people visit (the navigation, the network home page, legal pages). A service without it is not a site. 1.1.0 (plan T11 lane D) adds the optional showcase fields copied from the OpenVibe.Sites catalog (tld, accent, description, pillars, faq, keywords, vision, highlight, launch, relationships; defined in registry.product@1): a site carrying tld is the catalog home of its domain (its publicOrigin host, or host), so that domain has no manifests/products file.

name.description: Short name after 'OpenVibe.' (or a full name containing a dot).

legalProfile.description: Which legal wording its /terms, /privacy and /dmca use (openvibe-shared/legal).

host.description: Only while the manifest has no publicOrigin.

neighbourhood.description: The room's launcher group in OpenVibe.Shared rooms.js and OpenVibe.Network frame/sites.js; optional so older manifests retain their meaning.

lifecycle.description: How the service starts, stops, recovers and is rolled back (roadmap WS-P task 1), taken from its code and its systemd units, never from intent. A part that does not apply is { "none": "<why>" }. `ovhost validate` refuses a host service whose lifecycle lacks a field, whose shutdown deadline exceeds its unit's TimeoutStopSec, or whose installed openvibe-contracts is outside contracts.range.

liveness.description: The endpoint that says the process is alive, and what a 200 from it proves. Readiness (can it serve?) is `ready`.

endpoint.description: A path on internalOrigin; the same as `health`.

means.description: What a 200 proves, and what it does not check.

oneOf.description: No liveness endpoint, and why (a library, a static site, a retired service, or code that has none).

shutdown.description: What happens between the stop signal and the process exiting.

signal.description: The signal the unit sends (KillSignal=, systemd's default SIGTERM) and the process handles.

deadlineSeconds.description: The longest the process takes from the signal to exiting, as its own code bounds it (a forced-exit timer); 0 when it exits at once. Must not exceed the unit's TimeoutStopSec, after which systemd kills it mid-drain.

drains.description: What it stops, finishes, flushes or closes before exiting, in order.

workers.description: Worker units the service owns that drain on their own (ovhost never restarts them): how long a stop signal lets them run.

deadlineSeconds.description: The longest a worker keeps running after the stop signal, as its code bounds it.

drains.description: What a worker keeps serving, and what it ends, before exiting.

note.description: Anything the fields above do not say (a gap the code has, a handler that is missing).

oneOf.description: No shutdown sequence, and why (a library, a static site, a retired service, or code that has none).

startupRecovery.description: Work a stop or a crash interrupted that the next start picks up.

resumes.description: Each thing the process resumes at boot.

kind.description: outbox: unsent events; jobs: queued or interrupted background work; sessions: client connections or media sessions; consumer: an event or change feed redelivered or read from a stored cursor; schedule: timed work that fell due; state: in-memory state rebuilt from storage.

oneOf.description: No startup recovery, and why (a library, a static site, a retired service, or code that has none).

rollback.description: When a release is rolled back, for how long that happens by itself, and what makes going back unsafe.

conditions.description: What triggers a rollback: automatic (readiness not reached after the restart) and manual.

window.description: How long after a deploy the rollback is automatic, and what bounds a manual one.

blockers.description: Changes a previous release cannot live with (forward-only migrations, table rebuilds, authority switches), or { none } with the reason.

oneOf.description: No rollback blockers, and why (a library, a static site, a retired service, or code that has none).
No rollback, and why (a library, a static site, a retired service, or code that has none).

contracts.description: The openvibe-contracts versions the service accepts.

range.description: The accepted versions, the same range as contractRanges['openvibe-contracts'].

note.description: Where the range comes from, when it is not the obvious one.

oneOf.description: No contracts range, and why (a library, a static site, a retired service, or code that has none).

leases.description: What the service claims so that one owner acts at a time, and how a stale owner is fenced.

claims.description: Each thing claimed, with its holder, expiry and fencing.

holder.description: Who holds the claim (a process, a worker id, a row).

expires.description: When the claim lapses and how it is renewed.

fencing.description: How a stale owner is kept from acting after its claim lapsed.

oneOf.description: No leases, and why (a library, a static site, a retired service, or code that has none).

schema.title: Product
schema.description: A product domain of the network's catalog (manifests/products/<domain>.json) that has no service manifest presenting it as a site: a planned product, a sub-domain of a service, a brand domain of a multi-domain service, a closed or moved address. Carries what the network's showcase pages need, copied from the OpenVibe.Sites catalog (plan T11 lane D) so Sites can be deleted. A product whose service manifest has a site block carries the same fields there (registry.service-manifest 1.1.0 site); every catalog domain has exactly one of the two homes. The $defs are shared with that site block.

domain.description: The product's host, unique across the catalog.

name.description: Full name, e.g. OpenVibe.Food.

icon.description: Icon name of the showcase pages (a Font Awesome name such as fa-utensils).

legalProfile.description: Which legal wording its /terms, /privacy and /dmca use (openvibe-shared/legal), as in a service manifest's site.

kind.description: Absent for a product page. closed: the address was decided against and points elsewhere; moved: the product lives at another address; status: the address shows the network's status. relationships.links say where.

tld.description: The product's short name used everywhere (frame service names, /shared paths), e.g. food for openvibe.food. Not unique: a moved product keeps it on both addresses.

launch.description: What a person still has to do or decide before the product launches. Absent once nothing blocks it.

highlight.description: A featured block on the product page.

vision.description: The product page's vision section (badge, call to action, design preview, steps, choices, features, connections), kept verbatim from the catalog: a presentation payload the showcase renders as it is, not a domain contract.

relationships.description: How the product relates to services, repositories and other pages.

service.description: The service manifest (manifests/services/<id>.json) that serves or will serve this product, when one exists.

plannedRepo.description: The repository planned or used for the product (under github.com/OpenVibers).

noRepo.description: No repository exists for the product yet.

links.description: Where to go instead (a closed, moved or status address).

meanwhile.description: What already works elsewhere on the network while the product is not launched.

statusApi.description: The status API a status page reads.

schema.title: Capability
schema.description: An action a principal may invoke. Authorization is checked at the owner's boundary against the grant, never inferred from the caller's route.

implementedBy.description: Current route(s) that perform this action today, e.g. 'POST /api/v1/:app/files'.

sensitive.description: The action has an external side effect (money, sending as the person, publishing, applying, deleting, physical control): an agent needs its owner's confirmation unless a standing rule covers it (roadmap WS-Z2).

schema.title: EventEnvelope
schema.description: Durable platform event (OpenVibe.Events, Wave 3). Producers write it to an outbox in the same transaction as the domain change.

schema.title: MediaRef
schema.description: Reference to a Media object. Canonical ids (med_<ULID>) arrive with the Wave 4 object model; until then legacy:<app>:<kind>:<id> addresses today's VOD/clip/file/paste/thumbnail rows.

schema.title: LineageResolveRequest
schema.description: What a caller knows about a channel, stream, VOD, clip or Media object, sent to the canonical channel/owner resolver (roadmap §15.10, requirement D20): the body of POST /internal/lineage/resolve on OpenVibe.Live (capability live.lineage.resolve). GET takes the same fields as query parameters, with legacy_ids flattened to live_user_id and network_user_id. The answer is lineage.resolution@1, whose description has the precedence rules. Every input given is checked, not only the first. display_name is never a resolution input: a request that carries only a display name resolves nothing (reason display_name_only), and next to other inputs it is ignored.

slug.description: Channel slug (Live: the username, as in /@<username>; the @ is optional), or a nested <channel>/<slot> naming a stream slot inside the channel by its slug or id. With parent_slug, a plain slug names the slot inside that parent.

parent_slug.description: The channel slug when slug names a slot inside it ({ parent_slug: 'alice', slug: 'garage' } is 'alice/garage'). Alone, it names the channel.

channel_id.description: The channel's id at its owner (Live: channels.id).

slot_id.description: A persistent stream slot (Live: managed_streams.id; OpenRestream stream definitions refer to it as live:managed_stream:<id>).

vod_id.description: A VOD (the Media v1 VOD id, the same id Live's VODs had before the Media split).

clip_id.description: A clip (the Media v1 clip id). A clip belongs to the clipped channel, never to the person who clipped it.

media_object_id.description: A Media object: med_<ULID>, or a legacy:<app>:<kind>:<id> reference (the media_id forms of media.media-ref@1).

owner_subject.description: The canonical subject that owns the channel (identity.subject-ref@1 user id).

legacy_ids.description: Pre-subject ids of the channel owner. Resolving through them is confidence legacy_map.

network_user_id.description: OpenVibe.Network's integer user id, mapped to a Live account by the account link.

display_name.description: A label the caller holds. Accepted so the answer can say display_name_only; never used to resolve anything, because a display name is not an identity and is never sufficient to establish ownership.

schema.title: LineageResolution
schema.description: The canonical channel/owner resolver's answer to lineage.resolve-request@1 (roadmap §15.10, requirement D20; capability live.lineage.resolve). One resolver serves channel, stream, VOD, clip, Pulse and creator-UI callers. PRECEDENCE between inputs (the roadmap's order): 1 explicit_slug (slug), 2 nested_slug (slug <channel>/<slot>, or parent_slug), 3 channel_id, 4 stream_lookup (stream_id, then slot_id), 5 the record's own lineage (clip_id, then vod_id), 6 media_lineage (media_object_id), 7 owner_subject, 8 legacy_map (legacy_ids). The first input in that order that resolves decides (resolved_by). Every other input that resolves must name the same channel, otherwise the answer is unresolved with reason conflict. An input whose source could not be asked makes the answer unresolved with reason source_unavailable, since it might have disagreed. An input that names nothing is reported not_found in checked and does not block the others. LINEAGE inside a record, first link that answers wins: a stream belongs to its owner, and a slot too; a VOD goes to its stream, then to its slot when the stream row is gone, then to the owner recorded on the VOD (legacy_metadata); a clip goes to its stream, then to its parent VOD's lineage (vod_parent), then to the channel recorded on the clip (legacy_metadata), and never to the clipper; a Media object goes to the record its legacy_ref names (media_lineage), then to its owner subject, then to the owner user recorded on it (legacy_metadata); a legacy:<app>:<kind>:<id> reference is read as that record (legacy_map). CONFIDENCE is the weakest hop: exact when the input itself names the channel, a stream or slot row, or the owner subject; derived when the answer came through a parent record or an owner recorded on a record; legacy_map when it needed a legacy id map (legacy_ids, a legacy media reference). A display name never resolves anything. Unresolved answers carry no channel.

reason.description: Why nothing resolved. no_input: the request named nothing. display_name_only: only a display name was given. not_found: no input names anything that exists. conflict: two inputs name different channels. ambiguous: an input names more than one channel (an owner subject linked to two accounts). source_unavailable: a record could not be read (Media down); retry later.

id.description: The channel's id at its owner (Live: channels.id).

slug.description: The channel's current slug (Live: the username, /@<slug>). Slugs can change; id and owner_subject do not.

owner_subject.description: The owner's canonical subject, or null while the owner has not signed in through OpenVibe.Network since subjects were issued.

legacy_ids.description: The owner's pre-subject ids, for callers that still key by them.

id.description: The broadcast session, or null when only a slot was named.

missing.description: true when a record names this stream but the stream row no longer exists.

rule.description: The lineage rule that answered for the deciding input.

via.description: The hops the deciding input took, e.g. ["clip:7", "vod:42", "slot:3", "user:17"].

checked.description: What each input given came to.

channel_slug.description: The channel this input named, when it named one.

schema.title: ModuleNamespace
schema.description: Policy for one user-module namespace: portable per-subject summaries and preferences stored by OpenVibe.Network. Never domain truth, money or authoritative game inventory (roadmap 4.3-4.5). The person's account decides what happens to their records in every namespace: when an account is removed, Network deletes all of its records; when two accounts are merged (ADR-029), in a namespace where both have a record the survivor keeps its own and gains only the top-level fields it lacks from the other (its own values always win), a record only the absorbed account had moves to the survivor, and the absorbed account's records are deleted. Each of these changes is announced as network.module.updated (reason subject_removed or subject_merged). That is separate from onOwnerRemoved, which says what happens to a namespace's records when the service that owns the namespace is retired.

owner.description: Service that owns the namespace and may write it with network.modules.write.

version.description: Schema version stored with every record; a change needs a migration note.

schema.description: JSON Schema (2020-12) every stored value must satisfy.

writers.description: owner = the owning service with a token; user = the subject themselves.

publicFields.description: Top-level fields anyone may read. Everything else is readable only by the subject and granted services.

onOwnerRemoved.description: What happens to records when the owning service or mod is retired.

migration.description: How records of the previous version are upgraded.

readers.description: Field-level read rules: a service other than the owner, holding network.modules.read for the namespace, sees publicFields plus the fields listed for it here, and nothing else. A service not listed sees publicFields only. The owner and the person always see the whole record.

migrations.description: Declarative upgrades from each earlier version, applied in order when a stored record's version is below the namespace's: rename moves a field, drop removes fields, defaults adds fields the record lacks. Network upgrades a record when it is read and stores the upgraded record on its next write.

schema.title: ModuleRecord
schema.description: One subject's value in one namespace, as returned by Network. revision increases by one on every write; a write names the revision it read (If-Match) and fails with 412 if it moved.

schema.title: ReleaseManifest
schema.description: What a running web surface is serving (GET /release.json, ADR-016). Open clients compare it on focus and reconnect. A client outside the supported window is prompted and reloads only when that is safe. Since 1.1.0 the manifest can also say which components changed, so a client can apply style and content changes in place, and which contract versions the server still accepts, so a mixed-version population can be checked.

contracts_version.description: openvibe-contracts version the service runs against.

packages.description: Versions of the platform packages the page loads (openvibe-shared, openvibe-sdk, ...).

min_client_release.description: Oldest client release still supported; null while every client in the window is.

components.description: Since 1.1.0. Per-component versions. A client applies a new release in place only when every component that changed is a style, content or server component and the contract ranges still match. Any other change is applied by a reload at a safe moment. The shell component covers every client-facing file that no other component lists.

kind.description: style: stylesheets, swapped in place. content: server-rendered regions (data-ov-content), re-fetched in place. script: code the page runs, applied by a reload. server: code only the server runs, no client action.

version.description: Content hash of the component's files, or a version the service states.

assets.description: Since 1.1.0. Asset map: each logical URL path the release serves, mapped to its content-addressed URL. HTML from this release references only these URLs.

schema_generation.description: Since 1.1.0. The database schema generation this release migrates to and runs against; null when the service does not track one.

schema_compatible_from.description: Since 1.1.0. The oldest schema generation whose code still runs against this release's schema, because every migration since then only expanded it. Rolling back to a release whose schema_generation is lower is not data-safe.

contract_ranges.description: Since 1.1.0. For each contract the service produces (its API, as served to its own pages and clients) or consumes: the version this release speaks and the range of versions it accepts from the other side. A page from release A works against a server on release B when, for every contract A produces, A's version is in B's accepts and B's version is in A's accepts.

metrics_url.description: Since 1.1.0. Same-origin URL where clients POST their update outcome counts (applied, reloaded, deferred, failed); null or absent when the service does not collect them.

client_generation.description: Since 1.2.0. The generation of the client this release serves (its pages and scripts). It goes up only when an older client can no longer work against this server; the page carries it in the ov-release meta tag's data-generation. Null when the service does not track one.

min_client_generation.description: Since 1.2.0. Oldest client generation still supported: an open tab whose generation is lower reloads at the next safe moment (reason required), without waiting for the mixed-version window. Null when every generation in the window is.

shell.description: Since 1.2.0. The page shell (layout, router, navigation): the ids of the components that make it up and one version over them. A tab whose shell version differs never updates in place; it is prompted, and reloads only when it must. Null when the service names no shell.

version.description: The first 12 hex of SHA-256 over the shell components' ids and versions, in id order.

schema.title: NoBody
schema.description: common.no-body@1: the capability's request carries no body; its parameters are the path and query of the routes in implementedBy (an id, a page cursor). An input schema that says so explicitly, so every active capability names one (roadmap WS-C task 4).

schema.title: Binary
schema.description: common.binary@1: the response is the resource's bytes, not JSON — Content-Type names the media type, Content-Length (or Range with 206) the size. An error is still an application/problem+json body. A declaration for capabilities that serve files (roadmap WS-C task 4); there is nothing to validate but the headers.

schema.title: ConfigSnapshot
schema.description: One immutable revision of one service's configuration namespace (roadmap WS-C task 7; kept by openvibe-shared/config). A revision's values never change: revisions grow by one per namespace, and a rollback is a new revision that copies an older one's values. Only the state moves: proposed -> active -> superseded or rolled_back, or proposed -> rejected when validation or activation fails, in which case the previous active revision stays or is restored. A secret-class key's value never appears here: it is { redacted: true, fingerprint }, an HMAC-SHA256 of the value under a secret key the service keeps per namespace, so equal fingerprints within one namespace mean the value did not change, while the value cannot be recovered or guessed offline without that key. checksum is the sha256 of the canonical JSON (keys sorted, no whitespace) of values exactly as they appear here, secrets as their markers, so anyone can check it, and two snapshots of one namespace with the same checksum hold the same configuration.

previous_revision.description: The revision that was active when this one was proposed; null for the namespace's first.

values.description: The configuration, one member per key. A secret-class key's value is a redaction marker.

additionalProperties.description: Any JSON value. An object with a redacted member is a redaction marker, and nothing else.

fingerprint.description: HMAC-SHA256 (hex) of the canonical JSON of the value, keyed with the namespace's secret key: equal within one namespace when the value is unchanged, and not recoverable or guessable without the key.

anyOf.description: A redacted secret-class value.

classification.description: Every key of values, classified. A key the service does not classify is internal.

checksum.description: sha256 (hex) of the canonical JSON of values as they appear in this snapshot (secrets as their markers).

activated_at.description: When it became active; null while proposed, and for a rejected revision.

error.description: Why it was rejected: the validation errors, or what activation reported. Never a secret value.

copied_from.description: A rollback's source: the revision whose values this one copies.

schema.title: ModerationAction
schema.description: common.moderation-action@1 (ADR-022, roadmap WS-D task 1): one staff or moderator action on someone else's content or account, as a service reports it to OpenVibe.Network's moderation audit log. The payload of every <service>.moderation.action event that has no older shape of its own (tools, games, wiki, blog, news, reviews, deals, coupons, trade, codes); modelled on community.moderation.action@1. Written to the service's outbox in the transaction that performs the action. A person acting on their own content is not moderation and is not reported. Envelope: subject { type: moderation_action, id: <target type>:<target id> }, visibility internal, actor the staff member. Never carries the content itself, a secret or an address.

action.description: A short verb id, as the service names it: <thing>.<what happened> (post.hidden, user.banned, release.revoked, guard.blocked).

type.description: What was acted on, in the service's own words (post, page, release, user, player, …).

owner_subject.description: Whose content or account it was, when known.

actor_subject.description: The staff member or moderator (null only for a service acting without a person).

details.description: Per action: the fields changed, the previous and new state, a bulk action's count, … never the content.

schema.title: UsageRecorded
schema.description: common.usage-recorded@1 (roadmap WS-N task 4, ADR-014): one rollup of a developer project's use of one capability in one environment over one closed window (an hour or a day), as the service that owns the capability counted it. The payload of every <service>.usage.recorded event; OpenVibe.Network adds them up per project and day for the project's dashboard on OpenVibe.Codes. The producer counts in the transaction that does its own accounting (a job's end, a stored event, a delivery attempt) and writes the rollup to its outbox after the window has closed: never one event per request. Totals, not deltas: a later event with the same key (source, project_id, env, capability, resource, dimension, unit, window_start) replaces the earlier one, and a lower revision never replaces a higher one. Envelope: subject { type: project, id: <project_id> }, visibility internal, priority low, actor the producing service. Never carries a subject id, an address, a session, a request's input or content, or a file name. Rollups are counts for dashboards and quotas, never money: Billing never consumes any *.usage.recorded topic, and a service that bills posts platform.usage-sample readings (billing.usage.record).

project_id.description: The developer project whose app token did the work.

env.description: The environment of that app token.

capability.description: The capability the usage counts against: tools.job.create, tools.tool.run, events.app.publish, events.app.subscribe.

dimension.description: Optional finer key inside the capability, as the producer names it: a job type (img.process) or a tool id (image-resize). Never the id of a person, an app, a request or a job.

resource.description: Optional resource name (ADR-034 section 2) of the project resource the usage counts against, so a dashboard or quota can group a count by resource (rollups are counts, never money; Billing never consumes them and rates only platform.usage-sample readings): ovrn:zone:<project_id>:object-zone/<zon_id> on Media's per-zone rollups (ADR-031 amendment 2026-10-02). Its project is project_id: a resource of another project is refused (contracts.usage.checkUsageRecorded). Added in 1.1.0. Never the resource name of a person, an app, a request or a job.

unit.description: What quantity counts (jobs, events, deliveries, requests, bytes, tokens): the same word a Network project quota uses for its unit.

window_start.description: UTC, on the hour (midnight for a day).

quantity.description: Units used in the window, by work that succeeded and work that failed alike.

errors.description: Operations in the window that failed or were refused: a job that failed, a publish refused with a problem, a webhook attempt without a 2xx. A refused operation may use no unit, so errors can exceed quantity.

error_codes.description: The errors by problem code (at most 20 codes; the rest are only in errors).

samples.description: The last failures of the window, newest first, so a developer can find them in their own logs.

status.description: The HTTP status the failure was answered with, when there was one.

trace_id.description: The W3C trace id of the request (or event) that failed.

ref.description: What failed, when the project can look it up with its own token: a job, an event, an AI run, a Media object. Never a subject.

revision.description: 1 when absent. A producer that re-emits a window with corrected totals raises it.

schema.title: MediaFileUpload
schema.description: media.file-upload@1: the multipart/form-data body of POST /api/v1/:app/files (media.object.upload, namespace :app): one part named `file` with the bytes and its filename and type. The tenant's quota is checked against the bytes; the answer is media.file@1 (201).

file.description: The multipart part named file (filename and Content-Type from the part).

schema.title: IndexDocument
schema.description: What an owning service tells OpenVibe.Search about one of its resources (roadmap §15.12, §4.2 A). The owner stays the source of truth; Search keeps a revision-ordered, permission-aware copy for discovery. A document with deleted=true is a tombstone: it removes the resource from every result and wins over any upsert with the same or an older revision.

owner.description: Owning service id (wiki, blog, news, community, sources…). Only that service may write the document.

type.description: Resource type inside the owner (page, post, story, entity, offer, coupon, instrument, item…).

id.description: Resource id inside owner+type. Stable across revisions.

revision.description: Owner's monotonic revision of the resource. An older revision never overwrites a newer one; at equal revision a deletion wins.

deleted.description: Deletion marker. true = tombstone; every other content field is ignored.

visibility.description: public: anyone. unlisted: never listed except to ACL matches; fetchable by exact id by a signed-in subject. members: subjects, groups or entitlements in acl. private: subjects in acl.subjects only. draft: never served.

acl.description: Who may see a non-public document. Ignored for public documents. Empty means nobody (for members/private) or direct-id only (for unlisted).

groups.description: Opaque group keys owned by some service, e.g. role:admin (Network role), wiki.space:spc_…:member.

entitlements.description: Entitlement keys (VIP/Billing), e.g. vip.plan:pln_…. Only a first-party service that just resolved them may present them for a viewer.

body.description: Plain text for full-text search (no HTML). Keep it under the Events payload limit when publishing through Events.

facets.description: Filterable values (category, tags, space, author subject, currency…). Filter with facet.<key>=<value>.

provenance.description: Where the content came from: typed references to source records (Sources items, citations, Media objects).

stub.description: true when the reference came from a stub provider; the document is then never indexable.

publication_state.description: Only published documents are ever served.

indexability.description: The owner's deterministic indexability decision (publishing packages, roadmap §32.3). Search can only make it stricter.

reasons.description: Known reasons: draft, private, members_only, unlisted, not_published, deleted, thin_content, duplicate_without_canonical, unsupported_claims, unsourced, stub_provider, sensitive_unreviewed, ai_unreviewed, missing_canonical_url, third_party_content, owner_decision.

schema.title: SearchQuery
schema.description: search.query@1: the query string of GET /api/v1/search (and, with q/owner/type/limit only, GET /api/v1/suggest), capabilities search.query.run and search.query.delegate. Who sees what is decided by Search per hit: anonymous callers get public, published, indexable documents; a person also restricted documents naming them; a delegating service passes X-OV-Subject. Filters narrow; they never widen visibility.

q.description: Words to match (FTS5; empty lists by recency).

owner.description: One owner service (live, community, wiki, …).

type.description: One document type within the owner (channel, vod, thread, …).

facets.description: Comma-separated facet keys to count over what the caller can see.

^facet\\.[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,39}$.description: A facet filter (facet.<key>=<value>); repeat the parameter for several values.

schema.title: SearchQueryResult
schema.description: search.query-result@1: the answer of GET /api/v1/search — one page of hits the caller may see, a cursor for the next page, and facet counts when asked. Never a total count and never an ACL.

indexable.description: false for a noindex document the caller may still see.

snippet_html.description: Escaped text with <mark> around the matches; nothing else.

ranks.description: 1-based position in the keyword and vector top-100 lists; null when absent from that list.

explain.description: How this page was ranked; reason is present only when ranking is keyword.

schema.title: SearchFabricRequest
schema.description: search.fabric-request@1: the body of POST /api/v1/query (or the query string of GET /api/v1/query, scopes comma-separated), capability search.fabric.query. One search over several scopes, routed the cheapest way that answers (plan 2026-10-28 §4.5). network: Search's own index, permission-aware exactly as search.query.run; mine: the caller's own private documents (a signed-in person, or a service with X-OV-Subject); web: OpenVibe's open index first, then paid providers in a ladder, each result keeping its provider, date and URL. Providers never receive an account identifier. A scope the caller may not use (mine without a person; web's paid providers for an anonymous caller, who gets cached and open-index results only) is reported in route.explain, never an error. The other scopes are facets of the same indexes and are accepted for forward compatibility; v1 answers them as network results filtered by kind.

scopes.description: Where to look; results are grouped by scope. Default: network.

filters.description: Narrow the network and mine scopes (never widen what the caller may see).

site.description: web: results from this host only.

freshness.description: How recent results must be, where the source dates them.

depth.description: quick: indexes and caches only (no paid provider); standard: the ladder until a step answers; deep: every step, merged.

answer.description: Ask for a short cited answer written by AI from the results. Never without citations; labelled AI. A deployment may decline (answer: null, with the reason in route.explain).

cursor.description: next_cursor of the previous page (network and mine only).

schema.title: SearchFabricResult
schema.description: search.fabric-result@1: the answer of search.fabric.query. results come grouped by scope order (the room's own first when the caller asked for it); every web result keeps its provider, URL and date; route.explain says, step by step, what was asked, what answered, from cache or not, and what it cost. The query is never echoed: a page renders results without writing the query into its HTML (the ?q= rule).

kind.description: document: in Search's index (owner, type, id set); page: a web page (provider set).

retrieved_at.description: When a web page was read (by the provider or the open index).

provider.description: page: who found it (open_index, deepseek, wikipedia, brave, …).

score.description: Rank within its scope (higher first); not comparable across scopes.

ranks.description: 1-based position in the keyword and vector top-100 lists; null when absent from that list.

groups.description: How many results each scope gave on this page.

label.const: Written by AI from these sources

skipped.description: Why the step did not run (not allowed for this caller, quick depth, an earlier step answered, provider standing down).

cost_usd.description: What this query cost OpenVibe (paid provider calls; cached answers cost 0).

schema.title: SearchProviderOffer
schema.description: search.provider-offer@1: one web search provider as the Search Fabric's ladder and Route see it (GET /api/v1/query/providers, capability search.fabric.query): what it covers, what it costs, whether it is usable now and how it has answered. Prices are the vendor's published ones as of checked_at; nothing here is a secret.

independent_index.description: Searches its own crawl rather than reselling another engine's.

available.description: Configured and not standing down (balance, key, rate limit, daily cap).

answered_rate.description: Share of calls in the last day that returned at least one result.

schema.title: SearchWriteResult
schema.description: search.write-result@1: the answer of PUT /api/v1/documents/:owner/:type/:id (search.document.write). applied: stored (or a tombstone recorded); unchanged: the same revision with the same content. A revision older than the stored one is a 409 problem search.stale_revision; the same revision with different content is 409 search.revision_conflict.

stored_revision.description: What Search held before this write (null: nothing).

schema.title: Source
schema.description: A registered source (roadmap §4.2 B, Wave 14): where it is fetched from and on what terms. Credentials are referenced by environment-variable NAME only. A source's existence is never permission to fetch: robots and terms are verified before it is enabled, and the fetcher re-checks robots.txt on every run.

format.description: json (default), xml, or tsv: a tab-separated file whose first line names the columns, read as an array of records keyed by those names (items_path is ""; BLS series files, Sources 2026-10-24).

duplicates.description: Two records with the same identity: first (default) keeps the first, last keeps the last in the first one's place (a file listing each series oldest to newest then yields its newest value; Sources, 2026-10-24).

items_shape.description: array (default): items_path names a JSON array of records. map: items_path names an object whose own properties are the records, in sorted key order, with the key available as the path $key (Sources#37).

where.description: Records kept only when every path equals its value (or one of an array of values), or, for { pattern }, is text the regular expression matches; others are left out before max_items counts. Paths follow the field rules: relative to the record, $key, an absolute $root.<path> into the response (a {$key} segment there is the record's map key), * for an object's single child, and key[field=value,...] selectors (Sources#39, Sources#51).

request_content_type.description: Sent as the request's Content-Type on this endpoint's GET (no body). Open Collective's GraphQL API answers a GET only with it, as its CSRF guard (Sources#65).

max_bytes.description: The body cap for this endpoint, in bytes (1 KiB to 32 MiB); the deployment's cap otherwise. OVHcloud's VPS catalog is about 12 MB (Sources#51).

timeout_ms.description: This endpoint's fetch deadline, in milliseconds (1 s to 120 s); the deployment's otherwise. NYC Open Data computes the HPD per-building violation tally in 12 to 60 seconds (Sources#76).

extra.description: Extra fields copied as the API gave them (scalars). A path is relative to the record; $key is the map key; $root.<path> reads the response from its root, where a {$key} segment is the record's map key; * steps into an object's single child; key[field=value,...] (one to four conditions) steps into the first element of the array key whose fields equal the values, compared as text, where a value is literal text or $rec.<path> read from the record (Sources#51).

extra_lists.description: Lists the API gives (tags, job types): each field maps to a path whose array of scalars is kept as up to 20 of them; a lone scalar is a list of one and a missing value an empty list. Separate from extra, which reads an array as null (Sources, 2026-10-24).

extract.description: rss and atom sources only (Sources#45): facts an item states in its own title or summary, read by the source's patterns. An item that yields every REQUIRE'd field is stored as KIND with those fields; any other item is skipped. Each field's PATTERN has one capturing group; AS date turns a stated day such as October 20 into YYYY-MM-DD (without a year, the first such day on or after the item's publication).

crawl.description: type crawl only: how the crawler walks one site from its endpoints (the seeds). Every request still passes the site's robots.txt (RFC 9309) and the per-host spacing, a page that says noindex is not kept, and only what a page publishes for machines is read (schema.org JSON-LD: products and offers for deals, articles, reviews). A crawl adds pages to its frontier from the site's own sitemaps and, if asked, its links; each run fetches the pages that are due and schedules them again after recrawl_sec, so a price seen twice becomes a history.

sitemaps.description: Find pages from the site's sitemaps: the Sitemap lines of its robots.txt, else /sitemap.xml, following sitemap indexes (default true).

follow_links.description: Also follow links on crawled pages to pages of the same host that match include (default false).

include.description: Regular expressions over a URL's path and query; a page must match one (none given: every page of the host).

exclude.description: Regular expressions over a URL's path and query; a page matching one is never fetched.

max_pages.description: The most pages the frontier holds for this site (default 5000).

pages_per_run.description: Pages fetched in one run (default 100); the host spacing still applies between them.

recrawl_sec.description: How long after a fetch a page is due again (default 86400, a day).

max_depth.description: With follow_links, how many links away from a seed or sitemap page a page may be (default 2).

require_structured.description: Keep only pages that publish schema.org JSON-LD the adapter reads (default true); a page without it is fetched once and dropped from the frontier.

env.description: Name of the environment variable holding the credential. Never a value.

min_interval_ms.description: Rate limit: the least time between two requests to this source (the per-host floor and robots Crawl-delay may raise it).

retire_after_sec.description: Retire what the feed stopped showing (jobs, listings): once a fetch of this source succeeds, an item it has not seen for this many seconds is removed with reason "gone_from_source" (a change, so consumers following the change feed learn it). null (the default): items stay, as a news archive or a dataset should.

review_required.description: Products must review what they derive from this source before it can be indexable.

default_indexability.description: What a product's indexability gate starts from for content derived from this source.

search_visibility.description: members = raw items are indexed in OpenVibe.Search for staff only (never indexable).

schema.title: SourceItem
schema.description: One thing a source said, with its provenance: source, canonical URL, retrieval time, content hash, raw-body hash, parser version and the terms it was ingested under. A field the source did not state is null — never guessed. Items change only through successful fetches (a new revision per content change) or an explicit, audited removal.

kind.description: article | url | sitemap | product | offer | review | review_signal | record | coupon …

identity.description: The source's own id (guid, @id, API id) or the canonical URL.

summary.description: Plain text, capped. Sources keeps metadata and short descriptions, not republishable full text.

fields.description: Adapter-specific parsed fields (offers, ratings, prices as stated, API extras).

retrieved_at.description: Last successful fetch that contained this item (observation time).

entered_by.description: Principal that entered a manual item.

schema.title: ModManifest
schema.description: A mod as the platform knows it (ADR-013): who publishes it, which runtime runs it, which capabilities it asks for and the resources it may use. Requested capabilities are only a request: the install's approved subset is the grant, and trust tiers are install metadata that never change a grant check. The runtime-specific payload (a data pack, a script bundle) is not part of the manifest. 1.1.0 (openvibe-contracts v0.34.0) adds the optional permissions.readGrants and writeGrants, billingHooks and dependencies (ADR-013 amendment of 2026-09-24); every 1.0.0 manifest stays valid.

id.description: Stable mod id; its principal subject is mod:<id>.

publisher.description: Who publishes the mod (a user or an app subject).

target.description: Where the mod runs: <service>.<surface>, e.g. games.browser, games.source, live.overlay.

runtime.description: Runtime adapter and its major version, e.g. games-content@1 (declarative data pack) or source-quickjs@1.

capabilities.description: Capability ids the mod asks for (3+ segments). The target runtime binds only those it implements, and only once granted.

events.description: Event types the mod wants delivered to it.

modules.description: User-module namespaces the mod wants to read or write (a trailing .* names a family). A namespace listed here may be read and written; readGrants and writeGrants (1.1.0) say which.

mediaNamespaces.description: Media namespaces the mod wants to read or write. A namespace listed here may be read and written; readGrants and writeGrants (1.1.0) say which.

readGrants.description: 1.1.0: namespaces the mod may only read. A namespace that is only here is read-only. The install's approved subset is still the grant.

modules.description: User-module namespaces (a trailing .* names a family).

writeGrants.description: 1.1.0: namespaces the mod may read and write. A write needs the namespace here, or in the older modules and mediaNamespaces lists, which mean read and write.

modules.description: User-module namespaces (a trailing .* names a family).

resources.description: The budget the mod asks for. Runtimes meter it; the sandbox that enforces it lives in OpenVibe.Host (Stage C).

cpuMs.description: CPU milliseconds per tick (game runtimes) or per request.

outboundHosts.description: Hosts the mod may reach over the network. Empty or absent = none.

assets.description: Assets the mod ships, as Media object references.

runtime.description: Semver range of the runtime this release works with, e.g. ">=1.0.0 <2.0.0".

contracts.description: Semver range of openvibe-contracts releases it was built against.

billingHooks.description: 1.1.0: how the mod takes part in money, only through Billing and VIP primitives (ADR-013 amendment, ADR-012). entitlement: the mod checks that the person holds this entitlement (billing.entitlement.check or vip.entitlement.check, granted like any other capability). checkout: the mod sends the person to the platform's own checkout for this plan (vip.membership.checkout or a Billing intent). A mod never takes payment, sees payment details or holds a balance. Prices live in Billing and VIP, never in the manifest.

key.description: The entitlement or plan key as Billing and VIP name it, e.g. vip.plan:pln_01jab… (lowercase, the form search.index-document@1 acl.entitlements uses).

description.description: What it unlocks or sells, shown at install.

dependencies.description: 1.1.0: other mods this release needs. A runtime refuses to enable the mod while a required dependency is not installed, not enabled or outside its range. An optional one is used only when present.

version.description: Semver range of the dependency's releases this release works with, e.g. ">=1.2.0 <2.0.0".

schema.title: StaffRoleMap
schema.description: The staff roles and the staff capabilities each one holds (ADR-022; roadmap W1 D7, D05). OpenVibe.Network owns the roles and issues the capabilities as claims in its user tokens; every service checks a staff capability instead of comparing role names. Roles are ordered lowest first, and a role holds every capability whose minRole is at or below it. Channel-scoped powers (a channel's owner and its moderators) are not staff capabilities: they stay with the product that owns the channel and are listed under local. The map in force is manifests/policy/staff-roles.json; contracts.staff reads it.

version.description: Version of the map. Adding a capability or lowering a minRole is a minor; removing one or raising a minRole is a major.

roles.description: Lowest first. Each role holds every capability of the roles before it.

staff.description: Whether holders are staff. Non-staff roles hold no staff capability.

source.description: Where the role is stored and how a token carries it today.

id.description: staff.<area>.<action>.

minRole.description: The lowest role that holds it; must be a staff role in roles.

since.description: The map version that added this capability. A token whose issued staff_caps come from an older map (its staff_map claim is lower, or absent = 1.0.0) is judged for it by its role instead, so an addition reaches existing tokens at once.

gates.description: Where the raw role check this capability replaces lives today, per service (file:line and what it guards). Adoption swaps each for a capability check.

claims.description: Claim names in OpenVibe.Network user tokens.

role.description: The stored role (user, streamer, global_mod or admin). owner is never stored as a role.

owner.description: Boolean claim, true only for the owner account. With role admin it makes the effective role owner; on any other role it is ignored.

capabilities.description: Array claim of the staff capabilities the effective role holds, issued only to staff.

map.description: String claim: the version of this map the issued capabilities come from (absent means 1.0.0).

local.description: Channel-scoped or self-scoped powers that are not staff capabilities and stay with the product that owns the resource.

rules.description: Rules a capability check alone does not express, which every service applies on top.

schema.title: AppManifest
schema.description: PROPOSAL (OpenVibe.Codes, roadmap Wave 20): an app release as the platform knows it. The app is a Network developer app (ADR-014): its id is the Network app id, its capabilities are only a request (the grants in Network are the authority), and trust tiers are metadata that never change a grant check. OpenVibe.Codes validates with this schema, loaded into openvibe-contracts' validator, until Contracts publishes it as codes.app-manifest@1.

id.description: The Network app id (its client_id). Its principal subject is app:<id>.

publisher.description: Who publishes the release: the app itself or a member of its project.

project_id.description: The Network project that owns the app. Tenancy in other services is keyed by it (ADR-014).

environment.description: The app's environment. Apps never change environment.

capabilities.description: Capability ids the app asks for (3+ segments). Only active public (or partner, by staff allowance) capabilities can ever be granted to apps.

consumes.description: Event types (or a trailing .* family) the app subscribes to.

redirect_uris.description: Informational copy of the redirect URIs registered in Network (Network's list is the authority).

contracts.description: Semver range of openvibe-contracts releases it was built against.

sdk.description: Semver range of openvibe-sdk releases it uses.

schema.title: CodesReleaseManageResult
schema.description: codes.release-manage-result@1: answers of codes.release.manage on OpenVibe.Codes (an app token managing its own releases). POST /api/v1/apps/:app/releases → 201 { release, warnings } (a draft, or published at once with publish: true; manifest validation warnings); POST /api/v1/releases/:id/publish | deprecate | revoke → { release, event_id } (the codes.release.* event announcing it; null when a revoke announced nothing). Refusals are problem+json: 401 auth.required, 403 release.forbidden (another app's release), 409 release.not_draft, 422 with validation errors.

schema.title: CodesRelease
schema.description: codes.release@1: one release of an app or mod as OpenVibe.Codes presents it (server/domain/releases.js view): its lifecycle (draft → published → deprecated or revoked), compatibility ranges and the app's trust tier (metadata only; grants in OpenVibe.Network are the authority). The manifest itself is served separately (codes.app-manifest@1).

schema.title: CodesReleaseReadResult
schema.description: codes.release-read-result@1: answers of codes.release.read on OpenVibe.Codes (public; no token needed, but a token that is presented must hold the capability; never drafts). GET /api/v1/apps/:app/releases → { app_id, trust, releases } (published, deprecated and revoked releases, newest first); GET /api/v1/apps/:app/trust → { app_id, tier, note, set_by, set_at, note_on_authority } (metadata only: grants in OpenVibe.Network are the authority); GET /api/v1/releases/:id → { release, manifest } (the manifest as published: codes.app-manifest@1 for an app, mods.mod-manifest@1 for a mod). An id that is not an app or a release is 404.

schema.title: CodesReleaseManageRequest
schema.description: codes.release-manage-request@1: bodies of codes.release.manage on OpenVibe.Codes (an app token managing its own releases). POST /api/v1/apps/:app/releases: { kind?, manifest, notes?, publish? } — kind mod or app (anything else is app); manifest must validate as codes.app-manifest@1 for an app or mods.mod-manifest@1 for a mod (422 manifest.invalid with the validation otherwise; a version that already has a release is 409); notes are cut to 2000 characters; publish true publishes the draft at once. POST /api/v1/releases/:id/deprecate: { reason, replacement? } (a reason is required, cut to 500 characters; replacement must be a published release of the same app). POST /api/v1/releases/:id/revoke: { reason } (required). POST /api/v1/releases/:id/publish takes no body. Unknown fields are ignored.

kind.description: mod, or app (the default).

schema.title: CodesModerationActionPayload
schema.description: codes.moderation.action v1 (ADR-022, roadmap WS-D task 1). A staff or moderator action on someone else's content or account in OpenVibe.Codes, such as revoking or deprecating someone else's release or app, and withdrawing trust in a publisher or signing key. Not a person acting on their own content. Written to the service's outbox in the transaction that performs the action; OpenVibe.Network keeps it in the moderation audit log. The payload is common.moderation-action@1. Envelope: subject { type: moderation_action, id: <target type>:<target id> }, visibility internal, actor the staff member. Never carries the content itself.

schema.title: AppManifest
schema.description: PROPOSAL (OpenVibe.Services, roadmap Wave 20): an app release as the platform knows it. The app is a Network developer app (ADR-014): its id is the Network app id, its capabilities are only a request (the grants in Network are the authority), and trust tiers are metadata that never change a grant check. OpenVibe.Services validates with this schema, loaded into openvibe-contracts' validator, until Contracts publishes it as services.app-manifest@1.

id.description: The Network app id (its client_id). Its principal subject is app:<id>.

publisher.description: Who publishes the release: the app itself or a member of its project.

project_id.description: The Network project that owns the app. Tenancy in other services is keyed by it (ADR-014).

environment.description: The app's environment. Apps never change environment.

capabilities.description: Capability ids the app asks for (3+ segments). Only active public (or partner, by staff allowance) capabilities can ever be granted to apps.

consumes.description: Event types (or a trailing .* family) the app subscribes to.

redirect_uris.description: Informational copy of the redirect URIs registered in Network (Network's list is the authority).

contracts.description: Semver range of openvibe-contracts releases it was built against.

sdk.description: Semver range of openvibe-sdk releases it uses.

schema.title: ServicesReleaseManageResult
schema.description: services.release-manage-result@1: answers of services.release.manage on OpenVibe.Services (an app token managing its own releases). POST /api/v1/apps/:app/releases → 201 { release, warnings } (a draft, or published at once with publish: true; manifest validation warnings); POST /api/v1/releases/:id/publish | deprecate | revoke → { release, event_id } (the codes.release.* event announcing it; null when a revoke announced nothing). Refusals are problem+json: 401 auth.required, 403 release.forbidden (another app's release), 409 release.not_draft, 422 with validation errors.

schema.title: ServicesRelease
schema.description: services.release@1: one release of an app or mod as OpenVibe.Services presents it (server/domain/releases.js view): its lifecycle (draft → published → deprecated or revoked), compatibility ranges and the app's trust tier (metadata only; grants in OpenVibe.Network are the authority). The manifest itself is served separately (services.app-manifest@1).

schema.title: ServicesReleaseReadResult
schema.description: services.release-read-result@1: answers of services.release.read on OpenVibe.Services (public; no token needed, but a token that is presented must hold the capability; never drafts). GET /api/v1/apps/:app/releases → { app_id, trust, releases } (published, deprecated and revoked releases, newest first); GET /api/v1/apps/:app/trust → { app_id, tier, note, set_by, set_at, note_on_authority } (metadata only: grants in OpenVibe.Network are the authority); GET /api/v1/releases/:id → { release, manifest } (the manifest as published: services.app-manifest@1 for an app, mods.mod-manifest@1 for a mod). An id that is not an app or a release is 404.

schema.title: ServicesReleaseManageRequest
schema.description: services.release-manage-request@1: bodies of services.release.manage on OpenVibe.Services (an app token managing its own releases). POST /api/v1/apps/:app/releases: { kind?, manifest, notes?, publish? } — kind mod or app (anything else is app); manifest must validate as services.app-manifest@1 for an app or mods.mod-manifest@1 for a mod (422 manifest.invalid with the validation otherwise; a version that already has a release is 409); notes are cut to 2000 characters; publish true publishes the draft at once. POST /api/v1/releases/:id/deprecate: { reason, replacement? } (a reason is required, cut to 500 characters; replacement must be a published release of the same app). POST /api/v1/releases/:id/revoke: { reason } (required). POST /api/v1/releases/:id/publish takes no body. Unknown fields are ignored.

kind.description: mod, or app (the default).

schema.title: ServicesModerationActionPayload
schema.description: services.moderation.action v1 (ADR-022, roadmap WS-D task 1). A staff or moderator action on someone else's content or account in OpenVibe.Services, such as revoking or deprecating someone else's release or app, and withdrawing trust in a publisher or signing key. Not a person acting on their own content. Written to the service's outbox in the transaction that performs the action; OpenVibe.Network keeps it in the moderation audit log. The payload is common.moderation-action@1. Envelope: subject { type: moderation_action, id: <target type>:<target id> }, visibility internal, actor the staff member. Never carries the content itself.

schema.title: RedactionDirective
schema.description: payload.redacts (ADR-026): a producer takes back events it published earlier. Any event may carry it, normally the producer's own *.deleted event. It names event_ids, or subject_type + subject_ids, or both, never an empty list. event_ids names events directly; subject_type + subject_ids names every stored event of the same source (for an app, the same project and environment) about those subjects. OpenVibe.Events rewrites each target into a tombstone (events.tombstone-payload@1) in the transaction that stores the directive. Naming another source's event is 403 events.redaction_not_allowed (the whole batch is refused); a malformed directive is 422 events.invalid_redaction. An event that carries a directive is never redacted itself.

event_ids.description: Events to redact by id. Duplicates are ignored.

subject_type.description: Envelope subject.type of the events to redact (chat_message, post…). Goes with subject_ids.

subject_ids.description: Envelope subject.id values; every not-yet-redacted event of the same source about each one is redacted.

schema.title: TombstonePayload
schema.description: The payload of a redacted event (ADR-026). OpenVibe.Events replaces the original payload with this and the actor with the producer itself ({ type: service, id: <source> }, or the app); event_id, seq, event_type, version, subject, timestamp and visibility stay. Every read path serves it from then on: pull, GET by id, SSE replay, queued deliveries and DLQ replays. A consumer checks payload.redacted before validating a payload against its event type's schema.

redacted_by.description: The event_id of the redacting event; an operator label (e.g. backfill) when OpenVibe.Events redacted by script.

schema.title: EventsDeliveryAdminRequest
schema.description: events.delivery-admin-request@1: the body of POST /api/v1/deliveries/replay on OpenVibe.Events (events.delivery.admin, operators): { subscription_id } and exactly one of from_seq (requeue everything the subscription matches from that seq) or event_ids (at most 1000). GET /api/v1/deliveries?status=&subscription_id=&after_seq=&limit= takes no body.

schema.title: EventsDeliveryAdminResult
schema.description: events.delivery-admin-result@1: answers of events.delivery.admin on OpenVibe.Events. GET /api/v1/deliveries → { deliveries, counts } (per delivery: event, subscription, seq, status pending|delivered|failed|dead, attempt, next_attempt_at, the last HTTP status and error, delivered_at; counts by status); POST /api/v1/deliveries/replay → { subscription_id, queued }.

schema.title: EventsPublishResult
schema.description: events.publish-result@1: the answer of POST /api/v1/events on OpenVibe.Events (events.event.publish for services, events.app.publish for developer apps). One envelope → { event_id, cursor, duplicate } (a repeat whose stored copy retention removed: { event_id, duplicate: true, pruned: true }, no cursor) (201 when stored, 200 when every event was a repeat); a batch { events: [...] } (at most 100, atomic) → { results } in the same order. Refusals are problem+json: 422 events.invalid_envelope / events.invalid_redaction, 403 events.source_mismatch / events.type_not_allowed / events.actor_mismatch, 413 events.payload_too_large / events.batch_too_large, 429 events.quota_exceeded (apps).

duplicate.description: true: this event_id was stored before; its stored position is returned and nothing is stored twice.

cursor.description: Opaque position (ADR-042): hand it back as after= to read on from here, or as Last-Event-ID; never parse it.

pruned.description: A repeat of an event_id whose stored copy retention already removed (hot and replay): nothing is stored again and there is no position to return, so `cursor` is absent.

duplicate.description: true: this event_id was stored before; its stored position is returned and nothing is stored twice.

cursor.description: Opaque position (ADR-042): hand it back as after= to read on from here, or as Last-Event-ID; never parse it.

pruned.description: A repeat of an event_id whose stored copy retention already removed (hot and replay): nothing is stored again and there is no position to return, so `cursor` is absent.

schema.title: EventsReadRequest
schema.description: events.read-request@1: request bodies of the pull API on OpenVibe.Events (events.event.read, events.app.read). PUT /api/v1/checkpoints: { topic, cursor, carrier? } stores the calling consumer's opaque cursor for a topic pattern (an app's patterns must start with a literal segment and app.* must name its own project_key). GET /api/v1/events?topic=&after=&limit=, GET /api/v1/events/:event_id, GET /api/v1/checkpoints?topic= and GET /realtime/stream?topics= take no body. A position is only ever an opaque cursor (ADR-042 decision 7): after_seq is refused (400) and a numeric checkpoint cursor is refused.

topic.description: Dot-separated segments of [a-z0-9_] or *, where * stands for one or more whole segments (*.* is refused).

cursor.description: An opaque cursor: a page's next_cursor (or latest_cursor). Never a number, never parsed.

carrier.description: The carrier the position is on (ADR-042), recorded with it.

schema.title: EventsReadResult
schema.description: events.read-result@1: answers of the pull API on OpenVibe.Events. GET /api/v1/events → { events: [{ cursor, event }], next_cursor, latest_cursor, gap? } (keep next_cursor as the position and read on with after=: it moves past events that did not match; latest_cursor is the head, for a consumer that starts at now; without after= a page starts at the oldest retained event; gap { from_seq, to_seq } says events after the position were already pruned by retention); GET /api/v1/events/:event_id → { cursor, event }; GET|PUT /api/v1/checkpoints → { consumer, topic, cursor, carrier, updated_at } (cursor, carrier and updated_at null when none is stored). GET /realtime/stream?topics= (events.event.read) is a Server-Sent Events feed whose messages carry { event } with the cursor as the SSE id; it resumes from Last-Event-ID (or last_event_id=) when that is a cursor, and a gap message comes first when the cursor is older than retention. A position is only ever an opaque cursor (ADR-042 decision 7): there is no per-event sequence number and no global order; dedupe on event.event_id. An app sees only its project's events in its token's environment plus public first-party events.

cursor.description: Opaque position (ADR-042): hand it back as after= to read on from here, or as Last-Event-ID; never parse it.

next_cursor.description: Opaque position after this page (ADR-042): pass it back as after= for the next page.

latest_cursor.description: The head as an opaque cursor (ADR-042): a consumer that starts at now stores it and reads on with after=.

cursor.description: Opaque position (ADR-042): hand it back as after= to read on from here, or as Last-Event-ID; never parse it.
The stored opaque cursor, as it was stored; null when none is.

carrier.description: The carrier the stored position is on (ADR-042), or null.

schema.title: EventsSubscriptionRequest
schema.description: events.subscription-request@1: the body of POST /api/v1/subscriptions on OpenVibe.Events (events.subscription.manage for services, events.app.subscribe for developer apps; the consumer is always the caller). topic_pattern (topic is accepted for it) and endpoint are required: a service's endpoint must be http(s) on the allow-list (127.0.0.1, *.openvibe.*), an app's must be https resolving only to public addresses. secret, when given, is 32 to 256 characters (else one is generated); retry_policy accepts max_attempts (1..20) and backoff_ms (1..20 delays of 0..86400000 ms) and nothing else. The same pattern and endpoint twice is 409 events.subscription_exists. GET /api/v1/subscriptions[/:id] and POST /api/v1/subscriptions/:id/disable|enable take no body.

topic_pattern.description: Dot-separated segments of [a-z0-9_] or *, where * stands for one or more whole segments (*.* is refused).

topic.description: Dot-separated segments of [a-z0-9_] or *, where * stands for one or more whole segments (*.* is refused).

schema.title: EventsSubscriptionResult
schema.description: events.subscription-result@1: answers of the subscription routes on OpenVibe.Events. POST /api/v1/subscriptions → 201 events.subscription@1 with its secret (shown once); GET /api/v1/subscriptions → { subscriptions } (the caller's own, no secrets); GET /api/v1/subscriptions/:id and POST …/disable|enable → events.subscription@1. Another consumer's subscription is 404.

schema.title: EventsSubscription
schema.description: events.subscription@1: one push subscription as OpenVibe.Events shows it to its consumer (server/store.js subscriptionView). The signing secret appears only in the answer that creates it (and in a rotation's). A developer app's subscription also names its project and environment.

secret.description: Only when the subscription is created: shown once.

schema.title: EventsPublishRequest
schema.description: events.publish-request@1: the body of POST /api/v1/events on OpenVibe.Events (events.event.publish for services, events.app.publish for developer apps): one events.event-envelope@1, or a batch { events: [...] } of 1 to 100 envelopes stored all or nothing. trace_id, priority (important) and visibility (internal) default when left out. source must be the caller and event_type one of its prefixes (an app: app-<ULID> and app.<project_key>.*, actor the app or the user it acts for).

schema.title: ChatMessageDeletedPayload
schema.description: chat.message.deleted v1 (OpenVibe.Chat server/db/database.js _announceDeleted). Public messages were deleted: by a moderator, through Live's bridge, the author's or an anon's history, a time-range purge or the auto-delete sweep. Envelope: subject { type: chat_message, id: <first id> }, visibility public, priority important, actor service:chat. One event per 500 ids. Carries only ids, never the text, the author or who deleted it; payload.redacts makes OpenVibe.Events tombstone the chat.message.created of each id.

message_ids.description: Chat message ids (the id in chat.message.created).

redacts.description: { subject_type: chat_message, subject_ids: message_ids as strings }.

schema.title: ChatRoomMessageCreatedPayload
schema.description: chat.room.message.created v1 (OpenVibe.Chat server/rooms/rooms.js post, WS-I task 9). A message was posted in a PUBLIC chat room, so it reaches the realtime plane (browsers subscribed to chat.room.*). Private rooms and DMs never emit it: they stay on Chat's own WebSocket. Envelope: subject { type: chat_room_message, id }, visibility public, actor the author (user). Written in the transaction that stores the message; chat.room.message.deleted redacts it.

user_subject.description: The author's usr_ subject, when they have one.

text.description: The message as shown in the room (after the word filter).

schema.title: ChatRoomMessageDeletedPayload
schema.description: chat.room.message.deleted v1 (OpenVibe.Chat server/rooms/rooms.js, WS-I task 9). Messages of a public room were deleted (by the author, a room mod or chat staff), or the room turned private or was archived, so what it had published must stop being replayable. Envelope: subject { type: chat_room_message, id: <first id> }, visibility public, actor service:chat. Carries ids only; payload.redacts makes OpenVibe.Events tombstone the chat.room.message.created of each id.

redacts.description: { subject_type: chat_room_message, subject_ids: message_ids as strings }.

schema.title: SourcesItemCreatedPayload
schema.description: sources.item.created v1 (OpenVibe.Sources server/items.js ingest → itemEvent). A successful fetch, or a manual entry, produced an item Sources had not seen (revision 1). A summary only: consumers fetch the full sources.item@1 with sources.item.read. Envelope: subject { type: item, id: <item_id>, revision }, visibility internal, priority important, actor service:sources.

kind.description: article | url | sitemap | product | offer | review | record … (sources.item@1 kind).

retrieved_at.description: Last successful fetch (or manual entry) that contained the item.

schema.title: SourcesItemUpdatedPayload
schema.description: sources.item.updated v1 (OpenVibe.Sources server/items.js ingest → itemEvent). A successful fetch or manual entry changed an existing item's content hash, which made a new revision. A removed item is never updated (removal is sticky). Envelope: subject { type: item, id: <item_id>, revision }, visibility internal, priority important, actor service:sources.

kind.description: article | url | sitemap | product | offer | review | record … (sources.item@1 kind).

retrieved_at.description: Last successful fetch (or manual entry) that contained the item.

schema.title: SourcesItemRemovedPayload
schema.description: sources.item.removed v1 (OpenVibe.Sources server/items.js remove → itemEvent, from DELETE /api/v1/items/:id). Staff removed an item (takedown, licence, error). Sticky: a later fetch that still lists it does not bring it back. The removal bumps the revision; content_hash is the last content's. Envelope: subject { type: item, id: <item_id>, revision }, visibility internal, priority important, actor service:sources.

kind.description: article | url | sitemap | product | offer | review | record … (sources.item@1 kind).

retrieved_at.description: Last successful fetch (or manual entry) that contained the item.

schema.title: SourcesFetchFailedPayload
schema.description: sources.fetch.failed v1 (OpenVibe.Sources server/ingest.js failedEvent).
