schema.description: openre.key-rotate-request@1: the body of POST /api/v1/streams/:id/keys/rotate on OpenRestream (openre.key.rotate). grace_seconds (0 by default, at most 7 days) keeps the old key working that long; end_sessions true also ends the stream's open sessions. An empty body rotates with no grace.

schema.title: OpenreKeyRotateResult
schema.description: openre.key-rotate-result@1: the answer of POST /api/v1/streams/:id/keys/rotate on OpenRestream: the new key (shown once, Cache-Control no-store), the keys it retired (grace or revoked), when the grace ends, how many sessions were asked to end, and the ingest endpoints. openre.key.rotated is announced.

key.description: The plain ingest key: only in this answer.

ingest.description: Where an encoder publishes (never the key).

schema.title: OpenreOutputReadResult
schema.description: openre.output-read-result@1: answers of openre.output.read on OpenRestream. GET /api/v1/streams/:id/destinations → { destinations }; GET /api/v1/sessions/:id/outputs → { outputs } (with health); GET /api/v1/destinations/:id/logs and GET /api/v1/outputs/:id/logs?limit= → { logs } (newest first, at most 500).

schema.title: OpenreOutputWriteRequest
schema.description: openre.output-write-request@1: the body of POST /api/v1/streams/:id/destinations (platform and server_url required) and PATCH /api/v1/destinations/:id (fields left out keep their value) on OpenRestream (openre.output.write). server_url must pass the destination URL rules (rtmp, rtmps or srt, public hosts); stream_key (at most 512 characters, no spaces) and srt_passphrase (10 to 79 characters) are sealed and never read back — __keep__ leaves them unchanged, empty clears them. Numbers out of range become null: srt_latency_ms 20-8000, custom_video_bitrate 500-50000, custom_audio_bitrate 32-512, custom_fps 15-120; an unknown custom_encoder_preset becomes null. DELETE /api/v1/destinations/:id and POST /api/v1/destinations/:id/test|start|stop take no body.

schema.title: OpenreOutputWriteResult
schema.description: openre.output-write-result@1: answers of openre.output.write on OpenRestream. POST …/destinations → 201 { destination }; PATCH /api/v1/destinations/:id → { destination }; DELETE → 204 with no body (409 openre.destination_running while it still runs); POST …/test → { ok, checks } (URL rules, DNS, TCP reachability; each check { check, ok, detail }); POST …/start → { output } (for the stream's live session; 409 when held, disabled, keyless or not live); POST …/stop → { stopping } (outputs asked to stop).

schema.title: OpenreOutput
schema.description: openre.output@1: one restream output (a destination running for a live session) on OpenRestream (server/store/outputs.js publicOutput), with its desired and actual state, restarts and progress.

schema.title: OpenreSessionEndResult
schema.description: openre.session-end-result@1: the answer of POST /api/v1/sessions/:id/end on OpenRestream (openre.session.end): 202 { requested: true, state } when the owning worker was asked to disconnect the encoder, 409 { requested: false, state } when the session could not be ended (already ending or over).

schema.title: OpenreSessionReadResult
schema.description: openre.session-read-result@1: answers of openre.session.read on OpenRestream. GET /api/v1/sessions?stream_id=&state=&limit=&before= → { sessions } (the owner's; a service sees those of the subject it acts for); GET /api/v1/sessions/:id → { session } with transitions, outputs, recording and playback; GET /api/v1/sessions/:id/playback → { playback } (where to watch: flv and rtmp URLs, internal loopback and public); GET /api/v1/workers → { workers } (worker generations; staff and services only).

schema.title: OpenreStreamReadResult
schema.description: openre.stream-read-result@1: answers of openre.stream.read on OpenRestream. GET /api/v1/streams[?external_ref=<service>:<type>:<id>&limit=] → { streams } (the owner's, or the one bound to that external reference; staff may ask for all); GET /api/v1/streams/:id → { stream }; GET /api/v1/streams/:id/keys → { keys } (metadata only, never a key). Another owner's or an archived stream is 404 openre.stream_not_found.

schema.title: OpenreStreamWriteRequest
schema.description: openre.stream-write-request@1: the body of POST /api/v1/streams and PATCH /api/v1/streams/:id on OpenRestream (openre.stream.write). A person creates streams for themselves; a service names the owner with X-OV-Subject (or owner_subject, which must then match). title is cleaned and cut to 140 characters (Untitled stream when blank), description to 2000; protocols is a non-empty subset of rtmp, whip, webrtc, jsmpeg; external_refs (create only, at most 10, each bound to one stream) link it to another service's record, e.g. { service: live, type: managed_stream, id: 12 }; state (update only) is active or disabled. Fields left out keep their value. DELETE /api/v1/streams/:id (archive; refused while live) takes no body. Refusals are 400 openre.invalid_* and 409 openre.ref_taken / openre.stream_live.

schema.title: OpenreStreamWriteResult
schema.description: openre.stream-write-result@1: answers of openre.stream.write on OpenRestream. POST /api/v1/streams → 201 { stream, key } where key is the first ingest key, shown once (Cache-Control no-store); PATCH /api/v1/streams/:id → { stream }; DELETE /api/v1/streams/:id → 204 with no body.

key.description: The plain ingest key: only in this answer.

schema.title: OpenreStream
schema.description: openre.stream@1: one stream definition as OpenRestream's API shows it (server/api/v1.js publicDefinition): the owner's stream with its protocols, recording and playback settings, ingest endpoints, key metadata (hints only, never a key) and the open session if any.

ingest.description: Where an encoder publishes (never the key).

schema.title: HostDeployCreateRequest
schema.description: host.deploy-create-request@1: bodies of host.deploy.create on OpenVibe.Host (a deployer or above of the project; an app principal added as deployer can deploy from CI). POST /api/v1/sites/:id/deploys uploads a deploy: the raw body is a tar or tar.gz archive (Content-Type application/gzip, application/x-gzip, application/x-tar or application/octet-stream), or multipart/form-data with archive=<one archive> or files=<file>… (each part's filename is its path); optional fields activate=1, root=<subdirectory to deploy> and strip=folder (removes a shared first segment) also work as query parameters. It is validated (path traversal, links, special and hidden files, server-side code, file types, sizes and quotas) and never executed; a refusal is a problem whose extra carries the failed deploy_id and its log (413 upload.too_large, quota.storage; 422 validation codes; 429 quota.deploys_per_day; 403 site.taken_down; 503 upload.busy; 507 storage.host_full). POST /api/v1/deploys/:id/activate { expected_active? } and POST /api/v1/sites/:id/rollback { deploy_id?, expected_active? } switch the site's pointer in one step (rollback without deploy_id goes to the deploy active before; 409 deploy.not_ready, site.active_changed when expected_active is stale, deploy.no_previous). GET /api/v1/sites/:id/deploys, /deploys/:id and /deploys/:id/log take no body.

anyOf.description: The upload itself: the tar or tar.gz bytes, or the multipart/form-data body (as common.binary@1).

expected_active.description: The deploy you saw active (null: none); refused with 409 site.active_changed when it moved.

schema.title: HostDeployCreateResult
schema.description: host.deploy-create-result@1: answers of host.deploy.create on OpenVibe.Host. GET /api/v1/sites/:id/deploys?limit= → { active_deploy_id, deploys, activations } (newest first; the last 20 pointer switches). POST /api/v1/sites/:id/deploys → 201 { deploy, activated, url } (the ready deploy with its validation log; activated when activate=1 switched the site to it). GET /api/v1/deploys/:id → { deploy } with its files. GET /api/v1/deploys/:id/log → { deploy_id, state, log }. POST /api/v1/deploys/:id/activate and /sites/:id/rollback → { active_deploy_id, previous_deploy_id, changed } (changed false when it was already active). Emits host.deploy.created|activated|failed.

schema.title: HostDeploy
schema.description: host.deploy@1: one immutable static deploy on OpenVibe.Host (server/http/serialize.js deploy): ready (validated and stored, never executed) or failed (refused, with its failure code and log), whether the site serves it, its size and manifest hash. GET /api/v1/deploys/:id adds the files; the upload answer adds the log.

git.description: Present on source git: the commit this deploy was built from (public provenance, never a credential).

new_bytes.description: Bytes this deploy added to the project's store.

schema.title: HostDomainManageRequest
schema.description: host.domain-manage-request@1: bodies of host.domain.manage on OpenVibe.Host (a maintainer or above of the project). POST /api/v1/sites/:id/domains { hostname } adds a custom domain, pending until its TXT record is verified: a fully qualified host name, lowercased (422 domain.invalid_hostname; 422 domain.reserved for any OpenVibe domain; 403 domain.sandbox in sandbox projects; 429 quota.custom_domains; 409 domain.exists, domain.taken). GET /api/v1/sites/:id/domains, POST /api/v1/domains/:id/verify (checks the TXT record now) and DELETE /api/v1/domains/:id (409 domain.default: the default domain goes only with the site) take no body.

hostname.description: e.g. www.example.org (a trailing dot is dropped).

schema.title: HostDomainManageResult
schema.description: host.domain-manage-result@1: answers of host.domain.manage on OpenVibe.Host. GET /api/v1/sites/:id/domains → { domains } (the default domain first). POST /api/v1/sites/:id/domains → 201 { domain } with the DNS records to publish. POST /api/v1/domains/:id/verify → { domain } after the check (status verified and served once the TXT record matches, else last_error says what was found; emits host.domain.verified). DELETE /api/v1/domains/:id → { deleted: true }.

schema.title: HostDomain
schema.description: host.domain@1: one domain of a static site on OpenVibe.Host (server/http/serialize.js domain): the default <site>.openvibe.host, or a custom domain that is served only once its DNS TXT record is verified (re-checked daily; it lapses when the record is gone). A custom domain carries the records its owner must publish (the TXT verification value is public by design and shown only to members); TLS certificates are issued by an operator.

name.description: _openvibe-host.<hostname>

routing.description: A CNAME for a subdomain; A/AAAA for an apex domain when the operator configured them.

schema.title: HostProject
schema.description: host.project@1: one OpenVibe.Host tenant project (server/http/serialize.js project): owned by a person (usr_…), production or sandbox, with the caller's role in it and any staff takedown. POST /api/v1/projects and GET /api/v1/projects/:id add the effective quota and the usage.

network_project_id.description: The OpenVibe.Network project once Network has projects.

role.description: The caller's role (staff: a Network admin who is not a member).

takedown.description: A staff takedown covering it: serving stops while the content is kept for review.

quota.description: The effective quota: the project's override where set, else its environment's default.

schema.title: HostSiteManageRequest
schema.description: host.site-manage-request@1: bodies of host.site.manage on OpenVibe.Host (judged by the acting principal's project role too; a sandbox token is refused on production projects). POST /api/v1/projects { name, environment?, network_project_id? } creates a project owned by the person named with X-OV-Subject (403 project.owner_must_be_user; 422 project.invalid_name over 80 characters, project.invalid_environment; 429 quota.projects; 409 project.network_project_taken). PUT /api/v1/projects/:id/quota { storage_bytes?, deploys_per_day?, max_files?, max_file_bytes?, sites?, custom_domains? } (a Network staff user: 403 auth.staff_only; fields left out keep their value). PUT /api/v1/projects/:id/members/:principal { role } (the owner: 422 member.invalid_role, 409 member.owner_fixed). POST /api/v1/projects/:id/sites { name } (a maintainer; lowercased and trimmed, one DNS label of 3–40 characters: 422 site.invalid_name, site.name_reserved; 409 site.name_taken, site.name_held; 429 quota.sites). POST /api/v1/projects/:id/takedown and /sites/:id/takedown { reason } (staff: stop serving, keep the content; 409 takedown.exists); DELETE on those { note? } lifts it. GET /api/v1/projects, /projects/:id, /projects/:id/quota, /projects/:id/sites and /sites/:id, and DELETE /api/v1/projects/:id, /projects/:id/members/:principal, /sites/:id and /deploys/:id take no body (deleting refuses taken-down content for non-staff: 409 site.taken_down; an active deploy: 409 deploy.active).

name.description: 1–80 characters once trimmed.

environment.description: Default production; a sandbox credential creates sandbox projects only.

storage_bytes.description: A non-negative integer, or null for the environment default.

deploys_per_day.description: A non-negative integer, or null for the environment default.

max_files.description: A non-negative integer, or null for the environment default.

max_file_bytes.description: A non-negative integer, or null for the environment default.

sites.description: A non-negative integer, or null for the environment default.

custom_domains.description: A non-negative integer, or null for the environment default.

role.description: Only a person (usr_…) can be an owner.

name.description: The site name (lowercased).

reason.description: Members see it.

schema.title: HostSiteConfig
schema.description: host.site-config@1: one Host site's serving configuration (plan T12 J3). headers are applied to every response of the site before the platform's own, which always win; the platform's security, routing, caching, scope and transport headers (Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, Set-Cookie, Cache-Control, Content-Type, Location, Service-Worker-Allowed, Alt-Svc and the rest of Host's reserved list) and every X-Forwarded-* header are refused. redirects are local paths only (no scheme, host, protocol-relative URL, backslash or control character, also after percent-decoding). spa serves /index.html for an extensionless path that has no file. A site with no configuration answers { headers: {}, redirects: [], spa: false }.

schema.title: HostSiteConfigRequest
schema.description: host.site-config-request@1: the body of PUT /api/v1/sites/:id/config on OpenVibe.Host (host.site.config; the acting principal must be a maintainer or owner of the site's project). { headers?, redirects?, spa? } replaces the whole configuration: a field left out is reset to its default. A redirect's status defaults to 301. Refusals are 422 problem+json: site_config.reserved_header, site_config.header_name, site_config.header_value (longer than 1024 characters or a control character), site_config.too_many (over 50 headers or 200 redirects), site_config.redirect (not a local path, a duplicate from, or a status outside 301/302/307/308), site_config.headers and site_config.redirects (wrong type). GET and DELETE /api/v1/sites/:id/config take no body (DELETE resets to the defaults).

schema.title: HostSiteConfigResult
schema.description: host.site-config-result@1: every answer of host.site.config on OpenVibe.Host. GET, PUT and DELETE /api/v1/sites/:id/config → { config } (after a PUT, the configuration as stored; after a DELETE, the defaults).

schema.title: HostDeployActivatedPayload
schema.description: host.deploy.activated v1 (OpenVibe.Host server/domain/deploys.js switchPointer, Stage B tenant hosting). A tenant site's active deploy changed, written into Host's event outbox in the transaction that moves the pointer (activate or rollback). Envelope: subject { type: deploy, id: <deploy id> }, visibility internal, priority low, actor the person or app that switched it. A network service's release going live is host.release.published, not this.

previous_deploy_id.description: The deploy that served before; null for the site's first activation.

rollback.description: true when the switch was a rollback.

schema.title: HostReleasePublishedPayload
schema.description: host.release.published v1 (roadmap WS-P task 9, ADR-016 amendment 1). A network service's release went live. OpenVibe.Host's operator plane (lib/announce.js) publishes it after `ovhost deploy|rollback <service>` went live and for `ovhost announce <service>` (services deployed by their own scripts: Live, Tools, Sites, OpenRestream, Games). Envelope: subject { type: release, id: <service>:<release> }, visibility public (signed-out browsers get it over Events realtime), priority low, actor service:host. Open tabs whose /release.json names `service` (openvibe-shared release-watch 1.17.0, topics=host.release.published) check it when `release` is not the one they run. It carries identifiers only, never what changed. At most one per service and release unless an operator forces it; a retry reuses the event_id. Tenant sites' activations are host.deploy.activated, not this.

service.description: The service id the pages' /release.json names (registry.release-manifest@1 `service`): live, tools, or a Sites placeholder's id such as news.

release.description: The release id that service's /release.json reports now (registry.release-manifest@1 `release`). A client compares it with the release it runs, treating a hex prefix of the other as the same release.

commit.description: The deployed commit when it is known and `release` is its prefix, or what the operator passed; null otherwise (a Sites placeholder's release is a page hash).

origin.description: The public origin the release serves (https://openvibe.live): the inventory's origin or the service manifest's publicOrigin; null when neither is known.

deployed_at.description: When Host announced it (UTC); after `ovhost deploy`, just after the service answered ready.

components.description: Optional. The component versions /release.json reported (registry.release-manifest 1.1.0 `components`, kind and version only).

rollback.description: Present after `ovhost rollback`: the release is an older one.

schema.title: HostSiteManageResult
schema.description: host.site-manage-result@1: answers of host.site.manage on OpenVibe.Host. GET /api/v1/projects → { projects } (the caller's projects with their role). POST /api/v1/projects → 201 { project } (with quota and usage). GET /api/v1/projects/:id → { project, sites, members }. GET and PUT /api/v1/projects/:id/quota → { quota, usage }. PUT and DELETE /api/v1/projects/:id/members/:principal → { members }. GET /api/v1/projects/:id/sites → { sites }. POST /api/v1/projects/:id/sites → 201 { site }. GET /api/v1/sites/:id → { site, domains }. DELETE /api/v1/projects/:id and /sites/:id → { deleted: true } (serving stops at once; the objects are removed). DELETE /api/v1/deploys/:id → { deleted: true, objects_removed }. POST …/takedown → 201 { takedown }; DELETE …/takedown → { lifted: true }.

quota.description: The effective quota: the project's override where set, else its environment's default.

schema.title: HostCatalogManageRequest
schema.description: host.catalog-manage-request@1: bodies of host.catalog.manage on OpenVibe.Host (a Network staff user only). POST/PATCH /api/v1/catalog/providers { slug, name, homepage_url, description?, affiliate_url?, affiliate_note?, status? }; POST/PATCH /api/v1/catalog/plans { provider_id, external_id, name, kind, currency, price_monthly, source_url, vcpu?, ram_mb?, disk_gb?, disk_type?, bandwidth_gb?, unmetered?, port_mbps?, ipv4?, locations?, price_hourly?, setup_fee?, checked_at?, status? } (a plan from OpenVibe.Sources takes only status); POST/PATCH /api/v1/catalog/promos { provider_id, title, url, details?, code?, affiliate?, starts_at?, ends_at?, status? }. A PATCH carries any subset. Unknown fields are refused (422 host.catalog.invalid); a missing entry is 404 host.catalog.not_found; anyone but staff is 403 host.catalog.forbidden. A staff plan's checked_at defaults to now: the staff member confirming the price that day.

affiliate_note.description: The exact disclosure shown beside the provider's affiliate links.

checked_at.description: Epoch milliseconds the price was confirmed.

schema.title: HostCatalogManageResult
schema.description: host.catalog-manage-result@1: the saved entry, under its type's name: { provider } (with affiliate_rel and affiliate_disclosure when it has an affiliate link), { plan } or { promo } (an active promo past ends_at reads as ended). 201 on create, 200 on update.

schema.title: HostSite
schema.description: host.site@1: one static site on OpenVibe.Host (server/http/serialize.js site): its name (one DNS label), the default hostname and URL it is served at, the deploy it serves (one pointer; null until a deploy is activated) and any staff takedown.

takedown.description: A staff takedown covering it: serving stops while the content is kept for review.

schema.title: NetworkNode
schema.description: network.node@1: one machine of the OpenVibe platform as the node registry lists it (ADR-034 section 12; roadmap WS-X1). Roles are what it serves; location is region-level; the beacon is an HTTPS URL a client times to measure its own round trip. No addresses, capacity or secrets are public: a node is found by role and location, and reached through the service that uses it.

beacon.description: Timed by clients (GET, tiny body, no caching) to measure round-trip time.

cell.description: Cell the node belongs to, e.g. wnam-1.

schema.title: NetworkNodeReportRequest
schema.description: network.node-report-request@1: POST /internal/nodes/report on OpenVibe.Network (capability network.node.report, held by the Host principal). The complete set of nodes one Host inventory knows, with their health now: a node absent from a later report of the same source is marked down, never deleted silently.

source.description: The reporting inventory (e.g. the host id).

schema.title: NetworkNodeListResult
schema.description: network.node-list-result@1: GET /api/v1/nodes on OpenVibe.Network (public, cacheable): every node of the platform, filterable by ?role= and ?region=. The input of openvibe-sdk/geo's nearest().

schema.title: NetworkMachine
schema.description: network.machine@1: one machine of a person, as the network's machines hub shows it (plan L34, steps M2 and M4). A machine is a Bot device of kind machine: an OpenVibe Node install that paired with the person's account. Bot stays the registry underneath (the device id is its dev_…); Network fronts it for the person and for apps the person consented. The roles are what the machine does for the network (the catalogue: network.machine-roles@1), and running is what it does right now. Nothing here is a secret: no credential, no hash, no address.

id.description: The machine's device id in Bot's registry (dev_…).

principal_id.description: The machine's node principal on Network (nod_…): the credential it holds. Absent for a machine Bot knows but Network has no principal for.

name.description: The name the owner gave it. Absent when they gave none.

kind.description: What the machine is, as Bot's device record says: onboard (the robot's own machine), bridge (a machine that drives a robot over the robot's own link), server (a machine that runs its owner's jobs).

os.description: The operating system the Node reports (linux, darwin, windows). Absent until the machine has checked in.

online.description: Whether the machine is connected to Bot right now.

last_seen_at.description: When the machine was last seen. Absent before its first check-in.

node_version.description: The OpenVibe Node version the machine reports. Absent until it has checked in.

roles.description: What the machine does for the network: the ids from the catalogue (network.machine-roles@1). The owner sets these; the machine applies them at its next check-in.

running.description: What the machine is doing right now, as a short list: its Codes jobs, its desks, the local models it serves and the robots it drives.

label.description: A short, plain description for the owner (the desk's name, the model's name).

schema.title: NetworkMachineListResult
schema.description: network.machine-list-result@1: a person's machines, as the network's hub lists them (plan L34, step M2: GET /api/v1/machines). Only the caller's own machines are ever in it.

schema.title: NetworkMachineManageResult
schema.description: network.machine-manage-result@1: the machine as it is after a change (plan L34, step M2: PATCH /api/v1/machines/:id, PUT /api/v1/machines/:id/roles, POST /api/v1/machines/:id/revoke). The pairing route answers network.machine-pairing@1 instead, because a pairing is a code and not a machine.

schema.title: BotMachineManageRequest
schema.description: bot.machine-manage-request@1: what a caller changes on a machine (plan L34, step M2). A rename gives a name; a roles change gives the whole set of roles (network.machine-roles-put@1's shape). The same body is what the network's hub sends to Bot, so both sides speak one shape.

name.description: The name the owner gives the machine. Absent when the call changes something else.

roles.description: The machine's roles after the change. Absent when the call changes something else.

schema.title: BotMachineManageResult
schema.description: bot.machine-manage-result@1: the machine as it is after the change (plan L34, step M2). Bot is the registry underneath: it answers with its own device record, never with a credential.

schema.title: NetworkMachineRole
schema.description: network.machine-role@1: one role a machine can have (plan L34, step M4). A role is what the machine does for the network: a name for the owner, what it installs on the machine and what the hub shows. The catalogue is network.machine-roles@1; a role outside it is refused.

id.description: The role's id: the product that owns it, then what it is (codes.worker, desks.host, ai.host, bot.robot).

name.description: The role's name, in the owner's words.

installs.description: What the role puts on the machine (the job runner, the desk sandbox, the local model server).

shows.description: What the hub shows for a machine with this role.

schema.title: NetworkMachineRoles
schema.description: network.machine-roles@1: the catalogue of machine roles (plan L34, step M4). A product declares a role — a name, what it installs on the machine and what the hub shows — and the Node turns it on at its next check-in. The first roles are Codes' worker, Desks' host, AI's local models and Bot's robot. A role outside this catalogue is refused (network.machine-roles-put@1).

schema.title: NetworkMachineRolesPut
schema.description: network.machine-roles-put@1: the roles the owner gives a machine (PUT /api/v1/machines/:id/roles, capability machines.manage). The whole set, not a change: what is not named is turned off. Every id must be in the catalogue (network.machine-roles@1); an unknown role is refused and nothing is changed.

roles.description: The machine's roles after the change. An empty array turns every role off.

schema.title: NetworkMachinePairing
schema.description: network.machine-pairing@1: a one-time code that pairs a machine with the person's account (POST /api/v1/machines/pairings, capability machines.manage). The code is shown once, expires, and works once: the machine redeems it and becomes the person's. The command is what the owner runs on the machine (openvibe.bot/install). The code is never stored in the clear and never returned again.

code.description: The one-time pairing code, eight Crockford base32 characters in two groups (XXXX-XXXX).

pairing_id.description: The pairing's id, as the install command carries it. Absent when the authority behind it does not name one.

installer.description: The command the owner runs on the machine (openvibe.bot/install, with the network, the pairing id and the code).

schema.title: NetworkMachineOnlinePayload
schema.description: network.machine.online v1 (OpenVibe.Network, plan L34: the machines hub). A machine of a person (a Bot device of kind machine) came online: it checked in and is connected to Bot. Network republishes Bot's change (Bot reports it to Network, which writes this event), so a consumer of the network's events hears about a machine once, in one place. Envelope: subject { type: machine, id: <dev_…> }, visibility internal, actor service:network.

principal_id.description: The machine's node principal on Network, when it has one.

owner.description: The person the machine belongs to.

schema.title: NetworkMachineOfflinePayload
schema.description: network.machine.offline v1 (OpenVibe.Network, plan L34: the machines hub). A machine of a person went offline: it is no longer connected to Bot. Network republishes Bot's change, so a consumer of the network's events hears about a machine once, in one place. Envelope: subject { type: machine, id: <dev_…> }, visibility internal, actor service:network.

principal_id.description: The machine's node principal on Network, when it has one.

owner.description: The person the machine belongs to.

schema.title: NetworkMachinePairedPayload
schema.description: network.machine.paired v1 (OpenVibe.Network, plan L34: the machines hub). A machine was paired with a person's account: it redeemed the one-time code and became theirs. It holds a credential from then on; the code is spent. The machine's device id in Bot is absent until the machine checks in for the first time. Envelope: subject { type: machine, id: <nod_…> }, visibility internal, actor service:network.

machine_id.description: The machine's device id in Bot's registry, when Bot already knows the device.

principal_id.description: The node principal the pairing created. Also the envelope subject id.

owner.description: The person the machine belongs to.

schema.title: NetworkMachineRolesChangedPayload
schema.description: network.machine.roles_changed v1 (OpenVibe.Network, plan L34, step M4). A machine's roles changed: the whole set after the change, from the catalogue (network.machine-roles@1). The machine applies them at its next check-in, so this event says what was asked for, not what the machine has already done. Envelope: subject { type: machine, id: <dev_…> }, visibility internal, actor service:network.

owner.description: The person the machine belongs to.

roles.description: The machine's roles after the change.

changed_by.description: Who asked for the change: the person, or an app acting with their consent.

schema.title: NetworkMachineRevokedPayload
schema.description: network.machine.revoked v1 (OpenVibe.Network, plan L34: the machines hub). A machine of a person was revoked: it is no longer theirs and its credential is dead. The machine's credential and its hash are never carried. A second revoke changes nothing and emits nothing. Envelope: subject { type: machine, id: <dev_…> }, visibility internal, actor service:network.

principal_id.description: The machine's node principal on Network, when it had one.

owner.description: The person the machine belonged to.

reason.description: Why it was revoked, when the caller gave one. Absent otherwise.

schema.title: NetworkAvatarWriteRequest
schema.description: network.avatar-write-request@1: the body of POST /internal/user-avatar on OpenVibe.Network (capability network.avatar.write, held by the site a person picked the avatar on; Live posts here through its notify helper). Adopts the picture as the account's avatar and fans it out to the other sites. Only an openvibe.media address is accepted, so an avatar can never be a tracking pixel or a third-party file. Refusals are { error }: 400 without a user_id, 404 for an unknown user, 422 for anything but an openvibe.media address, 503 while the avatar service is down.

avatar_url.description: An https://openvibe.media/… picture; null clears the avatar.

origin.description: Who asked ('live', 'network'); kept in the audit row and used to avoid echoing a push back.

schema.title: NetworkAvatarWriteResult
schema.description: network.avatar-write-result@1: the answer of POST /internal/user-avatar on OpenVibe.Network: { ok: true, changed } — changed is false when the account already had this picture (nothing was written, and nothing is fanned out to the sites). Refusals are { error } (400, 404, 422, 503).

schema.title: NetworkRegistryReadResult
schema.description: network.registry-read-result@1: the answer of GET /internal/url-registry/resolved on OpenVibe.Network (capability network.registry.read): { ok: true, registry } — every site's resolved base URLs, keyed by setting name, that the shared navbar and service clients use. Secret-typed entries (deploy tokens) and sensitive keys are filtered out, so a caller never gets a credential. The keys are open (the registry grows with the sites); a failure is { ok: false, error }.

registry.description: Setting name → resolved value; secrets and sensitive keys are omitted.

schema.title: NetworkCoinsReadResult
schema.description: network.coins-read-result@1: the answer of GET /internal/coins/stats on OpenVibe.Network (capability network.coins.read): site-wide OpenCoins totals for public stat displays — earned, spent, circulating and holders, the transaction count, and two rolling seven-day windows (recent.<metric>.w is this week, .pw the seven days before it) so a display can say whether the economy is speeding up. Counts only, never a named person's balance. The answer is held for a minute; a failure is { error }.

schema.title: ResourceOffer
schema.description: What one node or external provider can run right now (roadmap WS-Z9, decision 43): capabilities, multidimensional capacity, measured latencies, health and pricing. First-party only: it carries capacity the public node registry (network.node@1) deliberately leaves out.

provider.description: provider or hosting company

adapter.description: carrier or provider adapter id, for kind provider (e.g. nats-v1, cf-queue-v1)

trust.description: the offer's trust class (ADR-046): first-party (operated by the OpenVibe network), user-owned (a person's own node, eligible only for workloads whose requirements name user-owned), partner, community or external

owner.description: For a user-owned offer: the person whose node it is (ADR-046). Such an offer is eligible only for that person's own workloads (a job whose requester is this subject and whose requirements name user-owned); a placer must never put a user-owned offer without an owner, or with another owner, on anyone's work. First-party only: a public projection leaves user-owned offers out.

capabilities.description: e.g. node:http, worker:browser, worker:ffmpeg, worker:ai-gpu, events:gateway, events:durable, object:r2. Kind harness: task:edit, task:review, task:browse, task:run, task:test and task:plan for the task kinds it takes (its detail's task_capabilities), and harness:mcp, harness:resume, harness:host-access and harness:long-autonomy for its detail's capabilities that are true. The `worker:<class>` names that map to platform.runtime-class@1 values are reserved for OpenVibe.Node's job worker, one per class: worker:function, worker:code, worker:browser, worker:linux, worker:desktop and worker:gpu ($defs.reservedWorkerCapabilities). A node advertises the name of each class it runs (Node's status.capabilities.worker); every other `worker:` name (worker:ffmpeg, worker:ai-gpu) is an ordinary capability name. Beside them, a kind harness names `runtime:<class>` for each platform.runtime-class@1 class it can run (runtime:function, runtime:code, runtime:browser, runtime:linux, runtime:desktop, runtime:gpu); these are ordinary capability names, not reserved, and OpenVibe.Codes already advertises the classes it offers.

workers.description: free worker slots by kind (browser, ffmpeg, ai, …)

queues.description: queue depth and age by name

latency_ms.description: measured p50/p95 by operation, e.g. publish_p95, ack_p95

rate_card.description: platform.rate-card id when the price comes from one

detail.description: The kind's own offer: platform.storage-offer@1, platform.delivery-offer@1, platform.runtime-offer@1, platform.agent-offer@1 or platform.harness-offer@1 for those kinds; absent for kind node and provider.

reservedWorkerCapabilities.description: The reserved Fabric capability names of OpenVibe.Node's job worker, one per platform.runtime-class@1 value: `worker:` + the class. These six names are reserved in this contract — the `capabilities` pattern alone accepted any `worker:` name — and a node advertises only the classes it actually runs, in class order.

schema.title: WorkloadRequirements
schema.description: What a workload needs, so the platform can place it (roadmap WS-Z9). Hard constraints are filtered before any objective is scored; a cheaper candidate that misses one is never chosen.

kind.description: what runs, e.g. watch.browser, media.transcode, ai.run, events.deliver

residency.description: region or jurisdiction the work and its data must stay in

trust.description: trust classes allowed to run it (ADR-046); when absent, first-party, partner, community and external. user-owned is never a default: a user-owned offer is eligible only when this list names it

partition_key.description: stable key for rendezvous placement (room, stream, session)

schema.title: PlacementResult
schema.description: Where a workload was (or would be) placed and why: the chosen candidate, the reasons, and every candidate with its eligibility, estimated cost and latency (POST /api/v1/placement/explain; roadmap WS-Z9).

selected.description: The id of the chosen candidate, or null when none qualified — every candidate was ineligible or none was offered — in which case `reasons` says why. openvibe-sdk/placement plan() returns null on the same condition.

schema.title: PlacementPlan
schema.description: A signed, expiring route plan (roadmap WS-Z3 and WS-Z9): which carrier or pool serves each route. Every SDK and service caches the last valid plan and keeps working while the control plane is unreachable; unsigned or expired plans are refused.

route.description: a route name: an event delivery class and scope, a workload kind, a service

signature.description: Ed25519 over the canonical JSON of every other field, base64url

schema.title: RateCard
schema.description: One provider price with its free allowance, in the provider's real billing unit, with effective dates and where it was checked (roadmap WS-Z3 task 5). Changed only by review; never written by an AI on its own.

metric.description: e.g. queue-operation-64kb, request, gib-delivered, message, gb-month, class-a-op

schema.title: ProviderState
schema.description: A provider's usage against its allowances this billing period and its forecast, used to compute marginal cost (roadmap WS-Z3 task 5).

reserve.description: share of each free allowance kept for higher-priority classes

schema.title: CostSnapshot
schema.description: Cost and volume for a window, by carrier or provider, with the counterfactuals: what the same work would have cost all-local, all-provider and with the optimiser (roadmap WS-Z9 task 6).

schema.title: CapacitySnapshot
schema.description: A node's reported capacity at one moment, sent by its Host agent (roadmap WS-Z9 task 1).

workers.description: free worker slots by kind (browser, ffmpeg, ai, …)

queues.description: queue depth and age by name

schema.title: UsageSample
schema.description: One metered usage reading with retry-safe attribution (T1 Universal Fabric; ADR-034 proposed). Consumers dedupe on `idempotency_key`. A running platform.job@1 `function` job is one reading per wall-clock second (service `run`, operation `function.invoke`, unit `s`, idempotency_key `run:<job id>:<second>`), derived as platform.job-frame@1 `job_usage` describes.
schema.$comment: Additive optional fields may extend this v1 contract.

idempotency_key.description: Stable across retries. The only dedupe key, and it encodes work identity only (examples: tools:job:<id>, ai:<run>:tokens, run:<job>:<n>), never route_epoch, node, region or trace_id.

service.description: The Contracts manifest id of the producing service (tools, ai, run).

resource.description: The producing service's billing resource: the platform.rate-card@1 `metric` for this reading's `provider` (e.g. `tokens`, `queue-operation-64kb`), and never a run, job, object or other work id. The reading's `unit` must be that metric's unit, so Billing rates it against the card found by (provider, resource): a resource that names no card, or a unit the card's metric does not fit, is left unrated (`billing.no_card` / `billing.unit_mismatch`).

free_allowance_used.description: How much of this reading's `quantity` the free allowance covered (platform.rate-card@1 `free_allowance` for this provider/metric and period), in the reading's own `unit`, not in rate-card units, money or Vibes: a 1.5 GiB reading with 1 GiB free carries 1. Never more than `quantity`; 0 when nothing was free. Absent: not rated against a rate card.

vibes_charged.description: Vibes charged for this reading, as an integer count of vibes-bits (Billing's ledger minor unit, currency `vibes-bits`; balance credit and ledger amounts use the same unit). Never whole Vibes, USD or a fraction: round once, when rating. Covers only `quantity` minus `free_allowance_used`; 0 means rated and nothing charged. Absent means not rated (yet). Records a charge already made in Billing's ledger; it is never a request to charge.

route_epoch.description: Epoch of the signed placement plan that chose where this reading ran (platform.placement-plan@1 `epoch`). A later plan supersedes it; absent when Fabric did not place the work.

trace_id.description: Opaque trace id tying this reading to the request and route that produced it, the same `trace_id` platform.telemetry-sample@1 carries; absent when the producer had no trace.

schema.title: TelemetrySample
schema.description: Universal operation observation for routing and autoscaling, with product dimensions in extra (T1 Universal Fabric; ADR-034 proposed).
schema.$comment: Additive optional fields may extend this v1 contract.

ttfb_ms.description: Time to first byte in milliseconds

extra.description: Product-specific scalar dimensions; no payloads or secrets

schema.title: NodeCapabilities
schema.description: Node hardware, placement regions, tags, and operating costs (T1 Universal Fabric; ADR-034 proposed).
schema.$comment: Additive optional fields may extend this v1 contract.

capabilities.description: What the machine offers, in the platform.resource-offer@1 capability form (e.g. node:http, worker:ffmpeg).

agent_version.description: Version of the node agent that reported.

schema.title: ServiceInstance
schema.description: One running instance registered in a cell (T1 Universal Fabric; ADR-034 proposed).
schema.$comment: Additive optional fields may extend this v1 contract.

route_weight.description: Share of this service's traffic the router sends to this instance, relative to its siblings; absent means equal weight.

schema.title: RuntimeOffer
schema.description: Available execution capacity for code on a node (T1 Universal Fabric; ADR-034 proposed).
schema.$comment: Additive optional fields may extend this v1 contract.

schema.title: StorageOffer
schema.description: Durable storage capacity and operation pricing (T1 Universal Fabric; ADR-034 proposed).
schema.$comment: Additive optional fields may extend this v1 contract.

schema.title: DeliveryOffer
schema.description: Transport and edge delivery capacity with cache policy and pricing (T1 Universal Fabric; ADR-034 proposed).
schema.$comment: Additive optional fields may extend this v1 contract.

schema.title: AgentOffer
schema.description: Agent model capacity and token pricing (T1 Universal Fabric; ADR-034 proposed).
schema.$comment: Additive optional fields may extend this v1 contract.

schema.title: HarnessOffer
schema.description: Registered coding or agent harness, its access method, limits, and price (T1 Universal Fabric; ADR-034 proposed).
schema.$comment: Additive optional fields may extend this v1 contract.

edit.description: edits files in its working tree

review.description: reviews a change and reports findings

tools.description: calls tools such as a shell, search, or file reads on its own

computer_use.description: operates a desktop through its screen, keyboard, and mouse

runtimes.description: platform.runtime-class@1 classes the harness runs in

target.description: Endpoint URI, executable, or MCP server name

task_capabilities.description: task kinds the harness takes; its resource offer lists the same kinds as task:<kind> capabilities

runtime_needs.description: runtimes the harness needs on its host, e.g. git, node, python, docker

byo_key.description: the caller supplies their own provider key

success_rate.description: measured share of routed tasks that finished green

agents.description: the agents (models) this harness offers; each one is a platform.agent-offer@1 whose harness names this offer

schema.title: RuntimeClass
schema.description: platform.runtime-class@1: the kind of execution environment a platform.job@1 asks for (plan T14 Run; ADR-034 proposed). A name only: this contract defines no behavior, and a worker runs only the classes it advertises and refuses every other one (`nack`). `function` is the first class implemented (OpenVibe.Node's function worker); the others are reserved names. Each class names one reserved Fabric capability in platform.resource-offer@1.capabilities — `worker:` + the class (worker:function, worker:code, worker:browser, worker:linux, worker:desktop, worker:gpu) — and a node advertises the name of each class it runs.
schema.$comment: Additive: a class may be added to v1; none is removed, renamed or reordered.

oneOf.description: A pre-registered artifact (name and exact version) run once with declared args to one result: single-shot, no persistent filesystem, no dependency resolution, network denied.
Arbitrary source with its dependency tree in a longer-lived environment; needs image handling and isolation stronger than a container.
A headless or headed web browser session driven remotely.
A full Linux environment (shell, filesystem, processes) that lives across commands.
A graphical desktop session with screen and input under control levels.
A workload that holds one or more GPUs for its lifetime.

schema.title: Job
schema.description: platform.job@1: one unit of work a dispatcher (OpenVibe.Bot now, Fabric later) hands to an execution worker (plan T14 Run; ADR-034 proposed). It rides the device control link inside a `job` frame (platform.job-frame@1). The worker answers it with `ack` (accepted) or `nack` (refused: an unknown or unimplemented class, a missing artifact, limits it cannot honor, the local kill switch), then runs it at most once. Metering: a running `function` job is billed by wall-clock second as platform.usage-sample@1 readings; platform.job-frame@1 `job_usage` gives the mapping.
schema.$comment: Additive optional fields may extend this v1 contract.

id.description: Minted by the dispatcher (job_<ULID>): the idempotency and ack key, as a Node command `id` is. A worker that already holds or ran this id never runs it again: a resent `job` is acked again while it runs and answered with its `job_exit` once it ended. Never reused: it is the stem of every usage reading's key (`run:<id>:<second>`).

artifact.description: The pre-registered artifact to run; required for classes `function` and `code`.

version.description: One exact version, never a range

args.description: The artifact's declared input as JSON; the whole `job` frame stays within the link's 1 MiB frame limit.

ttl_ms.description: Lifetime from the worker's receipt of the job, covering any wait and the run; the worker caps it with its own local maximum (the stricter wins, as with `max_command_ms`). When it runs out, a job not yet started never starts and a running one is killed; either way `job_exit` says `ttl`.

limits.description: Caps the worker enforces on the running process (merged stricter with its local caps); exceeding one kills the job and `job_exit` says `limit`.

net.description: Network policy; absent means `deny`. `none` is `deny` spelled as OpenVibe.Node's worker.egress names it; `public` and `openvibe-only` ask for egress the host must already allow (ADR-046): a worker whose host policy is stricter runs the stricter one, and a worker that cannot enforce what is asked refuses the job (`nack`) rather than running it weaker.

inputs.description: Files placed in the job's working directory before the process starts. Each is an OpenVibe.Media object pinned by digest: a size or digest mismatch ends the job failed before the process ever runs (run.job.input_digest_mismatch). Never a caller-chosen URL and never a credential; the worker holds its own token. Names are unique and carry no path separator.

schema.title: JobFrame
schema.description: platform.job-frame@1: one job lifecycle frame on the device control link (plan T14 Run; ADR-034 proposed). The link is OpenVibe.Node's WebSocket to OpenVibe.Bot (Node docs/protocol.md section 2); Fabric may terminate it later. Each frame is one JSON object in one text message, with the link's envelope at the top level: `v` (1), `seq` (per-direction counter from 1 on each connection), `ts` (sender's clock, Unix ms) and `type`. Server to device: `job`, `job_cancel`, `job_exit_ack`. Device to server: `job_started`, `job_stdout`, `job_usage`, `job_exit`. The link's existing `ack`/`nack` frames, keyed by the job id, accept or refuse a `job`; a worker that runs jobs advertises its classes in `status.capabilities`. A running `function` job is metered per wall-clock second into platform.usage-sample@1 readings: see `job_usage` and `job_exit`.
schema.$comment: Additive: new frame types and optional fields may extend this v1 contract; a receiver ignores frame types it does not know.

oneOf.description: Server to device: run this job (platform.job@1). Resent until acked; the job id makes a resend harmless.

Server to device: stop this job. A running job's process group is killed and `job_exit` says `cancelled`; a job not yet started never starts; an ended or unknown id is ignored (the ended job's `job_exit` is resent if not yet acked).
Server to device: every usage reading of this job is recorded (written or replayed by Billing), so the worker may forget it and stops resending its `job_exit`.
Device to server: the job's process started. `started_ms` anchors every usage second of the job and never changes.
Device to server: a chunk of the job's stdout, best effort (a chunk lost with the link is not resent; a receiver drops a `chunk_seq` it already has). Never metered.

chunk_seq.description: The job's own chunk counter from 1, across reconnects (the envelope `seq` is the connection's)

oneOf.description: Device to server: wall-clock second `second` of the job has fully elapsed. Metering (platform.usage-sample@1, written through billing.usage.record by whoever terminates the link: OpenVibe.Bot now, Fabric later): second n is [started_ms + n*1000, started_ms + (n+1)*1000) on the worker's monotonic clock. A worker sends `job_usage` for n only once that second has fully elapsed, so every `job_usage` stands for quantity 1; the partial last second is never sent here, only in `job_exit`. Each second is exactly one reading: `id` and `idempotency_key` `run:<job id>:<n>`, `service` `run`, `operation` `function.invoke`, `unit` `s`, `quantity` 1 (the partial last second: (wall_ms mod 1000)/1000, never 0), `at` new Date(started_ms + n*1000).toISOString(), `resource` the job id, `node` the worker's device id, `source` `openvibe-node.worker`, and `project`, `subject` and `provider` from the dispatcher's own record of the job. No field depends on when or how often a frame was sent, and no rating fields (`cost_estimate`, `free_allowance_used`, `vibes_charged`) are set, because Billing keeps the first reading under a key, replays an identical one and refuses a different one (409): a resend after a reconnect, a `job_usage` and the `job_exit` backfill of the same second, and two writers of one job all land on one record.

cpu_ms.description: CPU time used in this second; informational, never billed

oneOf.description: Device to server: the job ended (only after an `ack`). Its `usage` is authoritative for metering: from it the writer writes (or replays) seconds 0 to floor(wall_ms/1000) - 1 with quantity 1 and, when wall_ms mod 1000 > 0, the partial last second, so a lost `job_usage` is backfilled and none is billed twice. Every reason is billed for the seconds the process held. The worker resends the same `job_exit` after every reconnect until `job_exit_ack`. wall_ms comes from the monotonic clock `job_usage` uses, so it is at least (n+1)*1000 for every second n already sent.

reason.description: exited: the process ended by itself; cancelled: `job_cancel`; ttl: `ttl_ms` ran out; limit: a `limits` cap was hit; stopped: the local kill switch or e-stop; failed: the worker could not run it (spawn error, missing artifact)

code.description: The process's exit status; null when it was killed or never ran

result.description: The artifact's declared output (any JSON); null unless reason is `exited` with code 0

wall_ms.description: Running time from `started_ms` to the process's end, monotonic clock; 0 when it never started

started_ms.description: When the job's process started, worker's wall clock, Unix ms

schema.title: Task
schema.description: platform.task@1 (plan T17, ADR-044): one task at OpenVibe.Actor's task router. POST /api/v1/tasks (actor.task.create) creates it from a plain-language `task` plus a `mode` and a `budget`; the router mints `id`, sets `state` and `created_at`, picks a backend from the registered agent systems, runs the task, verifies the result, escalates or fails over, and answers with `result`, `cost` and `explanation`. GET /api/v1/tasks/{id} (actor.task.read) reads the same resource. Progress streams as server-sent events from `progress.stream_url` (actor.task-event@1; the task's own counter in `progress.last_seq`); `cancel` records that a cancel was requested (POST /api/v1/tasks/{id}/cancel), `error` says why a task failed, and `webhooks` are the registered endpoints the router delivers each state change to (actor.task-webhook@1, signed with `webhook_secret`, which only the creating answer carries). Owned by `network` like every other platform.* contract and implemented by OpenVibe.Actor (manifests/services/actor.json). This v1 contract may grow optional fields.
schema.$comment: Additive optional fields may extend this v1 contract. It is the task resource, not a device frame: Actor's link is HTTP/SSE where Run's is the Node WebSocket.

id.description: Minted by the router (tsk_<ULID>): the idempotency key of the task and the stem of its usage readings, as platform.job@1's id is for a job. Never reused.

project_id.description: The project the caller's token names (ADR-034 §5): budgets, usage and the bill are the project's. Absent for a person's own task (one made signed in, without a project token): the person's free allowance and daily budget apply.

requester.description: The person or agent the task belongs to: a user subject for a person, an agent subject for an agent acting under the grants its owner delegated (roadmap WS-Z2).

task.description: The instruction in plain words, exactly as the caller gave it. Not a backend command and not a model prompt: the planner turns it into one.

mode.description: The plan's five modes, in contract spelling: Cheapest, Balanced (the default), Best, Fastest and Private are `cheapest`, `balanced`, `best`, `fastest` and `private`. A mode is the planner objective, never a fixed backend list (plan T17). `cheapest`: the lowest expected cost that still meets the task class's quality bar. `balanced` (the default): cost, quality and speed weighed together. `best`: the highest chance of a right answer first time. `fastest`: the shortest time to a checked result. `private`: only backends that keep the data on OpenVibe (first-party, and a user-owned node only when the task names it), per ADR-046.

budget.description: Hard limits the router never exceeds (plan T17: 'a hard limit per task and per day'). A task whose cheapest eligible backend would take it over `per_task_usd` ends failed (actor.budget.exceeded) rather than running; `per_day_usd` caps the project's tasks in one UTC day and a new task waits or fails, it never overruns.

state.description: queued: stored, waiting for the planner. running: a backend is working, or a cascade is between attempts. verifying: a result exists and a check (the task's own tests, a citation check, a postcondition) runs before it is delivered. succeeded, failed and cancelled are the end states; an end state never changes.

finished_at.description: When the task reached its end state; null before.

result.description: The checked deliverable (any JSON, as a platform.job@1 `result` is): for a code task a diff or branch reference, for research a brief with citations, for an action a postcondition report. Never a credential and never raw sandbox output. Null (or absent) in every state but succeeded, which the allOf below enforces.

usd.description: What this task was billed, to the cent, across every attempt it made.

free_allowance_used.description: The part of `usd` covered by the project's free allowance; metered as platform.usage-sample@1.

cost.description: Present once the task has run an attempt (also when it ends failed or cancelled); null while queued. One key, one bill (plan T17), through Billing (ADR-012).

explanation.description: One platform.placement-result@1 per backend the planner tried, oldest first, an escalation appending a new one: which backend won, why and what else was considered, from openvibe-sdk/placement (ADR-046 §1). Null while queued.

stream_url.description: The text/event-stream endpoint that carries this task's progress. Each event mirrors platform.job-frame@1's job_stdout/state shape: a state change, an output chunk, or the end.

last_seq.description: The task's own event counter, from 0 before the first event; a reconnecting reader resumes after it, as a job frame's seq counts on one link.

events.description: The event kinds the stream delivers, run.job-stream-event@1's own three.

progress.description: Streaming progress (plan T17). Null before the router opens a stream and after the end.

requested_at.description: When POST /v1/tasks/{id}/cancel was accepted. The running backend is stopped as its own contract allows; the state becomes cancelled and `finished_at` is set.

cancel.description: Cancellation (plan T17): null until a cancel is requested, then it records who asked and when; the task's outcome is `state`.

url.description: The HTTPS endpoint the router POSTs a state change to. A plain-HTTP URL is refused.

events.description: The state changes delivered; the same names as `state`.

secret_ref.description: The NAME of the project secret used to sign the delivery (an HMAC header), never the secret itself, as community.moderation-request@1 names a webhook_url_ref and ADR-043 keeps device credentials by reference. Project secrets (ADR-056) are named in lower case; the upper-case form is the earlier environment-variable reference.

webhooks.description: Webhooks (plan T17), registered at creation. A delivery that fails is retried with backoff and never delays the task; the task's own record is the source of truth.

code.description: A stable problem code, e.g. actor.budget.exceeded, actor.no_agent, actor.check.failed, actor.task.interrupted.

error.description: Why the task failed, once it has; null otherwise. Never a credential and never raw provider output.

webhook_secret.description: The secret every webhook delivery of this task is signed with (X-OpenVibe-Signature-V2: t=<unix seconds>,v2=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<raw body>">, verified by openvibe-sdk/events verifyDeliveryV2). Present only in the answer that created the task (and an idempotent repeat of it), never in a read or a list; erased once the task has ended and its deliveries are done.

examples.task: Research five competitors of my shop and write a one-page brief with sources.
Fix the failing thumbnail test in OpenVibe.Media and open a PR.

reasons: the task is code; the Codes adapter exposes a code harness

examples.task: Check this week's outage report and summarize the causes.

result.brief: Two outages; both were a saturated connection pool.

reasons: research task; the checks are citations, met by the cheapest candidate

schema.title: DeliveryPolicy
schema.description: How an event type is carried (roadmap WS-Z3 task 2): its delivery class sets the minimum semantics, which a publisher's intent may raise and never lower; ordering is per key; the route planner picks the carrier.

schema.title: ResourceSummary
schema.description: One resource of any service, as the resource index lists it (roadmap WS-Z7): every service answers GET /api/v1/resources with these, so OpenVibe.Services shows any resource without owning its data.

kind.description: service.kind, e.g. watch.watch, actor.actor, media.object, events.subscription

ovrn.description: Optional resource name (ADR-034 section 2), the name grants, audit, events, usage records and bills use: ovrn:<service>:<project_id>:<type>/<id>, e.g. ovrn:watch:<project_id>:watch/<wch_id>, with the pattern of common.usage-recorded@1 resource. Its service, project and id are this summary's service, project_id and id. Added in 1.1.0.

schema.title: ResourceListResult
schema.description: A page of the resource index (roadmap WS-Z7).

partial.description: Authorities a merged index (OpenVibe.Services, ADR-048) could not read for this page: a slow or failing authority is omitted, never fails the page. Each entry names the authority and the problem code it answered. Added in 1.1.0; a single authority's own index leaves it out.

schema.title: ResourceCost
schema.description: One charge in weighted cost units (roadmap WS-Z1): which subject used what, reserved and committed or released, with an idempotency key so a retried charge counts once.

schema.title: ConfirmationRequest
schema.description: A sensitive action waiting for its owner's approval (roadmap WS-Z2): an agent (or app) asks to do something with an external side effect; the owner approves or denies from any OpenVibe site; the decision is an event.

schema.title: NetworkConfirmationChangedPayload
schema.description: network.confirmation.changed v1 (OpenVibe.Network; roadmap WS-Z2, docs/t2-projects-and-grants.md section 5; shape from OpenVibe.Network docs/contracts-proposal/network.confirmation.changed.v1.json). A confirmation request (network.confirmation-request@1) an agent raised for a sensitive capability was created, approved, denied, expired, cancelled or used. state is the state after the change, named as in network.confirmation-request@1: created leaves it pending (or approved when a standing rule covers it, with rule_id), used leaves it approved, and every other change names its state. A cancelled change says why in cancel_reason. Written to Network's outbox in the transaction that changes it, beside an audit row. Never carries the summary or details, which may hold message text: a reader that needs them asks Network with its own authority. Envelope: subject { type: confirmation, id: cnf_… }, visibility internal, on_behalf_of the owner, actor the owner who decided (or the system for an expiry, a cascade or a standing rule).

audience.description: The owning service of the capability: the only one that may consume or cancel the confirmation.

state.description: The state after the change. A use leaves it approved and sets used_at.

standing_rule.description: On approved: the rule the owner chose (once creates none).

rule_id.description: On created through a standing rule, or on approved with a session, until or always rule: that rule.

cancel_reason.description: On cancelled: what took the authority away.

schema.title: ObjectZone
schema.description: zone.object-zone@1 (ADR-031 amendment 2026-10-02): one named object zone, as OpenVibe.Zone's control API returns it (GET /api/v1/zones/{zone_id}, the list under /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/zones, and the 201 of a create). Zone owns this record: its name, environment, state, access policy and per-zone quota setting. Media owns everything inside it: the objects (ordinary med_ objects in the namespace media_namespace), their keys, bytes and replicas, quota enforcement, usage counting and the one deletion path. Zone never lists keys or holds bytes. The S3 bucket name is `name`, resolved within the project and environment of the access key that signs the request, at https://s3.openvibe.media/<name>/<key>. `ovrn` is ovrn:zone:<project_id>:object-zone/<id>, with the same project_id and id as this record. The id is never reused, and neither is a name: within one project environment a name belongs to one zone for ever, deleted or not, so a signed request names exactly one zone id. Name and env are immutable. Every environment has exactly one `default` zone, whose media_namespace is the environment root. Zone creates it with the environment, and it cannot be deleted on its own. Its access is per-object, and every other zone's is private. JSON Schema cannot compare fields: contracts.zones.checkObjectZone also requires that ovrn names this project_id and id, and that media_namespace is the environment root of project_id and env, followed by .<id> unless the zone is the default. More fields may be added.

ovrn.description: The resource name used in grants, audit, events, usage records and bills (ADR-034 section 2).

env.description: Fixed at creation. A sandbox key never resolves a production zone.

name.description: The S3 bucket name. It is unique among all the zones of one project environment, deleted ones included: a deleted zone's name is retired, never given to another zone. It is valid as an S3 bucket name.

default.description: The environment's default zone, named `default`. Its media_namespace is the environment root.

access.description: private: every named zone in v1. Its objects never have a public_url and never enter a public cache. per-object: only the default zone, whose existing objects keep their own visibility (public, unlisted or private), public URLs and cached copies, as media.object@1 allows. The S3 surface never serves an object without a signature, in either kind of zone. Publication of a named zone would add a value in a later minor version.

state.description: provisioning: Media has not yet acknowledged the zone. active: it serves requests. deleting: requests answer NoSuchBucket while Media tombstones the objects and erases every copy. deleted: no object or copy remains. The record is kept, and its name stays retired.

media_namespace.description: Where Media keeps the zone's objects. It is the environment root for the default zone, and <root>.<id> for every other zone.

quota_bytes.description: An optional byte ceiling for this zone. Media enforces it together with the project environment's byte quota, and a write over either is refused with QuotaExceeded. null means only the environment quota applies.

usage.description: A snapshot of the live objects, as Media reports it. Zone never counts. Billed usage comes from Media's hourly media.usage.recorded rollups, whose dimension is this id in lowercase.

deletion.description: Progress of a zone deletion, as Media reports it.

objects_remaining.description: Objects not yet tombstoned, plus tombstoned objects with a copy not yet confirmed erased.

held_objects.description: Objects whose erasure waits for a retention hold (ADR-006). They are already unreadable.

revision.description: Raised by every change. Zone sends it when it provisions the change in Media, and Media applies only a higher revision.

schema.title: ObjectZoneCreateRequest
schema.description: zone.object-zone-create-request@1 (ADR-031 amendment 2026-10-02): the body of POST /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/zones on OpenVibe.Zone, sent with an Idempotency-Key header. The answer is 201 with a zone.object-zone@1 in state provisioning or active. A name held by a zone of that environment in state provisioning or active answers 409 zone.name_taken, and one held by a zone in state deleting or deleted answers 409 zone.name_retired, because a name belongs to one zone for ever; and going over the project's zones quota answers 403 zone.quota_exceeded. `default` cannot be requested, because Zone creates that zone with the environment.

schema.title: ObjectZoneUpdateRequest
schema.description: zone.object-zone-update-request@1 (ADR-031 amendment 2026-10-02): the body of PATCH /api/v1/zones/{zone_id} on OpenVibe.Zone (capability zone.zone.manage). Only quota_bytes and description change. Name, environment and access are immutable, so a body naming them is refused. The answer is 200 with the zone.object-zone@1. A quota change takes effect once Media acknowledges it, and lowering quota_bytes below the zone's stored bytes only refuses later writes. It never deletes an object.

quota_bytes.description: null removes the zone's own ceiling, so only the environment quota applies.

schema.title: ObjectZoneListQuery
schema.description: zone.object-zone-list-query@1 (ADR-031 amendment 2026-10-02): the query string of GET /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/zones on OpenVibe.Zone (capability zone.zone.list). Without env it lists both environments the caller's grant reaches. A sandbox-only grant never lists production zones.

include_deleted.description: Also list zones in state deleted. Default false.

limit.description: Items per page, 1 to 200. A query string carries it as a string, which must name the same range.

schema.title: ObjectZoneList
schema.description: zone.object-zone-list@1 (ADR-031 amendment 2026-10-02): the answer of GET /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/zones on OpenVibe.Zone (capability zone.zone.list), filtered by zone.object-zone-list-query@1. Zones come oldest first, the environment's default zone before the others. Deleted zones are listed only with include_deleted=true. contracts.zones.checkObjectZoneList also checks each zone's identity. More fields may be added.

next_cursor.description: Pass as cursor for the next page; null on the last page.

schema.title: ObjectZoneDeleteQuery
schema.description: zone.object-zone-delete-query@1 (ADR-031 amendment 2026-10-02): the query string of DELETE /api/v1/zones/{zone_id} on OpenVibe.Zone (capability zone.zone.delete). The answer is 202 with the zone.object-zone@1 in state deleting. Without recursive=true, a zone that still holds live objects answers 409 zone.not_empty. A zone with an object under a retention hold answers 409 zone.held, as media.object.delete refuses a held object. The default zone always answers 409 zone.default. Deletion goes through Media's one deletion path: every object is tombstoned at once, with no restore window, and every copy is erased within 24 hours. A hold placed after the request delays only that object's purge. The zone's name is retired: no later zone of the environment can take it.

recursive.description: Delete the zone's objects too. Default false.

schema.title: ObjectZoneUsage
schema.description: zone.object-zone-usage@1 (ADR-031 amendment 2026-10-02): the answer of GET /api/v1/zones/{zone_id}/usage on OpenVibe.Zone (capability zone.usage.read). Zone never counts. current is the live-object snapshot that Media's internal zone endpoint returns. series sums Media's hourly media.usage.recorded rollups (common.usage-recorded@1) whose dimension is this zone id in lowercase, over the closed hours of the current UTC month. Rollups are counts; Billing rates only platform.usage-sample readings (billing.usage.record). Zone's control operations are not metered. ovrn is the OVRN of zone_id, never of another zone (contracts.zones.checkObjectZoneUsage). More fields may be added.

window_start.description: The start of the current UTC month.

window_end.description: The end of the last closed hour that Media has reported.

schema.title: BotRobot
schema.description: bot.robot@1: a robot on OpenVibe.Bot as its API presents it (domain.present.robot): its owner-chosen name, the device profile it runs, who may drive it (access_policy) and the latched e-stop.

schema.title: BotDevice
schema.description: bot.device@1: a paired device as the API presents it (domain.present.device): never a credential or publish-key hash; online is added when a robot's devices are listed.

roles.description: The machine roles the owner set (plan L34: the catalogue is network.machine-roles@1). Absent on a device that has none.

os.description: The operating system the device reported.

schema.title: BotRobotReadResult
schema.description: bot.robot-read-result@1: answers of bot.robot.read on OpenVibe.Bot (a service token needs no acting subject: only GET …/robots needs ?owner=). GET /api/v1/robots?owner= → { robots }; GET …/robots/:id → { robot, role }; GET …/robots/:id/operators → { operators }; GET …/robots/:id/devices → { devices } (no hashes, with online); GET …/robots/:id/audit?limit=&before= → { audit, next_before } (newest first).

schema.title: BotRobotManageRequest
schema.description: bot.robot-manage-request@1: bodies of bot.robot.manage on OpenVibe.Bot. POST /api/v1/robots → { owner (the person a service acts for), name, profile_id, access_policy?, limits? }; PATCH …/robots/:id → { name?, access_policy?, limits? }; POST …/robots/:id/operators → { subject, role? (operator by default) }. POST …/robots/:id/pairing-code and both DELETE routes take no body.

schema.title: BotRobotManageResult
schema.description: bot.robot-manage-result@1: answers of bot.robot.manage on OpenVibe.Bot. POST /api/v1/robots → 201 { robot, pairing }; PATCH …/robots/:id and POST …/robots/:id/estop/clear → { robot }; DELETE …/robots/:id → 204 (no body); POST …/robots/:id/pairing-code → 201 { code, expires_at, installer }; POST …/robots/:id/operators → 201 { operators }; DELETE …/robots/:id/operators/:subject → { operators }; POST …/devices/:id/rotate and /revoke → bot.device-connect-result@1.

pairing.description: A one-time pairing code (shown once), when it expires and the one-line installer command that uses it.

anyOf.description: A one-time pairing code (shown once), when it expires and the one-line installer command that uses it.

schema.title: BotRobotControlResult
schema.description: bot.robot-control-result@1: answers of bot.robot.control on OpenVibe.Bot. POST /api/v1/robots/:id/estop → { robot } with its e-stop as it now stands.

schema.title: BotDeviceConnectResult
schema.description: bot.device-connect-result@1: answers of OpenVibe.Bot's device credential routes, which Bot gates with bot.robot.manage (bot.device.connect is reserved, not enforced). POST /api/v1/devices/:id/rotate → { device, credential, publish_key } (both secrets shown once); POST …/devices/:id/revoke → { device } (its socket closes at once).

schema.title: BotRobotProfile
schema.description: bot.robot-profile@1 (ADR-043 decision 7): a robot profile as OpenVibe.Bot ships it (server/profiles/*.json) and serves it (GET /api/v1/profiles, /profiles/:id; validateProfile in server/profiles/index.js). The panel is a function of the profile. Capability and widget names are open strings that Bot checks against registries in code, so a new one never needs a schema change. As served, vendor, kind, description, variants and camera are null when the file leaves them out, limits carry their defaults (max_speed 1, max_turn 1, max_command_ms 300, heartbeat_ms 1000) and commands always include halt. mapping is the driver's own hardware map, open beyond driver. commands.button (an owner's buttons: names, each a label with an optional key, cooldown_ms and hold) and commands.point (a video-click layer, with its own cooldown_ms), rendered by the widget types buttons and video_click, were added in 0.109.0 (plan T15 R9).

schema.title: BotDeviceMessage
schema.description: bot.device-message@1 (ADR-043 decision 5): one frame on OpenVibe.Bot's device WebSocket (wss://openvibe.bot/device), JSON with v, seq and ts on every frame. Server to device: hello, config, command, estop, heartbeat_ack, error, paired (after a pair frame), rotate (a Network-paired machine is asked to rotate its credential with Network), voice_answer (Vibe's answer to a voice_ask). Device to server: pair (the only frame an unauthenticated socket may send), status, telemetry, ack, nack, heartbeat, reauth (Network-paired machines), estop_state, voice_ask (what the person asked after the machine's call word). The job frames on the same socket are platform.job-frame@1, not this contract. This duplicates two implementations that must not drift: OpenVibe.Bot server/realtime.js (the sender and reader in Bot) and OpenVibe.Node internal/protocol/protocol.go (the Go structs of the device agent).

oneOf.description: Server to device, once authenticated.
Server to device: the effective limits (the owner's clamped by the profile's), the kinds the profile takes and the latch; sent again when any of them changes.

voice.description: Vibe by voice: the owner turned it on for this machine, so it may listen for its call word and send voice_ask (absent or false: it does not).

call_word.description: The call word the owner chose ("hey vibe" unless they chose another); sent with voice on.

oneOf.description: Server to device: id is minted by Bot (the device's idempotency key), ref is the operator's own id. Never queued for an offline device, never replayed.

value.description: The command's value. screen_stream (OpenVibe.Node v0.12.0): {action: 'start', whip_url, publish_key, seconds? (30-1800, default 600), fps? (1-5, default 2)} or {action: 'stop'}: the machine's screen shown live on its own private OpenRestream stream. Bot alone fills in whip_url and publish_key (the machine's stream, playback private, never recorded); no operator, agent or service sends this kind.

deadline_ms.description: Absolute deadline, epoch milliseconds; the device stops the motion at it. For exec, fs, screen and screen_stream it is the reply window.

turn_epoch.description: The robot's control epoch when Bot decided this command (Bot#155): it rises each time a queue turn ends, is left or is paused by an owner takeover, and Bot's own halt for that change carries the new value. A device or plugin may refuse a command whose turn_epoch is lower than the newest halt's, defence in depth on top of Bot's own guarantee that nothing decided under a turn is sent after that turn's halt. Milliseconds on Bot's clock, so it keeps rising across Bot restarts. Absent from Bots before 0.213.0 and on robots without a turn queue.

target.description: OpenVibe.Node only: the driver to send it to.
