schema.title: BotCommand
schema.description: bot.command@1: an operator's command frame on OpenVibe.Bot's operator WebSocket (wss://openvibe.bot/control, after join; server/realtime.js onOperatorCommand). id is the operator's idempotency key (at most 64 characters; Bot mints one when it is missing): a repeated id answers with the first result. Bot's gate stamps the robot, the operator and the role, builds the value from the robot profile's commands (clamped by the owner's limits) and sets the deadline; ms asks for a duration within max_command_ms. Answered by one command_result frame (bot.command-result@1). The kinds button (a profile button by name, with an optional state for a hold button) and point (a normalised x, y video click) were added in 0.109.0 (plan T15 R9). The computer kinds (exec, fs, screen, input, browser; OpenVibe.Node's computer plugin, Node docs/computer.md) are taken only for a person's own machine, from its owner or an agent the owner let use it (bot.computer.control); the machine's owner sets on the machine what they may do, and the answer comes back in bot.command-result@1's data. probe (a read-only check of something on the machine's own network) is the one computer kind OpenVibe.Watch may send, for owners who let their watches use the computer. input (added in 0.171.0) moves the mouse, clicks, scrolls, types or presses keys on the machine's screen, at coordinates in the space of the screen picture the caller last saw (its width and height; the Node scales them to the real screen): refused at level observe, approved one by one at ask. browser (added in 0.174.0) drives a Chromium-family browser the agent uses on the machine, in a profile of its own: open an http(s) URL, click a CSS selector or the button or link showing a text, fill a field, press a named key, go back, read the page, take a screenshot, or close it. read, screenshot and close run at every level; the rest act (refused at observe, approved one by one at ask), and below level full open refuses an address on the machine's own network. desk (added in 0.214.0; plan track K, Vibe's desk) starts, stops or reports a private desk on the machine: a display of its own (Xvfb, a window manager, its own session and browser profile) where an agent works without touching the person's screen, which the person can watch and take over; screen, input and browser take desk: private to act there instead of on the person's screen (main, the default). Starting and stopping a desk act (refused at observe, approved one by one at ask); status runs at every level.

mode.description: write: create (default) never replaces a file

keys.description: one key or chord, for example Return, Escape, ctrl+s, alt+Tab

schema.title: BotCommandResult
schema.description: bot.command-result@1: the command_result frame OpenVibe.Bot answers a bot.command@1 with on the operator WebSocket (server/realtime.js). result: ack or nack (the device answered; reason is its fault code, latency_ms the round trip), refused (the gate refused it; code is Bot's refusal code such as bot.estop_latched, bot.cooldown or bot.device_offline, and reason says why), expired (no answer before the deadline) or pending (the same id is still in flight). cached is true when a repeated id is answered from the first result. An ack of a computer command (exec, fs, screen) carries its answer in data.

schema.title: BotJobDispatchResult
schema.description: bot.job-dispatch-result@1: what OpenVibe.Bot answers OpenVibe.Run's bot.job.dispatch calls (server/api/v1.js and server/jobs/index.js). POST /api/v1/jobs is 201 { job, sent }: `job` is Bot's run_jobs record and `sent` says whether the `job` frame went out on the device link now (false while the paired Node is away; it is resent on every reconnect until the Node acks it). POST /api/v1/jobs/:id/cancel is 200 { job, sent } with the same shape: `sent` says whether a `job_cancel` frame went out. GET /api/v1/jobs/:id is 200 { job, stdout }: the record plus the last 1 MiB of the job's captured stdout, or null when the Node sent none. The record's `state` follows the run_jobs lifecycle queued -> placed (the Node acked) -> running (job_started) -> one end state, and its `job` field is the platform.job@1 body Run dispatched, stored and resent verbatim. A refused dispatch answers a problem instead (422 bot.invalid_job, 404 bot.device_not_found, 409 bot.class_unadvertised, 409 bot.job_id_reused), never this contract.

job.description: One run_jobs row as presentJob renders it: what Run dispatched, to which device, and how far the job and its metering have come.

id.description: The platform.job@1 id Run minted and the stem of every usage reading key (run:<id>:<n>).

node_id.description: The paired device the job was sent to; a Node never reads another device's job.

state.description: queued (stored; sent and resent until acked), placed (the Node acked it), running (job_started), then one end state from job_exit: succeeded (exited 0), failed (another exit code, or reason limit, stopped or failed, or a nack), cancelled (a cancel before start, or reason cancelled), expired (reason ttl).

project_id.description: The payer project Run named; required on every dispatch (422 without it).

subject.description: The subject the readings are for (user:usr_…), as Run sent it; null when Run sent none.

provider.description: The offer's provider, as Run sent it; null for a first-party node.

cancel_requested.description: A cancel was asked for this job; a job not yet started is cancelled at once, a running one ends with its job_exit.

fault_code.description: The Node's nack fault code, or why Bot stopped sending the job (bot.class_unadvertised); null while it is still sendable.

sent_at.description: First time the `job` frame went out (epoch ms); null while queued and never sent.

started_ms.description: The Node's job_started started_ms: the anchor of every usage second; null until it started.

finished_at.description: When the first job_exit settled the job (epoch ms); null until then, and for a job cancelled before it started that no job_exit ever settled.

exit_reason.description: The first job_exit's reason (platform.job-frame@1); null until it arrived.

exit_code.description: The process's exit status; null when it was killed or never ran.

wall_ms.description: job_exit.usage.wall_ms as billed, capped at the job's limits.wall_ms; null until job_exit.

usage_read.description: Wall-clock seconds of the job already queued for Billing; only moves forward.

result.description: The job_exit result (any JSON); null unless a job_exit carried one.

job.description: The platform.job@1 body Run dispatched, stored and resent verbatim; present on every stored job.

created_at.description: Epoch ms Bot first stored the job.

updated_at.description: Epoch ms of the last change to the row.

stdout.description: The last 1 MiB of a job's captured stdout, held in memory by Bot (job_stdout chunks; a chunk_seq already held is dropped, and older chunks fall off once the ring is full).

text.description: The held chunks joined in order.

first_seq.description: The chunk_seq of the first held chunk; null when none is held.

last_seq.description: The highest chunk_seq seen for the job; 0 when none.

truncated.description: True when an earlier chunk fell off the 1 MiB ring.

dispatched.description: The answer of POST /api/v1/jobs (201) and POST /api/v1/jobs/:id/cancel (200): the row and whether the frame went out on the link now.

sent.description: True when the `job` (dispatch) or `job_cancel` (cancel) frame was written to the device's link; false when the device is away (a job is resent on reconnect until acked).

state.description: The answer of GET /api/v1/jobs/:id (200): the row and the job's held stdout (null when the Node sent none).

schema.title: BotRobotReadRequest

schema.title: BotPairRequest
schema.description: bot.pair-request@1: the body of POST /api/v1/pair on OpenVibe.Bot (and the fields of the pair frame on /device): a one-time pairing code (8 Crockford base32 characters, XXXX-XXXX) is its own credential and idempotency. robot narrows the code to one robot (wrong tries are then counted and lock the code); the rest is what the agent declares. schema.title: BotPairResult
schema.description: bot.pair-result@1: the 201 answers of OpenVibe.Bot's pairing routes (server/api/v1.js). POST /api/v1/pair → { device_id, credential, publish_key, whip_url?, robot_id, profile }; POST /api/v1/devices/bind (a Network node token) → the same without credential. The credential, the publish key and the WHIP URL are shown once and never again. Without OpenRestream configured there is no key: video is not_configured instead.

credential.description: The device credential: shown once (Bot keeps only its hash).

publish_key.description: The WHIP publish key, an ingest key OpenRestream issued for the robot's stream: shown once.

whip_url.description: Where the device publishes its camera (BOT_WHIP_BASE/<publish key>); it carries the key, so it is shown once too. Absent when BOT_WHIP_BASE is unset.

credential.description: The device credential: shown once (Bot keeps only its hash).

schema.description: bot.robot.online v1 (OpenVibe.Bot server/domain/index.js setOnline). A device authenticated on /device and serves the robot; one event per robot it is attached to. Envelope: subject { type: robot, id: <robot id> }, visibility internal, priority important, actor service:bot.

schema.title: BotRobotOfflinePayload
schema.description: bot.robot.offline v1 (OpenVibe.Bot server/domain/index.js setOnline). Envelope: subject { type: robot, id: <robot id> }, visibility internal, priority important, actor service:bot.

owner.description: The robot owner's user subject (Bot since 0.192.0; absent from older events). OpenVibe.Quest credits the owner's "Bring a robot online" quest from it.

schema.title: BotEstopSetPayload
schema.description: bot.estop.set v1 (OpenVibe.Bot server/domain/index.js writeEstop). The e-stop latched. by is the user subject, the service token's sub or the device id that set it; principal_kind says which. Envelope: subject { type: robot, id: <robot id> }, visibility internal, priority important, actor service:bot.

schema.description: bot.estop.cleared v1 (OpenVibe.Bot server/domain/index.js writeEstop via clearEstop). Envelope: subject { type: robot, id: <robot id> }, visibility internal, priority important, actor service:bot.

schema.title: BotCommandRefusedPayload
schema.description: bot.command.refused v1 (OpenVibe.Bot server/domain/index.js auditCommand). The gate refused a command (role, allowlist, limits, policy, e-stop, cooldown, turn, device offline) or a device reported an e-stop for a robot it is not attached to (kind estop_state). reason is Bot's refusal code; ids, kinds and codes only, never the value. schema.title: BrowserProviderJobCreateRequest
schema.description: browser-provider.job-create-request@1 (PLANNED; plan T14 R4a, ADR-034): the body OpenVibe.Run POSTs to an external managed-browser provider's job endpoint (capability browser_provider.job.dispatch). ID is the platform.job@1 id (job_<ULID>) and is also the idempotency key: a repeat POST with the same id answers the first job (200, created false) and never starts a second. CLASS is always browser. ARGS is the job's declared input as JSON (Run refuses more than 512 KiB serialized before it ever sends). INPUTS are files, each an OpenVibe.Media object pinned by sha256; never a URL, so the provider fetches nothing a caller chose. LIMITS are the hard caps of platform.job@1 (wall_ms required; cpu_ms and mem_bytes when the provider can enforce them). EGRESS is the network the job may reach, the values of OpenVibe.Node's worker.egress, as platform.job@1 `net` carries it. The request carries no project, subject, requester, token or other credential: the provider never learns who pays, and Run authenticates to it with a key from Run's own environment, sent in a header and never in this body. The provider's answer is browser-provider.job-create-result@1.

args.description: The job's declared input as JSON; Run enforces the 512 KiB cap before sending.

inputs.description: Files for the job, each an OpenVibe.Media object pinned by sha256; names are unique; empty when the job has none.

limits.description: Caps on the running job (platform.job@1 limits); the provider ends a job that hits one with exit_reason limit.

wall_ms.description: Running time from the job's start

cpu_ms.description: CPU time, user plus system; when the provider can enforce it

mem_bytes.description: Peak resident memory; when the provider can enforce it

schema.title: BrowserProviderJobCreateResult
schema.description: browser-provider.job-create-result@1 (PLANNED; plan T14 R4a, ADR-034): an external managed-browser provider's answer to OpenVibe.Run's job POST (browser-provider.job-create-request@1): 201 { job, created: true } when it accepted a new job, 200 { job, created: false } for an idempotent repeat of an id it already holds (the first job's state, nothing started twice). JOB is browser-provider.job-state@1 and Run validates it before adopting any of it. A refused POST answers a problem instead (4xx; 5xx is retried by Run on its next tick), never this contract. For the later calls, GET <provider>/jobs/:id answers browser-provider.job-state@1 and POST <provider>/jobs/:id/cancel answers it too; a 404 on either means the provider does not know the job.

created.description: True when this POST created the job (201); false for an idempotent repeat (200).

schema.title: BrowserProviderJobState
schema.description: browser-provider.job-state@1 (PLANNED; plan T14 R4a, ADR-034): an external managed-browser provider's state of one job, the body of GET <provider>/jobs/:id and the `job` of browser-provider.job-create-result@1. OpenVibe.Run validates it before adopting any of it: a malformed state is never adopted, and the job stays as Run last saw it. A 404 on GET or on cancel means the provider does not know the job (Run fails the job run.job.worker_failed). STATE is queued, running, then one end state: succeeded, failed, cancelled or expired. WALL_MS is the provider's CLAIM of the time the job ran, nothing more: Run bills from its own observed duration and clamps a larger claim (observed plus 5 s), so this field never sets a price. STARTED_MS and FINISHED_MS are the provider's clock, Unix ms, null until they happen. EXIT_REASON uses the reasons of platform.job-frame@1 `job_exit` (exited, cancelled, ttl, limit, stopped, failed) and is null until the job ended. EXIT_CODE is the browser script's exit status, null when it was killed or never ran. RESULT is the declared output (an object, at most 256 KiB serialized), null unless the job succeeded. STDOUT is the captured output in the ring shape OpenVibe.Bot returns (bot.job-dispatch-result@1) so Run's poller streams it the same way, or null when there is none. There is no node, project or class field: a provider cannot name a node or a project.

anyOf.description: The held tail of the job's stdout, the ring shape of bot.job-dispatch-result@1.

text.description: The held chunks joined in order, at most 1 MiB.

first_seq.description: The chunk_seq of the first held chunk; null when none is held.

last_seq.description: The highest chunk_seq seen for the job; 0 when none.

truncated.description: True when an earlier chunk fell off the ring.

stdout.description: The captured stdout, or null when the job has none.
