started_ms.description: When the job started, provider's clock, Unix ms; null until it started.

finished_ms.description: When the job ended, provider's clock, Unix ms; null until it ended.

wall_ms.description: The provider's CLAIM of the running time; Run clamps it to its own observed duration plus 5 s and never bills above that. 0 while the job has not run.

exit_reason.description: Why the job ended, as platform.job-frame@1 job_exit reason; null until it ended.

exit_code.description: The script's exit status; null when it was killed or never ran.

result.description: The declared output as a JSON object, at most 256 KiB serialized; null unless the job succeeded.

anyOf.description: The held tail of the job's stdout, the ring shape of bot.job-dispatch-result@1.

text.description: The held chunks joined in order, at most 1 MiB.

first_seq.description: The chunk_seq of the first held chunk; null when none is held.

last_seq.description: The highest chunk_seq seen for the job; 0 when none.

truncated.description: True when an earlier chunk fell off the ring.

stdout.description: The captured stdout, or null when the job has none.

schema.title: RunJobCreateRequest
schema.description: run.job-create-request@1 (PLANNED; plan T14 R1, ADR-034): the body of POST /api/v1/jobs on OpenVibe.Run (capability run.job.submit). The job belongs to the project the caller's token names, or, for a first-party service acting for a person (X-OV-Subject), the project it names with X-OV-Project once Network confirms the person is an admin or owner of it (ADR-003 amendment 2026-10-12); the person is then the requester and the service is recorded as via. CLASS is a platform.runtime-class@1 name; Run accepts any of them but places a job only on a node that advertises worker:<class> (platform.resource-offer@1), so a class no node runs today (browser, linux, desktop, gpu) ends expired with run.job.unplaceable. ARTIFACT is the pre-registered artifact to run (name and one exact version), required for function and code, as platform.job@1 carries it. ARGS is the artifact's declared input as JSON (at most 512 KiB serialized, else 413). INPUTS are files placed in the job directory before the process starts, each an OpenVibe.Media object pinned by its sha256: a size or digest mismatch fails the job (run.job.input_digest_mismatch) before the process ever runs; Run never fetches a caller-chosen URL. LIMITS are hard caps merged stricter with the node's own (platform.job@1 limits); a request over the project's tier cap is refused 422 run.limits.exceeded, never silently lowered. EGRESS is the network the job may reach, the values of OpenVibe.Node's worker.egress, carried per job as the same-named platform.job@1 net: none (default; no network), public or openvibe-only. A job asking for public or openvibe-only is placed only on a node whose worker.egress allows it; a worker whose host policy is stricter runs the stricter one. REQUIREMENTS (platform.workload-requirements@1) narrow placement; absent means { kind: run.<class>, mobility: job, latency_class: background, objective: balanced }. IDEMPOTENCY_KEY: a repeat from the same project within 24 h with an identical body answers the first job (200, created false); with a different body 409 run.idempotency.conflict. NODE pins the machine: the device id (dev_…) of the job's own machine in Run's placement (platform.resource-offer@1 node_id, as GET /api/v1/machines on OpenVibe.Bot names it), answered by 409 run.job.node_offline when that machine is not connected, never moved to another one (Codes C9c).

args.description: The artifact's declared input as JSON; default {}.

inputs.description: Files placed in the job directory before the process starts; names are unique (else 422).

ttl_ms.description: Lifetime from creation, covering the wait for a node and the run (platform.job@1 ttl_ms); when it runs out the job ends expired. Default: limits.wall_ms plus 600000.

node.description: The machine to run on, pinned: the device id (dev_…) of the job's own machine in Run's placement, as platform.resource-offer@1 node_id and OpenVibe.Bot's GET /api/v1/machines name it (Codes C9c). Run places the job only on that machine and refuses it 409 run.job.node_offline when it is not connected, never moving it to another one. Absent: Run places it on any machine that fits.

artifact.description: The pre-registered artifact to run (platform.job@1 artifact).

version.description: One exact version, never a range

input.description: One input file: an OpenVibe.Media object the caller's project can read, pinned by digest.

name.description: File name in the job directory; no path separators.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the object's bytes.

limits.description: Caps on the running process (platform.job@1 limits); hitting one ends the job failed with run.job.limit.

egress.description: OpenVibe.Node worker.egress values: none (no network), public (the internet without private, link-local or the network's own ranges), openvibe-only (the network's own endpoints only).

schema.title: RunJobCreateResult
schema.description: run.job-create-result@1 (PLANNED; plan T14 R1, ADR-034): the answer of POST /api/v1/jobs on OpenVibe.Run (capability run.job.submit). 201 with created true and the new job, queued; 200 with created false and the job first created under the same idempotency_key (in whatever state it has reached). Refusals are application/problem+json: 400 (body invalid), 413 (args over 512 KiB), 422 run.limits.exceeded or a duplicate input name, 409 run.idempotency.conflict, 429 (quota).

created.description: false when the idempotency_key matched an earlier job.

schema.title: RunJobReadResult
schema.description: run.job-read-result@1 (PLANNED; plan T14 R1, ADR-034): one job on OpenVibe.Run, as GET /api/v1/jobs/{id} answers it (capability run.job.read), POST /api/v1/jobs/{id}/cancel answers it after the cancel (run.job.cancel), and run.job-create-result@1 and run.job-list-result@1 carry it. STATES: queued (stored, waiting for a node) -> placed (sent to a node as platform.job@1, not yet started) -> running (the node sent job_started) -> one end state: succeeded (job_exit reason exited with code 0), failed (exited with another code, or reason limit, stopped or failed), cancelled (POST /api/v1/jobs/{id}/cancel, or job_exit reason cancelled), expired (ttl_ms ran out: before placement, before start, or while running, job_exit reason ttl). An end state never changes. Run mints the id (job_<ULID>) and sends it unchanged as platform.job@1 `id`, so every metering reading of the job is `run:<id>:<n>` (platform.job-frame@1 job_usage). usage.seconds is wall_ms / 1000: the sum of the job's readings (service run, operation function.invoke, unit s). Never carries the job's stdout (GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}/stream) or a credential. More fields may be added.

id.description: Minted by Run; the platform.job@1 id and the stem of every usage reading key (run:<id>:<n>).

project_id.description: The project the caller's token names; usage is billed to it.

requester.description: The token principal that submitted the job.

ttl_ms.description: The job's lifetime from created_at, the default filled in.

requirements.description: What the job was placed against, the default filled in.

placement.description: Where the job was sent; null while queued, and for a job cancelled or expired before placement.

started_at.description: From job_started started_ms; null until the process started.

finished_at.description: When the job reached its end state; null before.

exit.description: The node's job_exit; null until it arrived, and for a job that ended before a node ran it.

result.description: The artifact's declared output (job_exit result, any JSON); null unless state is succeeded.

error.description: Why the job failed or expired; null in every other state.

node.description: The worker's device id (the usage reading's `node`).

provider.description: The offer's provider (the usage reading's `provider`); null for a first-party node.

reason.description: platform.job-frame@1 job_exit reason.

code.description: The process's exit status; null when it was killed or never ran.

seconds.description: Metered wall-clock seconds, wall_ms / 1000 (unit s); 0 when the job never started.

code.description: run.job.exit_nonzero, run.job.limit, run.job.stopped, run.job.worker_failed, run.job.input_digest_mismatch, run.job.unplaceable (expired: no node offered the class, egress and requirements), run.job.ttl.

schema.title: RunJobListQuery
schema.description: run.job-list-query@1 (PLANNED; plan T14 R1): the query string of GET /api/v1/jobs on OpenVibe.Run (capability run.job.list) and of GET /api/v1/admin/jobs (run.job.admin, which alone may pass project_id). Without project_id it lists the caller's token project.

project_id.description: Admin only (run.job.admin): list this project's jobs; with run.job.list it is refused 403.

limit.description: Items per page, 1 to 200 (default 50). A query string carries it as a string, which must name the same range.

schema.title: RunJobListResult
schema.description: run.job-list-result@1 (PLANNED; plan T14 R1): the answer of GET /api/v1/jobs on OpenVibe.Run (capability run.job.list) and GET /api/v1/admin/jobs (run.job.admin), filtered by run.job-list-query@1. Jobs come newest first (by id). More fields may be added.

next_cursor.description: Pass as cursor for the next page; null on the last page.

schema.title: RunJobStreamTicketResult
schema.description: run.job-stream-ticket-result@1 (PLANNED; plan T14 R1): the answer of POST /api/v1/jobs/{id}/stream/ticket on OpenVibe.Run (capability run.job.stream), modelled on Events' realtime ticket (network.realtime-ticket-result@1). A browser cannot put a header on an EventSource, so it opens `${stream_url}?ticket=${ticket}` (plus Last-Event-ID when it resumes) at once. The ticket is a two-minute RS256 JWT that Run signs: audience openvibe.run, typ run-stream (so it is never a session token), it names this one job, and Run refuses a jti it has already seen while the ticket is valid, so a ticket opens one stream; ask for a fresh one for every reconnect. Never logged, never stored. A server caller may instead send its Bearer token to GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}/stream. The stream is text/event-stream of run.job-stream-event@1.

schema.title: RunJobStreamEvent
schema.description: run.job-stream-event@1 (PLANNED; plan T14 R1): the JSON `data` of one server-sent event on GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}/stream (capability run.job.stream). The SSE `event` field is the type and the SSE `id` is `seq`, so a reconnect with Last-Event-ID resumes after it. output: a chunk of the job's stdout (platform.job-frame@1 job_stdout, best effort: a chunk lost on the node's link is never resent, and Run keeps at most the last 1 MiB to replay). state: the job moved to a new state. end: the job reached its end state; the server closes the stream after it. A stream opened on an ended job replays what is kept, then end. Output is never metered and never in an event.

seq.description: The job's own stream counter from 1; the SSE id.

state.description: state and end: the job's state.

schema.title: RunJobQueuedPayload
schema.description: run.job.queued v1 (OpenVibe.Run; PLANNED: the Run service does not exist yet, plan T14 R1). A job was stored queued (POST /api/v1/jobs created it; not published for an idempotent repeat). A projection of run.job-read-result@1 without args, inputs, result or output. Envelope: subject { type: job, id: <job_id> }, visibility internal, priority low, actor service:run.

state.description: The job state (run.job-read-result@1 state).

schema.title: RunJobStartedPayload
schema.description: run.job.started v1 (OpenVibe.Run; PLANNED: the Run service does not exist yet, plan T14 R1). The node sent job_started: the process runs. Usage seconds count from started_at. A projection of run.job-read-result@1 without args, inputs, result or output. Envelope: subject { type: job, id: <job_id> }, visibility internal, priority low, actor service:run.

state.description: The job state (run.job-read-result@1 state).

schema.title: RunJobSucceededPayload
schema.description: run.job.succeeded v1 (OpenVibe.Run; PLANNED: the Run service does not exist yet, plan T14 R1). The job ended succeeded: job_exit reason exited with code 0. Carries no result (read it with GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}). A projection of run.job-read-result@1 without args, inputs, result or output. Envelope: subject { type: job, id: <job_id> }, visibility internal, priority normal, actor service:run.

state.description: The job state (run.job-read-result@1 state).

schema.title: RunJobFailedPayload
schema.description: run.job.failed v1 (OpenVibe.Run; PLANNED: the Run service does not exist yet, plan T14 R1). The job ended failed: job_exit with a non-zero code or reason limit, stopped or failed, or an input digest mismatch before the process started. A projection of run.job-read-result@1 without args, inputs, result or output. Envelope: subject { type: job, id: <job_id> }, visibility internal, priority important, actor service:run.

state.description: The job state (run.job-read-result@1 state).

schema.title: RunJobCancelledPayload
schema.description: run.job.cancelled v1 (OpenVibe.Run; PLANNED: the Run service does not exist yet, plan T14 R1). The job ended cancelled (POST /api/v1/jobs/{id}/cancel by its project or run.job.admin, or job_exit reason cancelled). A job cancelled before placement has no placement and no exit. A projection of run.job-read-result@1 without args, inputs, result or output. Envelope: subject { type: job, id: <job_id> }, visibility internal, priority normal, actor service:run.

state.description: The job state (run.job-read-result@1 state).

schema.title: RunJobExpiredPayload
schema.description: run.job.expired v1 (OpenVibe.Run; PLANNED: the Run service does not exist yet, plan T14 R1). The job ended expired: its ttl_ms ran out before a node took it (run.job.unplaceable), before it started, or while it ran (job_exit reason ttl, run.job.ttl). A projection of run.job-read-result@1 without args, inputs, result or output. Envelope: subject { type: job, id: <job_id> }, visibility internal, priority normal, actor service:run.

state.description: The job state (run.job-read-result@1 state).

schema.title: ResourceName
schema.description: common.resource-name@1: the one stable, cross-service name of an OpenVibe resource (OVRN; ADR-034 section 2, ADR-048, plan T13): ovrn:<service>:<project_id>:<type>/<id>, for example ovrn:media:prj_01J0000000000000000000000A:object/med_01K0000000000000000000000B. The service segment is the authority that owns the resource; the project segment is its tenancy boundary; type is the second half of a common.resource-summary@1 kind and id is that summary's id, so the name composes from any resource summary. It is used in grant scopes, audit rows, event subjects, usage records, bill lines and console URLs. It never names a person, an app, a request, a session or an event. The pattern is the one common.usage-recorded@1 resource and common.resource-summary@1 ovrn already use.

schema.title: ResourceControlRequest
schema.description: common.resource-control-request@1: one control operation OpenVibe.Services (or Actor's Console) sends to the authority that owns a resource (ADR-048, plan T13). Services never mutates another service's database; every create, update, start, stop, delete, resize, rotate, pair, grant or revoke is this request to the owning authority's control API, which decides and answers with a common.resource-control-result@1. A request names exactly one of resource (every action but create) or resource_kind (create, before the name exists). project_id is the tenancy boundary and equals the project segment of resource. idempotency_key makes a retry safe: the authority answers a repeated key with the first result. A sensitive action (money, publishing, deleting, physical control) is refused with confirmation_required until its owner approves; the retry carries that confirmation_id (roadmap WS-Z2). The cross-field rules are checked by contracts.resources.checkControlRequest.

resource.description: The resource acted on; required for every action but create.

resource_kind.description: service.type (a common.resource-summary@1 kind), for create, before the resource name exists.

params.description: Action-specific input, shaped by the authority's own contract (never redefined here).

on_behalf_of.description: The subject whose grant the authority checks; the caller's own token says who sent it.

confirmation_id.description: The approved confirmation from an earlier confirmation_required answer.

schema.title: OwnedResourceControlRequest
schema.description: common.owned-resource-control-request@1 (ADR-048 amendment 2026-10-15, step 8 phase 2): one control operation on a person-owned resource. Robots, chat rooms, restream definitions and pastes belong to a person, not to a project, so they carry no OVRN and the project-scoped common.resource-control-request@1 cannot name them. OpenVibe.Services sends this to the owning authority's POST /api/v1/resources/control (the same route, told apart by `owned`), acting for the person in on_behalf_of. owned names the resource by its index summary's kind and id. owner is the person it belongs to: the authority refuses unless its own record says the same (Services also offers actions only on the viewer's own resources). A sensitive action (deleting, physical control) asked by an agent is refused with confirmation_required until the owner approves, as for project resources. idempotency_key makes a retry safe: the authority answers a repeated key from the same caller with the first result, and refuses the key reused with another request. Answered with common.resource-control-result@1 (without resource: there is no OVRN). The actions each authority takes are in its <service>.resource.control capability; any other action is refused unsupported.

owned.description: The resource, as its owning authority's resource index lists it (common.resource-summary@1 kind and id).

id.description: The summary's id: a prefixed ULID (rob_…) or the service's own slug (a paste, a room).

owner.description: The person the resource belongs to. Person-owned resources belong to people, never to agents or apps.

params.description: Action-specific input, shaped by the authority's own contract (never redefined here).

on_behalf_of.description: Who asks: the owner, or their agent (whose sensitive actions wait for the owner's approval).

confirmation_id.description: The approved confirmation from an earlier confirmation_required answer.

schema.title: ResourceControlResult
schema.description: common.resource-control-result@1: the authority's answer to a common.resource-control-request@1 (ADR-048, plan T13). state is the outcome, not the resource's own state: done (applied), pending (accepted and asynchronous; the authority reports completion later on its events), refused (a policy or confirmation gate said no) or failed (an error). State rules: refused carries problem or confirmation_required; failed carries problem; done and pending carry neither; confirmation_required appears only on refused. result carries the authority's own response document and never another service's rows. The state rules are checked by contracts.resources.checkControlResult.

confirmation_required.description: The action needs its owner's approval; retry the same request with this confirmation_id once approved.

problem.description: RFC 9457 body when refused or failed.

schema.title: NetworkNodeRevokedPayload
schema.description: network.node.revoked v1 (OpenVibe.Network; plan T2, docs/t2-cells-and-node-principal.md section 10, migrations/0014_node_pairing.sql). A node principal (nod_…), a person's paired machine, was revoked: through POST /internal/node-principals/:id/revoke (network.node.manage, the service that paired it), through POST /api/v1/me/nodes/:id/revoke (the owner's session), or with the owner's account. Network revokes the row and clears the credential and its grace window; a machine holding a live node token is refused at its next use (≤ 300 s), and until this event only learned of the revoke at its next reauth (≤ 330 s). A consumer stops the machine at once; a second revoke changes nothing and emits nothing. The credential and its hash are never carried. Envelope: subject { type: node_principal, id: <nod_…> }, visibility internal, actor the service (svc:<service>) or the owner ({ type: user }) that revoked.

node_id.description: The machine's node id (platform_node_principals.node_id), minted with the principal and unique among principals.

principal_id.description: The revoked node principal. Also the envelope subject id.

owner.description: Who the machine belongs to, as GET /api/v1/me/nodes and the operator list show it: the person who paired it, the project it is paired into, or the platform for a Host-reported machine.

reason.description: Why it was revoked, when the caller gave one (the owner's text or the service's); absent otherwise.

schema.title: SpaceThreadCreatedPayload
schema.description: space.thread.created v1 (OpenVibe.Space server/events.js, queued in the transaction of the change). A forum thread was started in a space. Envelope: subject { type: thread, id }, visibility public when the item is public else internal, priority low, actor the person or service:space.

url.description: The public page, or null when the item is not public.

schema.title: SpacePostCreatedPayload
schema.description: space.post.created v1 (OpenVibe.Space server/events.js, queued in the transaction of the change). A reply was posted in a forum thread. Never the body. Envelope: subject { type: post, id }, visibility public when the item is public else internal, priority low, actor the person or service:space.

url.description: The public page, or null when the item is not public.

schema.title: SpaceModerationActionPayload
schema.description: space.moderation.action v1 (ADR-022; OpenVibe.Space server/events.js moderationAction). A staff or space moderator action on someone else's forum content, or a space moderator assignment: deleting, locking or unlocking a thread, deleting a post, adding or removing a space moderator. Not a person acting on their own content. Written to Space's outbox in the transaction that performs the action; OpenVibe.Network keeps it in the moderation audit log. The payload is common.moderation-action@1. Envelope: subject { type: moderation_action, id: <target type>:<target id> }, visibility internal, actor the moderator. Never carries the content itself.

schema.title: ActorTaskCreateRequest
schema.description: actor.task-create-request@1: the body of POST /api/v1/tasks on OpenVibe.Actor (capability actor.task.create), the creation subset of platform.task@1. TASK is the instruction in plain words. MODE is the planner objective (default balanced). BUDGET caps what this task may cost (per_task_usd) and what the caller's tasks may cost in one UTC day (per_day_usd); either may be left out for the person's free-allowance defaults, and a value above the person's tier is refused 422 actor.budget.over_tier, never silently lowered. AGENT pins one agent system by its id from GET /api/v1/agents (routing still checks that it can take the task). IDEMPOTENCY_KEY: a repeat from the same requester within 24 h with an identical body answers the first task (200), with a different body 409 actor.idempotency.conflict. WEBHOOKS (at most 8): each an https URL and the state changes to deliver there (the names of platform.task@1 `state`). Actor signs every delivery with a secret it mints for the task, returned once as `webhook_secret` in the answer that created it (and in an idempotent repeat), and POSTs actor.task-webhook@1 through its egress guard: public addresses only, ports 443 or 8443, no credentials in the URL, never a redirect. A URL that cannot be delivered to is refused 422 actor.webhook.refused. A webhook may instead name a project secret (`secret_ref`, ADR-056): its deliveries are then signed by OpenVibe.Network with that secret, in the same headers, and no webhook_secret is minted when every webhook names one. A secret_ref on a task outside a project is refused 422 actor.webhook.secret_unavailable.

agent.description: An agent system id from GET /api/v1/agents.

url.description: The HTTPS endpoint Actor POSTs to.

events.description: The state changes delivered; the names of platform.task@1 `state`.

secret_ref.description: The name of a project secret (ADR-056) that signs this webhook's deliveries instead of the task's own secret. The task must be made in a project (by an app or agent token carrying project_id and env); the secret is looked up in that project and environment, and the project must have granted it to actor for sign. Actor never sees the value: OpenVibe.Network computes each signature.

webhooks.description: Where Actor tells the caller about this task's state changes (plan T17).

examples.task: Find out who runs the mail for openvibe.network and whether its SPF and DMARC are set up properly.
Summarize today's top three posts on openvibe.news.

schema.title: ActorAgentManageRequest
schema.description: actor.agent-manage-request@1: bodies of actor.agent.manage on OpenVibe.Actor. POST /api/v1/me/agents { name, instructions, mode?, budget_per_run_usd?, daily_runs_max?, schedule?, schedule_at?, schedule_dow?, quiet_from?, quiet_to?, send_to_vibe?, status? } creates a personal agent (10 per person: 429 actor.agent.limit); PATCH /api/v1/me/agents/:id takes any subset. POST /api/v1/me/agents/:id/memory { text } adds a note (1–1000 characters; 50 notes, the oldest agent-written note goes first, a person's note never automatically) and PATCH /api/v1/me/agents/:id/memory/:mem { text } edits one. Unknown fields are 422 actor.agent.invalid; another person's agent is 404 actor.agent.not_found.

budget_per_run_usd.description: At most the person's per-task allowance.

schedule_at.description: HH:MM UTC, for daily and weekly.

quiet_from.description: HH:MM UTC: quiet hours start. No scheduled run starts from quiet_from to quiet_to (the window may cross midnight; an hourly run waits until it ends); a run its owner starts still runs. Both or neither.

send_to_vibe.description: Post each finished run into the person's own Vibe chat named after the agent (chat.vibe.deliver), so each run is a chat they can open and continue. Default true.

schema.title: ActorAgentManageResult
schema.description: actor.agent-manage-result@1: GET /api/v1/me/agents → { agents }; an agent (create 201, read, update); GET …/memory → { memory } (newest first); a note (create 201, update). DELETE answers 204 with no body.

budget_per_run_usd.description: At most the person's per-task allowance.

schedule_at.description: HH:MM UTC, for daily and weekly.

quiet_from.description: HH:MM UTC: quiet hours start. No scheduled run starts from quiet_from to quiet_to (the window may cross midnight; an hourly run waits until it ends); a run its owner starts still runs. Both or neither.

send_to_vibe.description: Post each finished run into the person's own Vibe chat named after the agent (chat.vibe.deliver), so each run is a chat they can open and continue. Default true.

budget_per_run_usd.description: At most the person's per-task allowance.

schedule_at.description: HH:MM UTC, for daily and weekly.

quiet_from.description: HH:MM UTC: quiet hours start. No scheduled run starts from quiet_from to quiet_to (the window may cross midnight; an hourly run waits until it ends); a run its owner starts still runs. Both or neither.

send_to_vibe.description: Post each finished run into the person's own Vibe chat named after the agent (chat.vibe.deliver), so each run is a chat they can open and continue. Default true.

schema.title: ActorAgentRunRequest
schema.description: actor.agent-run-request@1: POST /api/v1/me/agents/:id/run { input? } runs the agent now as an ordinary Actor task (its instructions, then its memory, then the input), under the same free tier, budget and daily limits as the person's own tasks, plus the agent's daily_runs_max (429 actor.agent.limit). Answered 201 with the task (platform.task@1). GET /api/v1/me/agents/:id/runs lists its tasks, newest first.

schema.title: ActorA2ATaskRequest
schema.description: actor.a2a-task-request@1: POST /a2a/v1/tasks gives OpenVibe.Actor one A2A task (the Agent2Agent shape: a message with text parts, an optional skill and an optional id to continue). The caller is a Network service token with the capability actor.a2a.task acting for a person (X-OV-Subject); the task runs under that person's allowance and allow-list, exactly like a task they started. Answered 201 with the A2A task (actor.a2a-task-result@1).

schema.title: ActorA2ATaskResult
schema.description: actor.a2a-task-result@1: the A2A task OpenVibe.Actor accepted or answered: its id, its state (submitted, working, completed, failed), the text answer when it has one and the id of the Actor task behind it. Never a credential.

schema.title: ActorTaskEvent
schema.description: actor.task-event@1: one event on a task's live stream (GET /api/v1/tasks/:id/events, text/event-stream; the SSE id is SEQ, so a reader resumes with Last-Event-ID). KIND is run.job-stream-event@1's three, as platform.task@1 progress names them: state (the task moved to STATE), output (one step of the agent's work: AGENT says what it is doing in TEXT, or calls TOOL with a short INPUT summary, or a tool answered), end (the task ended in STATE; nothing follows). Events are best-effort; the task record (GET /api/v1/tasks/:id) is the source of truth.

schema.title: ActorTaskEvent
schema.description: actor.task-event@2: one event on a task's live stream (GET /api/v1/tasks/:id/events, text/event-stream; the SSE id is SEQ, so a reader resumes with Last-Event-ID). Every field of actor.task-event@1 keeps its meaning and shape: KIND is run.job-stream-event@1's three, as platform.task@1 progress names them: state (the task moved to STATE), output (one step of the agent's work: AGENT says what it is doing in TEXT, calls TOOL with a short INPUT summary, or a tool answered), end (the task ended in STATE; nothing follows). v2 adds ARTIFACTS to a tool_result: the files and charts that tool made, stored on OpenVibe.Media, private to the task's requester, each with a stable Actor link the task page and a shared session can open. Events are best-effort; the task record (GET /api/v1/tasks/:id) and its result (which carries every artifact of the run) are the source of truth.

artifacts.description: The files and charts this tool made, in the order it made them. They belong to the task's requester on OpenVibe.Media; URL is Actor's stable link (GET /api/v1/tasks/:id/artifacts/:mediaId), which signs a fresh Media URL for the requester when it is opened, never an expiring signed URL. A public-chat task has no requester and makes none.

schema.title: ActorTaskListResult
schema.description: actor.task-list-result@1: GET /api/v1/tasks (capability actor.task.list): the caller's latest tasks, newest first, and NEXT, the `before` cursor for the following page (null on the last page).

schema.title: ActorTaskWebhook
schema.description: actor.task-webhook@1: the body OpenVibe.Actor POSTs to a task's webhook (plan T17) when the task reaches a state the webhook asked for. TYPE is actor.task.state; DELIVERY_ID is stable across retries (dedupe on it); STATE is the state reached; TASK is platform.task@1 as it was at that moment, without webhook_secret. Headers: X-OpenVibe-Delivery-Id, X-OpenVibe-Task-Id, X-OpenVibe-Task-State, X-OpenVibe-Delivery-Attempt, X-OpenVibe-Timestamp and X-OpenVibe-Signature-V2 (HMAC-SHA256 of "<timestamp>.<raw body>" with the task's webhook_secret; openvibe-sdk/events verifyDeliveryV2 checks it and the ±300 s window). A 2xx answer is delivered; 410 Gone, or a URL the egress guard refuses at send time, ends the delivery at once; anything else is retried with backoff for about a day. Deliveries never delay or change the task.

schema.title: ActorAgentListResult
schema.description: actor.agent-list-result@1: GET /api/v1/agents (capability actor.agent.read): every agent system Actor can route a task to. KIND is the backend class (ADR-044): openvibe-runtime (OpenVibe's own agent, acting through OpenVibe services), agent-platform (another platform's agent, called through its API), open-model (an open model on OpenVibe's own hardware), codes (coding work through OpenVibe.Codes), node and run (a person's machine or OpenVibe.Run). TRUST is ADR-046's class; private mode takes only first-party ones. CAN are the task classes and tools it takes (task:<class>, tool:<name>). RATE_CARD is the published price, revised by review and never written by a model (SOURCE says where it comes from, VERIFIED_AT when a person last checked it). AVAILABLE says whether it can take a task now and REASON why not.

per_call_usd.description: A fixed charge per tool call the platform bills (for example a web search).

schema.title: ActorAgentListResult
schema.description: actor.agent-list-result@2: GET /api/v1/agents (capability actor.agent.read). Every field of agent-list-result@1 keeps its meaning and shape (AGENTS: the systems Actor can run a task on, with trust, capabilities, rate card and availability). v2 adds what Actor's one agent loop resolves its model tiers to: TIERS is the model behind each tier (fast: classifying and small steps; smart: the loop; best: hard tasks and best mode; check: the verifier of another family; vision: reading images and screens), and MODELS lists the models the server's keys reach. A tier always names its provider and model, so a caller never has to guess which backend a task will run on.

per_call_usd.description: A fixed charge per tool call the platform bills (for example a web search).

tiers.description: The model each tier resolves to on this server.

models.description: The models the server's configured keys reach, as listed by the providers.

schema.title: ActorWait
schema.description: actor.wait@1: one wait (plan A2, Watch mode): the task and the step it belongs to, whose it is, what wakes it (until), the deadline, what happens when nothing comes (on_timeout) and the short line the person reads. A wait is a record, not a running loop: while a task waits, no model runs, its desk is released and its budget clock stops. The event that woke it is untrusted input: woken_by names the event, never its payload.

filter.description: The bounded matcher: a path (payload.a.b, subject.id, subject.type, actor.id, trace_id) and the value (or one of the values) the event must carry there. At most eight clauses; a filter is a matcher, not a query.

until.description: What wakes the wait: an Events topic (plus the earliest event it may match), a Watch target, or a time.

schema.title: FoodPantryRequest
schema.description: food.pantry-request@1: PUT /api/v1/pantry on OpenVibe.Food replaces the pantry with exactly these food slugs.

schema.title: FoodHouseholdChatContext
schema.description: food.household-chat-context@1: what food.household.read answers (GET /internal/households/:planId/chat-context): a household's pantry and plan as plain text for the AI member of its OpenVibe.Chat room, and where it comes from.

text.description: The household's members, the plan (days, people, budget, meals), what is still to buy and what is in their cupboards.

source.description: A label for the prompt, e.g. 'OpenVibe.Food household'.

schema.title: FoodPantryResult
schema.description: food.pantry-result@1: GET and PUT /api/v1/pantry on OpenVibe.Food: the slugs, each food as the food list shows it, and the suggestions matched against them (can_make: everything there; almost: one or two items missing, named).

schema.title: FoodPlan
schema.description: food.plan@1: one saved plan on OpenVibe.Food.

plan.description: The plan as Food worked it out: spec, items (the shopping list), by_store, menu (one entry a day: breakfast, lunch, dinner, snack), group_coverage and totals (cost, cost_per_person_day, kcal, protein). Food may add fields.

schema.title: FoodPlanCreateRequest
schema.description: food.plan-create-request@1: POST /api/v1/plans on OpenVibe.Food. people 1-12, days 1-14, budget (US dollars for the whole plan) optional, title optional.

schema.title: FoodPlanResult
schema.description: food.plan-result@1: answers of the plan routes on OpenVibe.Food: GET /api/v1/plans → { plans }; GET /api/v1/plans/:id and POST /api/v1/plans (201) → the plan itself (food.plan@1).

schema.title: InventoryKind
schema.description: An item kind (ADR-054 §2): what items of the kind carry (an attribute schema), where they can be equipped (slots) and which surfaces render them. A new kind is a contract plus a renderer, never a new table.

id.description: <namespace>.<kind>, e.g. live.name_effect, games.skin, network.badge.

slots.description: Where one item of the kind can be equipped; empty: the kind is not equippable (a collectible, a badge shown on the profile).

surface.description: Where an item of this kind shows.

renderer.description: The renderer contract the surface implements for this kind, e.g. live.name_effect.css@1.

attributes.description: A JSON Schema every definition's attributes must satisfy.

stackable.description: True: one person may hold several instances of one definition.

workshop.description: A Workshop kind (ADR-054 §6): any signed-in person may submit a definition of it, issued by and credited to them, published only after staff review.

schema.title: InventoryDefinition
schema.description: An item definition (ADR-054 §2): one item of a kind, issued by a service, an app or a creator, with an honest rarity, attributes valid against the kind and an optional supply cap. Published definitions can be granted; retired ones cannot, and their instances stay.

media_id.description: An OpenVibe.Media object (an image, an animation).

token.description: A token the kind's renderers know (a CSS class, a speech preset).

rarity.description: Shown as is; any odds that apply are shown with it, never hidden.

aliases.description: Earlier ids of the same item (Live's fx_rainbow, hat_crown, …).

credit.description: The creator of a community item (ADR-054 §6).

grantors.description: Other services or apps the issuer lets grant this one item (ADR-054 §3): Quest giving Live's hats as quest rewards. They grant only (origin earned or granted, idempotent per key); defining, editing, consuming and revoking stay the issuer's.

schema.title: InventoryInstance
schema.description: One item a person owns (ADR-054 §2): a definition, its origin and state. bought and traded are reserved for the later money ADR (ADR-054 §5) and are refused until it is accepted.

attributes.description: Per-instance values (a serial number, a wear value), valid against the kind.

serial.description: The instance's number within a capped supply.

schema.title: InventoryList
schema.description: A person's inventory page: their instances, newest first, with the definitions they refer to. The public read shows only owned instances of published definitions; the person's own read (inventory.item.list) also shows consumed and revoked ones.

schema.title: InventoryEquipped
schema.description: What a person has equipped (ADR-054 §2), keyed <kind>:<slot>. Surfaces read it in batches (inventory.equipped-batch@1) and cache it briefly.

token.description: The definition's art token, so a renderer needs no second read.

media_id.description: The definition's art image (an OpenVibe.Media object), so a renderer needs no second read.

schema.title: InventoryEquippedBatch
schema.description: The equipped sets of many people at once (GET /api/v1/equipped?subjects=…, up to 100): one query on the authority, one call per chat render batch.

schema.title: InventoryGrantRequest
schema.description: An issuer grants one instance of a definition it issued to a person (inventory.item.grant). Idempotent per idempotency_key: a repeat answers the instance already granted. A capped definition that is sold out answers 409 inventory.supply_exhausted.

reason.description: Shown in the ledger: what the person did (a quest, an event, a milestone).

schema.title: InventoryReviewRequest
schema.description: Staff's decision on a Workshop definition in review (ADR-054 §6): publish it (optionally with an honest rarity other than common) or reject it with a reason the creator sees.

reason.description: Required for reject: what the creator reads.

schema.title: InventoryEquipRequest
schema.description: Equip an instance the person owns in one slot of its kind, or clear the slot (instance_id null). One item per slot; equipping replaces what was there.

schema.title: InventoryDefinitionRequest
schema.description: Create or edit a definition in the issuer's namespace (inventory.definition.manage). A service's or app's definition is published when it asks; a creator's goes to staff review (in_review) first.

media_id.description: An OpenVibe.Media object (an image, an animation).

token.description: A token the kind's renderers know (a CSS class, a speech preset).

publish.description: Ask for publication (a creator's definition goes to review).

grantors.description: Other services or apps the issuer lets grant this one item (ADR-054 §3): Quest giving Live's hats as quest rewards. They grant only (origin earned or granted, idempotent per key); defining, editing, consuming and revoking stay the issuer's.

schema.title: InventoryItemGrantedPayload
schema.description: inventory.item.granted v1 (OpenVibe.Inventory, ADR-054). An instance was granted or earned (ADR-054 §4). Envelope: subject { type: user, id: owner }, visibility subject, actor the issuer.

schema.title: InventoryItemConsumedPayload
schema.description: inventory.item.consumed v1 (OpenVibe.Inventory, ADR-054). An issuer consumed an instance (a one-use item used up). Envelope: subject { type: user, id: owner }, visibility subject.

schema.title: InventoryItemRevokedPayload
schema.description: inventory.item.revoked v1 (OpenVibe.Inventory, ADR-054). An issuer or staff revoked an instance (granted in error, abuse). Envelope: subject { type: user, id: owner }, visibility subject.

schema.title: InventoryItemEquippedPayload
schema.description: inventory.item.equipped v1 (OpenVibe.Inventory, ADR-054). A person equipped an instance in a slot; surfaces drop their cached equipped set. Envelope: subject { type: user, id: owner }, visibility public.

schema.title: InventoryItemUnequippedPayload
schema.description: inventory.item.unequipped v1 (OpenVibe.Inventory, ADR-054). A person cleared a slot. Envelope: subject { type: user, id: owner }, visibility public.

schema.title: InventoryDefinitionPublishedPayload
schema.description: inventory.definition.published v1 (OpenVibe.Inventory, ADR-054). A definition became grantable (a service's on request, a creator's after review). Envelope: subject { type: item_definition, id }, visibility public.

schema.title: WorkIndexDocumentUpsertedPayload
schema.description: work.index_document.upserted v1 (OpenVibe.Work server/search-index.js, via openvibe-publishing/search-feed). The OpenVibe.Search document of a job listing page (type job, /jobs/<id>): the title, company, location, tags, salary text and the short excerpt Work keeps of a listing read from a public board, with the board as provenance (authorship imported). Sent after every ingest run that changed a listing and by the sweep (server/search-index.js); a listing that expired (not seen for the retention window) becomes a tombstone. The sequencer (work_index_revisions) gives an unchanged document its old revision and nothing is sent. Always visibility public and publication_state published; a page its own robots mark noindex stays in Search as a noindex document. Facets: source, remote, type, location. Consumed by OpenVibe.Search ('*.index_document.*'). Envelope: subject { type: job, id, revision: <document revision> }, visibility internal, actor service:work.

schema.title: WorkIndexDocumentDeletedPayload
schema.description: work.index_document.deleted v1 (OpenVibe.Work server/search-index.js, via openvibe-publishing/search-feed). A Search tombstone for a job page (/jobs/<id>) that is no longer listed or whose row is gone. Only sent for a page Search was sent before, and only when the tombstone's revision moved. Consumed by OpenVibe.Search ('*.index_document.*'). Envelope: subject { type: job, id, revision }, visibility internal, actor service:work.

revision.description: Index revision of the tombstone; wins over any document at the same or an older revision.

schema.title: HostIndexDocumentUpsertedPayload
schema.description: host.index_document.upserted v1 (OpenVibe.Host server/catalog/search-index.js, via openvibe-publishing/search-feed). The OpenVibe.Search document of a hosting catalog page: a plan (/catalog/plans/<id>: provider, plan name, vCPU, RAM, disk, transfer, monthly price and currency, the day the price was checked) or a provider (/catalog/providers/<slug>: its name, description and plan count), or a domain ending (type tld, /catalog/domains/<tld>, id tld-<tld> such as tld-dev or tld-co.uk: the cheapest first year, renewal and five years at any registrar and how many registrars list it; facets kind, register_usd, renew_usd). A plan from OpenVibe.Sources names its source as provenance (authorship imported); a staff entry names its source URL. A hidden or gone entry becomes a tombstone. The sequencer gives an unchanged document its old revision and nothing is sent. Facets: provider, kind, currency. Consumed by OpenVibe.Search ('*.index_document.*'). Envelope: subject { type: plan|provider|tld, id, revision }, visibility internal, actor service:host.

schema.title: HostIndexDocumentDeletedPayload
schema.description: host.index_document.deleted v1 (OpenVibe.Host server/catalog/search-index.js, via openvibe-publishing/search-feed). A Search tombstone for a hosting catalog page (a plan, a provider or a domain ending) that is hidden, gone or deleted. Only sent for a page Search was sent before, and only when the tombstone's revision moved. Consumed by OpenVibe.Search ('*.index_document.*'). Envelope: subject { type: plan|provider|tld, id, revision }, visibility internal, actor service:host.

revision.description: Index revision of the tombstone; wins over any document at the same or an older revision.

schema.title: RentIndexDocumentUpsertedPayload
schema.description: rent.index_document.upserted v1 (OpenVibe.Rent server/search-index.js, via openvibe-publishing/search-feed). The OpenVibe.Search document of a rental listing page (type listing, /listings/<id>): title, description, price and period, city, region, country and neighbourhood (never a street address or the contact link); or of a city page (type city, /in/<state>/<city>, id <state>-<city slug>, e.g. tx-austin): the city's typical rents by size from the Census ACS (facets state, population, rent_2br), sent by the sweep whenever the city data changed; or of an OpenVibe.Homes city page (type homes_city, https://openvibe.homes/in/<state>/<city>, the same id): the median home value and rent. Sent in the transaction that created, edited, renewed, hid or removed the listing, and by the sweep (server/search-index.js); a listing that is hidden, removed or past its expiry becomes a tombstone. The sequencer (rent_index_revisions) gives an unchanged document its old revision and nothing is sent. Always visibility public and publication_state published; a page its own robots mark noindex stays in Search as a noindex document. Facets: kind, country, city, currency, period, bedrooms. Consumed by OpenVibe.Search ('*.index_document.*'). Envelope: subject { type: listing, id, revision: <document revision> }, visibility internal, actor service:rent.

schema.title: RentIndexDocumentDeletedPayload
schema.description: rent.index_document.deleted v1 (OpenVibe.Rent server/search-index.js, via openvibe-publishing/search-feed). A Search tombstone for a listing page (/listings/<id>) that is no longer listed or whose row is gone, or for a city page on OpenVibe.Rent or OpenVibe.Homes (/in/<state>/<city>) that left the city data. Only sent for a page Search was sent before, and only when the tombstone's revision moved. Consumed by OpenVibe.Search ('*.index_document.*'). Envelope: subject { type: listing, id, revision }, visibility internal, actor service:rent.

revision.description: Index revision of the tombstone; wins over any document at the same or an older revision.

schema.title: HelpIndexDocumentUpsertedPayload
schema.description: help.index_document.upserted v1 (OpenVibe.Help server/search-index.js, via openvibe-publishing/search-feed). The OpenVibe.Search document of a help article page (type article, /a/<domain>/<slug>, id <domain>:<slug>): one question from a product manifest's FAQ with its answer, quoted verbatim from OpenVibe.Contracts. Sent by the sweep at boot and on a timer (server/search-index.js) whenever the catalog Help was built from changed; an article whose FAQ entry left the catalog becomes a tombstone. The sequencer (help_index_revisions) gives an unchanged document its old revision and nothing is sent. Always visibility public and publication_state published; a page its own robots mark noindex stays in Search as a noindex document. Facets: site (the product domain), kind. Consumed by OpenVibe.Search ('*.index_document.*'). Envelope: subject { type: article, id, revision: <document revision> }, visibility internal, actor service:help.

schema.title: HelpIndexDocumentDeletedPayload
schema.description: help.index_document.deleted v1 (OpenVibe.Help server/search-index.js, via openvibe-publishing/search-feed). A Search tombstone for a article page (/a/<domain>/<slug>) that is no longer listed or whose row is gone. Only sent for a page Search was sent before, and only when the tombstone's revision moved. Consumed by OpenVibe.Search ('*.index_document.*'). Envelope: subject { type: article, id, revision }, visibility internal, actor service:help.

revision.description: Index revision of the tombstone; wins over any document at the same or an older revision.

schema.title: InventoryIndexDocumentUpsertedPayload
schema.description: inventory.index_document.upserted v1 (OpenVibe.Inventory server/search-index.js, via openvibe-publishing/search-feed). The OpenVibe.Search document of an item definition page (type definition, /items/<id>): name, description, kind, rarity, issuer and supply. Only published definitions are documents; a draft, one in review or a retired one is a tombstone. Sent in the transaction that published or retired it, and by the sweep (server/search-index.js). The sequencer (inventory_index_revisions) gives an unchanged document its old revision and nothing is sent. Always visibility public and publication_state published; a page its own robots mark noindex stays in Search as a noindex document. Facets: kind, rarity, issuer. Consumed by OpenVibe.Search ('*.index_document.*'). Envelope: subject { type: definition, id, revision: <document revision> }, visibility internal, actor service:inventory.

schema.title: InventoryIndexDocumentDeletedPayload
schema.description: inventory.index_document.deleted v1 (OpenVibe.Inventory server/search-index.js, via openvibe-publishing/search-feed). A Search tombstone for a definition page (/items/<id>) that is no longer listed or whose row is gone. Only sent for a page Search was sent before, and only when the tombstone's revision moved. Consumed by OpenVibe.Search ('*.index_document.*'). Envelope: subject { type: definition, id, revision }, visibility internal, actor service:inventory.

revision.description: Index revision of the tombstone; wins over any document at the same or an older revision.

schema.title: QuestIndexDocumentUpsertedPayload
schema.description: quest.index_document.upserted v1 (OpenVibe.Quest server/search-index.js, via openvibe-publishing/search-feed). The OpenVibe.Search document of a quest page (type quest, /quests/<id>): its name, what to do and where, and the badge (and item) it rewards. Quests are Quest's own catalog (server/quests/catalog.js), so they are sent by the sweep at boot (server/search-index.js); a quest that left the catalog becomes a tombstone. The sequencer (quest_index_revisions) gives an unchanged document its old revision and nothing is sent. Always visibility public and publication_state published; a page its own robots mark noindex stays in Search as a noindex document. Facets: service (where the quest is done), badge. Consumed by OpenVibe.Search ('*.index_document.*'). Envelope: subject { type: quest, id, revision: <document revision> }, visibility internal, actor service:quest.

schema.title: QuestIndexDocumentDeletedPayload
schema.description: quest.index_document.deleted v1 (OpenVibe.Quest server/search-index.js, via openvibe-publishing/search-feed). A Search tombstone for a quest page (/quests/<id>) that is no longer listed or whose row is gone. Only sent for a page Search was sent before, and only when the tombstone's revision moved. Consumed by OpenVibe.Search ('*.index_document.*'). Envelope: subject { type: quest, id, revision }, visibility internal, actor service:quest.

revision.description: Index revision of the tombstone; wins over any document at the same or an older revision.

schema.title: WorkApplication
schema.description: work.application@1: a person's tracked job application on OpenVibe.Work (server/applications.js toWire), as GET/POST/PATCH /api/v1/me/applications[/:id] answer it. GET of one application adds its append-only status changes as `events`.

listing_id.description: The Work listing it was tracked from, or null when added by hand.

actor_task_id.description: The latest OpenVibe.Actor task asked for this application (POST …/assist).

schema.title: WorkApplicationWriteRequest
schema.description: work.application-write-request@1: bodies of work.application.manage. POST /api/v1/me/applications takes a listing_id (title, company and URL are copied from the listing; a second POST for the same listing answers the existing application with 200) or title + company + url by hand. PATCH /api/v1/me/applications/:id takes status, notes, applied_at, next_step and next_step_at; a status change appends an event, and status applied with no applied_at stamps it now. Unknown fields are 400.

schema.title: WorkApplicationResult
schema.description: work.application-result@1: what work.application.manage answers: one application, or a page of them (GET /api/v1/me/applications, newest first, ?status= and ?cursor=; `next` is the next page's cursor or null). DELETE answers 204 with no body.

schema.title: FoodRecipeSuggestRequest
schema.description: food.recipe-suggest-request@1: POST /api/v1/recipes/suggest. Asks OpenVibe.AI's food.suggest_recipes workflow for up to three recipes from the caller's saved pantry (an empty pantry is 422 food.pantry_empty). 10 a person a day (429 food.recipes_daily_limit); with Food's AI connection off, 503 food.ai_off.

schema.title: FoodRecipeSuggestion
schema.description: food.recipe-suggestion@1: one stored answer (the last 20 a person are kept). Ingredients are from the pantry or cite the food-list rows Food sent the workflow; to_buy and to_buy_cost are Food's own typical prices, never the model's. A recipe is AI-suggested and labelled so on the page.

schema.title: FoodRecipeResult
schema.description: food.recipe-result@1: what food.recipes.suggest answers: the new suggestion (POST /api/v1/recipes/suggest, 201) or the caller's recent ones (GET /api/v1/recipes).

schema.title: SpaceDeployCreateRequest
schema.description: space.deploy-create-request@1: bodies of space.deploy.create on OpenVibe.Space (a deployer or above of the project; an app principal added as deployer can deploy from CI). POST /api/v1/sites/:id/deploys uploads a deploy: the raw body is a tar or tar.gz archive (Content-Type application/gzip, application/x-gzip, application/x-tar or application/octet-stream), or multipart/form-data with archive=<one archive> or files=<file>… (each part's filename is its path); optional fields activate=1, root=<subdirectory to deploy> and strip=folder (removes a shared first segment) also work as query parameters. It is validated (path traversal, links, special and hidden files, server-side code, file types, sizes and quotas) and never executed; a refusal is a problem whose extra carries the failed deploy_id and its log (413 upload.too_large, quota.storage; 422 validation codes; 429 quota.deploys_per_day; 403 site.taken_down; 503 upload.busy; 507 storage.host_full). POST /api/v1/deploys/:id/activate { expected_active? } and POST /api/v1/sites/:id/rollback { deploy_id?, expected_active? } switch the site's pointer in one step (rollback without deploy_id goes to the deploy active before; 409 deploy.not_ready, site.active_changed when expected_active is stale, deploy.no_previous). GET /api/v1/sites/:id/deploys, /deploys/:id and /deploys/:id/log take no body.

anyOf.description: The upload itself: the tar or tar.gz bytes, or the multipart/form-data body (as common.binary@1).

expected_active.description: The deploy you saw active (null: none); refused with 409 site.active_changed when it moved.

schema.title: SpaceDeployCreateResult
schema.description: space.deploy-create-result@1: answers of space.deploy.create on OpenVibe.Space. GET /api/v1/sites/:id/deploys?limit= → { active_deploy_id, deploys, activations } (newest first; the last 20 pointer switches). POST /api/v1/sites/:id/deploys → 201 { deploy, activated, url } (the ready deploy with its validation log; activated when activate=1 switched the site to it). GET /api/v1/deploys/:id → { deploy } with its files. GET /api/v1/deploys/:id/log → { deploy_id, state, log }. POST /api/v1/deploys/:id/activate and /sites/:id/rollback → { active_deploy_id, previous_deploy_id, changed } (changed false when it was already active). Emits space.deploy.created|activated|failed.

schema.title: SpaceDeploy
schema.description: space.deploy@1: one immutable static deploy on OpenVibe.Space (server/http/serialize.js deploy): ready (validated and stored, never executed) or failed (refused, with its failure code and log), whether the site serves it, its size and manifest hash. GET /api/v1/deploys/:id adds the files; the upload answer adds the log.

git.description: Present on source git: the commit this deploy was built from (public provenance, never a credential).

new_bytes.description: Bytes this deploy added to the project's store.

schema.title: SpaceDomainManageRequest
schema.description: space.domain-manage-request@1: bodies of space.domain.manage on OpenVibe.Space (a maintainer or above of the project). POST /api/v1/sites/:id/domains { hostname } adds a custom domain, pending until its TXT record is verified: a fully qualified host name, lowercased (422 domain.invalid_hostname; 422 domain.reserved for any OpenVibe domain; 403 domain.sandbox in sandbox projects; 429 quota.custom_domains; 409 domain.exists, domain.taken). GET /api/v1/sites/:id/domains, POST /api/v1/domains/:id/verify (checks the TXT record now) and DELETE /api/v1/domains/:id (409 domain.default: the default domain goes only with the site) take no body.

hostname.description: e.g. www.example.org (a trailing dot is dropped).

schema.title: SpaceDomainManageResult
schema.description: space.domain-manage-result@1: answers of space.domain.manage on OpenVibe.Space. GET /api/v1/sites/:id/domains → { domains } (the default domain first). POST /api/v1/sites/:id/domains → 201 { domain } with the DNS records to publish. POST /api/v1/domains/:id/verify → { domain } after the check (status verified and served once the TXT record matches, else last_error says what was found; emits space.domain.verified). DELETE /api/v1/domains/:id → { deleted: true }.

schema.title: SpaceDomain
schema.description: space.domain@1: one domain of a static site on OpenVibe.Space (server/http/serialize.js domain): the default <site>.openvibe.website, or a custom domain that is served only once its DNS TXT record is verified (re-checked daily; it lapses when the record is gone). A custom domain carries the records its owner must publish (the TXT verification value is public by design and shown only to members); TLS certificates are issued by an operator.

name.description: _openvibe-space.<hostname>

routing.description: A CNAME for a subdomain; A/AAAA for an apex domain when the operator configured them.

schema.title: SpaceProject
schema.description: space.project@1: one OpenVibe.Space tenant project (server/http/serialize.js project): owned by a person (usr_…), production or sandbox, with the caller's role in it and any staff takedown. POST /api/v1/projects and GET /api/v1/projects/:id add the effective quota and the usage.

network_project_id.description: The OpenVibe.Network project once Network has projects.

role.description: The caller's role (staff: a Network admin who is not a member).

takedown.description: A staff takedown covering it: serving stops while the content is kept for review.

quota.description: The effective quota: the project's override where set, else its environment's default.

schema.title: SpaceSiteManageRequest
schema.description: space.site-manage-request@1: bodies of space.site.manage on OpenVibe.Space (judged by the acting principal's project role too; a sandbox token is refused on production projects). POST /api/v1/projects { name, environment?, network_project_id? } creates a project owned by the person named with X-OV-Subject (403 project.owner_must_be_user; 422 project.invalid_name over 80 characters, project.invalid_environment; 429 quota.projects; 409 project.network_project_taken). PUT /api/v1/projects/:id/quota { storage_bytes?, deploys_per_day?, max_files?, max_file_bytes?, sites?, custom_domains? } (a Network staff user: 403 auth.staff_only; fields left out keep their value). PUT /api/v1/projects/:id/members/:principal { role } (the owner: 422 member.invalid_role, 409 member.owner_fixed). POST /api/v1/projects/:id/sites { name } (a maintainer; lowercased and trimmed, one DNS label of 3–40 characters: 422 site.invalid_name, site.name_reserved; 409 site.name_taken, site.name_held; 429 quota.sites). POST /api/v1/projects/:id/takedown and /sites/:id/takedown { reason } (staff: stop serving, keep the content; 409 takedown.exists); DELETE on those { note? } lifts it. GET /api/v1/projects, /projects/:id, /projects/:id/quota, /projects/:id/sites and /sites/:id, and DELETE /api/v1/projects/:id, /projects/:id/members/:principal, /sites/:id and /deploys/:id take no body (deleting refuses taken-down content for non-staff: 409 site.taken_down; an active deploy: 409 deploy.active).

name.description: 1–80 characters once trimmed.

environment.description: Default production; a sandbox credential creates sandbox projects only.

storage_bytes.description: A non-negative integer, or null for the environment default.

deploys_per_day.description: A non-negative integer, or null for the environment default.

max_files.description: A non-negative integer, or null for the environment default.

max_file_bytes.description: A non-negative integer, or null for the environment default.

sites.description: A non-negative integer, or null for the environment default.

custom_domains.description: A non-negative integer, or null for the environment default.

role.description: Only a person (usr_…) can be an owner.

name.description: The site name (lowercased).

reason.description: Members see it.

schema.title: SpaceSiteManageResult
schema.description: space.site-manage-result@1: answers of space.site.manage on OpenVibe.Space. GET /api/v1/projects → { projects } (the caller's projects with their role). POST /api/v1/projects → 201 { project } (with quota and usage). GET /api/v1/projects/:id → { project, sites, members }. GET and PUT /api/v1/projects/:id/quota → { quota, usage }. PUT and DELETE /api/v1/projects/:id/members/:principal → { members }. GET /api/v1/projects/:id/sites → { sites }. POST /api/v1/projects/:id/sites → 201 { site }. GET /api/v1/sites/:id → { site, domains }. DELETE /api/v1/projects/:id and /sites/:id → { deleted: true } (serving stops at once; the objects are removed). DELETE /api/v1/deploys/:id → { deleted: true, objects_removed }. POST …/takedown → 201 { takedown }; DELETE …/takedown → { lifted: true }.

quota.description: The effective quota: the project's override where set, else its environment's default.

schema.title: SpaceSite
schema.description: space.site@1: one static site on OpenVibe.Space (server/http/serialize.js site): its name (one DNS label), the default hostname and URL it is served at, the deploy it serves (one pointer; null until a deploy is activated) and any staff takedown.

takedown.description: A staff takedown covering it: serving stops while the content is kept for review.

schema.title: SpaceSiteConfig
schema.description: space.site-config@1: one Host site's serving configuration (plan T12 J3). headers are applied to every response of the site before the platform's own, which always win; the platform's security, routing, caching, scope and transport headers (Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, Set-Cookie, Cache-Control, Content-Type, Location, Service-Worker-Allowed, Alt-Svc and the rest of Host's reserved list) and every X-Forwarded-* header are refused. redirects are local paths only (no scheme, host, protocol-relative URL, backslash or control character, also after percent-decoding). spa serves /index.html for an extensionless path that has no file. A site with no configuration answers { headers: {}, redirects: [], spa: false }.

schema.title: SpaceSiteConfigRequest
schema.description: space.site-config-request@1: the body of PUT /api/v1/sites/:id/config on OpenVibe.Space (space.site.config; the acting principal must be a maintainer or owner of the site's project). { headers?, redirects?, spa? } replaces the whole configuration: a field left out is reset to its default. A redirect's status defaults to 301. Refusals are 422 problem+json: site_config.reserved_header, site_config.header_name, site_config.header_value (longer than 1024 characters or a control character), site_config.too_many (over 50 headers or 200 redirects), site_config.redirect (not a local path, a duplicate from, or a status outside 301/302/307/308), site_config.headers and site_config.redirects (wrong type). GET and DELETE /api/v1/sites/:id/config take no body (DELETE resets to the defaults).

schema.title: SpaceSiteConfigResult
schema.description: space.site-config-result@1: every answer of space.site.config on OpenVibe.Space. GET, PUT and DELETE /api/v1/sites/:id/config → { config } (after a PUT, the configuration as stored; after a DELETE, the defaults).

schema.title: SpaceDeployActivatedPayload
schema.description: space.deploy.activated v1 (OpenVibe.Space server/domain/deploys.js switchPointer, Stage B tenant hosting). A tenant site's active deploy changed, written into Host's event outbox in the transaction that moves the pointer (activate or rollback). Envelope: subject { type: deploy, id: <deploy id> }, visibility internal, priority low, actor the person or app that switched it. A network service's release going live is space.release.published, not this.

previous_deploy_id.description: The deploy that served before; null for the site's first activation.

rollback.description: true when the switch was a rollback.

schema.title: SpaceDeployCreatedPayload
schema.description: space.deploy.created v1 (OpenVibe.Space, subject deploy dpl_…, visibility internal): an upload or a Git ingest became an immutable, content-addressed deploy in the ready state. It is not yet serving: space.deploy.activated follows when it is made active. No file contents or paths.

site.description: the site name (one DNS label; the site is served at <site>.openvibe.website)

source.description: how the deploy arrived: an archive or individual files, a private preview upload, or a Git ingest (always a preview)

manifest_sha256.description: sha256 of the deploy manifest (the content address of the whole deploy)

schema.title: SpaceDeployFailedPayload
schema.description: space.deploy.failed v1 (OpenVibe.Space, subject deploy dpl_…, visibility internal): an upload was refused and recorded as a failed deploy with its log, so the owner can see why. Problem codes only, at most ten; never file contents.

site.description: the site name (one DNS label; the site is served at <site>.openvibe.website)

code.description: the refusal problem code (for example deploy.too_large or storage.space_full)

problems.description: the problem codes of the files that were refused

schema.title: SpaceDomainVerifiedPayload
schema.description: space.domain.verified v1 (OpenVibe.Space, subject domain dom_…, visibility internal): a custom domain's TXT record (_openvibe-space.<hostname>) was found, and the domain now serves the site.

site.description: the site name (one DNS label; the site is served at <site>.openvibe.website)

hostname.description: the custom domain, a fully qualified host name in lower case

schema.title: VideoPlaylist
schema.description: video.playlist@1: one playlist on openvibe.video as the API returns it. `owner` is present on reads of one playlist: a person (kind user, with their username when known) or an app, agent or service (never named).

id.description: A playlist id (vpl_ + ULID).

schema.title: VideoPlaylistReadRequest
schema.description: video.playlist-read-request@1: video.playlist.read takes no body. GET /api/v1/video/playlists (the caller's own), GET /api/v1/video/playlists/:id (the owner sees a private one; anyone a public or unlisted one; otherwise 404 playlist.not_found, never 403) and the open GET /api/v1/video/users/:username/playlists, whose query is { limit?, cursor? } (limit 1-50, default 20; cursor is the previous page's next_cursor; 404 user.not_found).

schema.title: VideoPlaylistReadResult
schema.description: video.playlist-read-result@1: a list ({ playlists, next_cursor? }) or one playlist with its ordered items ({ playlist, items }).

kind.description: An OpenVibe.Live recording (vod) or clip.

id.description: The item's OpenVibe.Live id.

schema.title: VideoPlaylistManageRequest
schema.description: video.playlist-manage-request@1: bodies of video.playlist.manage on openvibe.video. POST /api/v1/video/playlists { title, description?, visibility? } creates one (default private; 422 playlist.invalid_title over 120 characters, playlist.invalid_description over 2,000, playlist.invalid_visibility, playlist.limit at 100 per owner). PATCH /api/v1/video/playlists/:id { title?, description?, visibility? }. POST /api/v1/video/playlists/:id/items { kind, id } adds one (409 playlist.item_duplicate; 422 playlist.invalid_kind, playlist.invalid_item, playlist.items_limit at 500). PATCH /api/v1/video/playlists/:id/items { items: [{ kind, id }, ...] } reorders: the full list, each item once (422 playlist.invalid_items). DELETE /api/v1/video/playlists/:id and /items/:kind/:itemId take no body. Another owner's playlist answers 404 playlist.not_found.

kind.description: An OpenVibe.Live recording (vod) or clip.

anyOf.description: The item's OpenVibe.Live id.

kind.description: An OpenVibe.Live recording (vod) or clip.

schema.title: VideoPlaylistManageResult
schema.description: video.playlist-manage-result@1: { playlist } after a create (201, Location) or an edit, { item } after an add (201), { items } after a reorder; a delete answers 204 with no body.

kind.description: An OpenVibe.Live recording (vod) or clip.

id.description: The item's OpenVibe.Live id.

kind.description: An OpenVibe.Live recording (vod) or clip.
