schema.title: CodesTaskStartRequest
schema.description: codes.task-start-request@1: the body of POST /api/v1/tasks on OpenVibe.Codes (capability codes.task.start). A first-party service (OpenVibe.Actor) starts a coding task for a person, named with X-OV-Subject: Codes runs it on that person's own machine through OpenVibe.Run (openvibe.codes/run, plan T16), in the project of their latest task there, so the person has used openvibe.codes/run once before a service can start one for them (else 409 codes.no_project). REPO is an https git URL with no credentials; REF a branch or tag to start from (default: the repository's default branch). PROMPT is the task. AGENT names one of Codes' agents (GET /harnesses), absent for Codes' router to pick. PERMISSION: review (read-only: research, audits, reviews; nothing is changed), edit (default; the agents edit files) or full (they may also run commands: tests, installs). PUSH asks for the change on a new branch (GitHub, with the machine's GITHUB_TOKEN; never the branch it started from), PULL_REQUEST also opens a pull request. IDEMPOTENCY_KEY: a repeat for the same person with the same key answers the first task (200, created false).

actor_task_id.description: The OpenVibe.Actor task id when this coding task was started from Actor.

actor_step_id.description: The OpenVibe.Actor step id when this coding task was started from Actor.

schema.title: CodesTaskStartResult
schema.description: codes.task-start-result@1: the answer of POST /api/v1/tasks (201 created, or 200 with created false for a repeated idempotency key).

schema.title: CodesTask
schema.description: codes.task@1: a coding task on OpenVibe.Codes, as GET /api/v1/tasks/:id answers it (capability codes.task.read) and POST /api/v1/tasks creates it. STATE follows the OpenVibe.Run job that carries it: queued (waiting for one of the person's machines), placed, running, then succeeded, failed, cancelled or expired (no machine of theirs took it in time). URL is the task's page on openvibe.codes, where its owner follows it live. RESULT is present once it has ended: OK says whether the agents finished, SUMMARY what they said, FILES and PATCH the change (the patch at most 256 KiB, PATCH_TRUNCATED when cut), PUSH where it went when asked, COST_USD the model use on the person's own keys, DURATION_MS the time on their machine. ERROR says why a task that never ran ended (Run refused it, or the job failed before a result).

id.description: The Codes task id (tsk_ + ULID).

actor_ref.description: The OpenVibe.Actor task and step that started this coding task, when it came from Actor.

schema.title: CodesTask
schema.description: codes.task@2: a coding task on OpenVibe.Codes, as GET /api/v1/tasks/:id answers it (capability codes.task.read) and POST /api/v1/tasks creates it. It is codes.task@1 with two added fields: ATTEMPTS, the task's timeline (each try of the task, with the state it ended in and why), and OUTCOME, what the task's attempts added up to (done, unfinished with what is left, or stopped). STATE follows the OpenVibe.Run job that carries it: queued (waiting for one of the person's machines), placed, running, then succeeded, failed, cancelled or expired (no machine of theirs took it in time). URL is the task's page on openvibe.codes, where its owner follows it live. RESULT is present once it has ended: OK says whether the agents finished, SUMMARY what they said, FILES and PATCH the change (the patch at most 256 KiB, PATCH_TRUNCATED when cut), PUSH where it went when asked, COST_USD the model use on the person's own keys, DURATION_MS the time on their machine. ERROR says why a task that never ran ended (Run refused it, or the job failed before a result).

id.description: The Codes task id (tsk_ + ULID).

actor_ref.description: The OpenVibe.Actor task and step that started this coding task, when it came from Actor.

attempts.description: The task's timeline: every try of it, in order. The first is the task itself; the others are what the agents did after it (the same conversation carried on, another agent taking over, a last turn before a limit).

id.description: The attempt id (att_ + ULID).

n.description: The attempt's number, 1 for the first try.

machine.description: The node that ran the attempt, or sandbox when it ran in a sandbox.

session.description: The harness session, so a following attempt can carry on in the same conversation.

why.description: One plain sentence: why this attempt happened, or how it ended.

end_why.description: How the attempt ended, in plain words.

outcome.description: What the task's attempts added up to: done, unfinished (with what is left), or stopped. Null while the task still runs.

schema.title: PlayTitleDefinition
schema.description: A title as its own principal registers it (play.title.manage, PUT /api/v1/titles/:title). Achievements and boards are listed in display order; one left out is retired, never deleted. A board's kind never changes.

url.description: where the game is played

hidden.description: a secret achievement: its name and text show only to whoever unlocked it

kind.description: best: each player's best score; sum: the total of their scores

schema.title: PlayTitleResult
schema.description: The answer to registering or updating a title: the title as anyone reads it, and whether this call created it (201) or updated it (200).

schema.title: PlayResultRequest
schema.description: What a title's principal posts about its players (play.result.write): a round's scores to a board (POST …/scores; idempotent by ref), achievements a player unlocked (POST …/unlocks), or the person a guest became (POST …/players/:guest/adopt).

ref.description: the round or run; a repeat changes nothing

at.description: epoch milliseconds, never in the future (an import of past results); default now

player.description: a person (usr_) or a guest the title names (guest:<opaque>)
a person (usr_) or a guest the title names (guest:<opaque>)

at.description: epoch milliseconds, never in the future (an import of past results); default now

schema.title: PlayResultResponse
schema.description: The answer to a result post: scores recorded and repeated, the achievements that were new, or the unlocks and scores a guest's adoption moved.

schema.title: PlayPlayerAchievements
schema.description: One player's unlocked achievements in a title the caller manages (play.player.read), newest first.

player.description: a person (usr_) or a guest the title names (guest:<opaque>)

schema.title: AccessKey
schema.description: media.access-key@1 (ADR-031, amended 2026-10-14): one S3 access key of OpenVibe.Media's S3 surface (https://s3.openvibe.media). It is bound to one project environment, reads and/or writes, and may be scoped to some zones of that environment (zone.object-zone@1 ids; empty means every zone). Media issues and verifies it: SigV4 needs the secret, so the party that checks signatures keeps it, encrypted, and shows it once (media.access-key-issued@1). The secret is never part of this record. A revoked key is refused at once; a key scoped only to a zone that is deleted is revoked with it. More fields may be added.

id.description: The S3 access key id.

name.description: What uses the key, as the person who issued it named it.

zones.description: The zones it may reach; empty = every zone of the environment.

last_used_at.description: The last signed request, to the minute.

schema.title: AccessKeyIssueRequest
schema.description: media.access-key-issue-request@1 (ADR-031): the body of POST /api/v1/projects/:project_id/access-keys on OpenVibe.Media (capability media.access_key.manage), sent by a first-party service (OpenVibe.Zone, OpenVibe.Services) for the person in on_behalf_of, who must be an admin or owner of the project (Network decides). The answer is 201 media.access-key-issued@1. A zone that is not an active zone of this project environment answers 404 media.access_key.unknown_zone; more than 50 live keys in one environment answer 409 media.access_key.limit.

schema.title: AccessKeyIssued
schema.description: media.access-key-issued@1 (ADR-031): the 201 of POST /api/v1/projects/:project_id/access-keys. `secret` is the S3 secret access key; it is in this answer only, and Media never shows it again. A caller relays it to the person once and keeps no copy.

schema.title: AccessKeyList
schema.description: media.access-key-list@1 (ADR-031): GET /api/v1/projects/:project_id/access-keys (capability media.access_key.manage, for a project admin in on_behalf_of): every key of the project, newest first, revoked ones included. No secret is ever listed.

schema.title: QuestAppQuestRequest
schema.description: quest.app-quest-request@1: PUT /api/v1/app-quests/:slug on OpenVibe.Quest with an app token (capability quest.app_quest.manage). A developer app defines a quest on its own project's events: each step counts events of type app.<project_key>.<name> whose envelope actor is a person (the app publishing on_behalf_of them). The badge is the only reward: app quests never pay OpenCoins. Only production apps' events are counted (Events never hands sandbox events to first-party consumers).

event_type.description: One of the app's own event types (app.<project_key>.<name>), as it publishes them at OpenVibe.Events.

url.description: Where a person does the steps: the app's own page.

status.description: retired: kept with its completions and badges, no longer counted or listed. Default active.

schema.title: QuestAppQuest
schema.description: quest.app-quest@1: one app quest as OpenVibe.Quest keeps it (the answer to PUT and GET /api/v1/app-quests[/:slug]). id is app.<project_key>.<slug>; badge.id is the same id; completions counts the people who finished it.

app.description: The app that last defined it.

event_type.description: One of the app's own event types (app.<project_key>.<name>), as it publishes them at OpenVibe.Events.

schema.title: ChatInboxRequest
schema.description: chat.inbox-request@1: a support inbox, made (POST /api/chat/inboxes, name required) or changed by its owner (PATCH /api/chat/inboxes/:id, any subset). Unknown fields are ignored; a bad value is 422 with a code (inbox.name, inbox.origin, inbox.hours, inbox.retention, …). Members (POST /:id/members { username }), saved replies (POST /:id/replies { shortcut, body }), webhooks (POST /:id/webhooks { url }), actions (POST /:id/actions { name, description, url, params }) and verified visitors (POST /:id/identity { action: on | rotate | off }) take their own small bodies on the routes chat.inbox.manage names.

greeting.description: The first line a visitor sees.

ai_instructions.description: What Vibe should know and how to answer (content, never rules that override Chat's).

knowledge_urls.description: https pages Vibe may read (an array, or one a line).

allowed_origins.description: The sites the widget answers (empty: any).

handoff.description: The inbox's people answer too (false: a site assistant where only Vibe answers).

hours.description: When the people answer; null: always.

route.description: round_robin: a visitor waiting for a person goes to the next of the people.

retention_days.description: How long finished conversations stay; null: forever.

schema.title: ChatInboxResult
schema.description: chat.inbox-result@1: a support inbox as its people see it ({ inbox, members?, embed? }: the widget snippet and panel address), or the inboxes a person works in ({ inboxes }, each with their role and how many conversations wait and are open). Secrets (the identity secret, webhook and action secrets) appear only on the answer that made them.

schema.title: ChatInboxReplyRequest
schema.description: chat.inbox-reply-request@1: what one of an inbox's people sends while working a conversation (chat.inbox.reply). A reply (POST /api/chat/inboxes/:id/conversations/:cid/messages { message }: the conversation becomes open, Vibe stays quiet in it, and the person takes it if nobody has); a status or an assignment (PATCH /:id/conversations/:cid { status: open | resolved | bot, assignee_id: one of the inbox's people | null }); a translation (POST /:id/conversations/:cid/messages/:mid/translate { to } or POST /:id/translate { text, to }). Marking read (POST /:id/conversations/:cid/read) takes no body.

schema.title: ChatInboxConversationsResult
schema.description: chat.inbox-conversations-result@1: an inbox's conversations ({ conversations }: waiting first, each with status, who has it, the visitor's name and whether their site verified them, a preview and unread count), one conversation's messages ({ conversation, messages }, ?after= a message id), a reply ({ message }), its saved replies ({ replies }), or the owner's export (?format=json: { inbox, exported_at, conversations: [{ …, messages }] }; ?format=csv is text/csv, one row per message). A message is { id, author: visitor | agent | ai | system, author_name, body, created_at, account? }.

schema.title: RunSession
schema.description: run.session@1 (the Desks plan's D6): one session on OpenVibe.Run, a browser desk held for one person, as GET /api/v1/sessions/{id} answers it (capability run.session.read) and run.session-list-result@1, POST /api/v1/sessions (run.session.create) and POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/end (run.session.control) carry it. A session is a desk (bot.command@1 kind desk, kind browser) that Run places on a machine and OpenVibe.Bot leases to it (bot.desk-lease@1): on one of the person's own machines where they let agents use it (trust user-owned, never another person's), or on a desk host that serves other people (trust first-party or community: the host's OpenVibe.Node runs every desk in its own sandbox, desk_isolation sandbox, and offers nothing else of the machine). STATES: placing (stored, looking for a machine) -> starting (the desk is leased and starting) -> running (the desk answered) -> ended. An ended session never changes; end.reason says why: ended (POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/end), ttl (ttl_s ran out), idle (no command for idle_s), host_lost (its machine went away or stopped the desk), unplaceable (no machine had room before ttl_s, or none at all) or failed (the desk would not start). USAGE: desk_seconds counts from started_at to ended_at (or now while running), metered to OpenVibe.Billing as one platform.usage-sample@1 per minute (service run, operation browser.desk, unit s, idempotency_key run:<session id>:<minute>). Run mints the id (ses_<ULID>).

owner.description: The person the session is for: only they (or a first-party service acting for them) read, act on or end it.

via.description: The first-party service that asked for the person (service:actor), or null when they asked themselves.

kind.description: A platform.runtime-class@1 name; browser (a headless browser driven over its pipe) is the only kind of session in v1.

ttl_s.description: The most the session lives, from created_at.

idle_s.description: A session no command used this long ends (end.reason idle).

size.description: The desk's page size (bot.command@1 kind desk width and height).

machine.description: The machine (OpenVibe.Bot device) the desk runs on.

desk.description: The desk's name there (bot.command@1 desk), leased to this session alone.

trust.description: The offer's trust class (platform.resource-offer@1): user-owned is always the owner's own machine.

offer_id.description: The platform.resource-offer@1 it was placed on; null when the request named the person's own machine.

reasons.description: Why this machine, in a few words each (the placer's reasons).

started_at.description: When the desk first answered (state running).

desk_seconds.description: Seconds the desk ran (started_at to ended_at, or to now while running); 0 when it never started.

reasons: a shared desk host with room

schema.title: RunSessionCreateRequest
schema.description: run.session-create-request@1 (the Desks plan's D6): the body of POST /api/v1/sessions on OpenVibe.Run (capability run.session.create), answered 201 with run.session@1 (state placing). The session is the caller's own: a person's token, or a first-party service acting for a person (X-OV-Subject; the service is recorded as via). MACHINE names one of the person's own machines (an OpenVibe.Bot device they own and let agents use): the session goes there or ends unplaceable, never elsewhere. Without it Run places the desk: on the person's own machines when REQUIREMENTS name user-owned (and only theirs), else on desk hosts that serve other people (first-party, then community, unless REQUIREMENTS narrow it), each of whose desks runs in its own sandbox. Absent REQUIREMENTS mean { kind: run.browser, mobility: session, latency_class: interactive, objective: balanced }. TTL_S (default 3600) and IDLE_S (default 900) bound its life. IDEMPOTENCY_KEY: a repeat from the same person within 24 h with an identical body answers the first session (200); with a different body 409 run.idempotency.conflict.

machine.description: One of the person's own machines, by its OpenVibe.Bot id; the session goes there or nowhere.

schema.title: RunSessionControlRequest
schema.description: run.session-control-request@1 (the Desks plan's D6): one command on a session's desk, the body of POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/commands on OpenVibe.Run (capability run.session.control), answered with run.session-control-result@1. KIND and VALUE are bot.command@1's for that kind (screen: a picture of the page; input: the mouse, wheel and keys on the page; browser: open, click, fill, press, back, read, screenshot) without desk, which is always the session's own: Run carries the command to OpenVibe.Bot on the session's lease (bot.desk-lease@1) and nothing on the machine other than that desk is reachable. A command on a session that is not running is refused 409 run.session.not_running. ID makes a retry safe: the same id within the session answers the first result.

value.description: bot.command@1's value for that kind, without desk (refused 422 if it names another desk).

schema.title: RunSessionControlResult
schema.description: run.session-control-result@1 (the Desks plan's D6): the answer to run.session-control-request@1. RESULT is bot.command-result@1's: ack (the desk did it; DATA is its answer, a page as text and refs, a picture, a receipt), nack (the desk refused; CODE is its fault code and REASON says why), refused (OpenVibe.Bot's gate refused it; CODE is Bot's refusal code) or expired (no answer in time). Every answer also says how the session stands now, so a caller sees it end (idle, ttl, host_lost) without asking again.

data.description: The desk's answer on an ack (bot.command-result@1 data).

schema.title: RunSessionListResult
schema.description: run.session-list-result@1 (the Desks plan's D6): GET /api/v1/sessions on OpenVibe.Run (capability run.session.read): the caller's own sessions, newest first, running ones by default (?state=ended or ?state=all for others), at most limit (default 20, at most 100) per page; next_cursor continues the list and is null on the last page.

schema.title: RunSessionStartedPayload
schema.description: run.session.started v1 (OpenVibe.Run; the Desks plan's D6). A session's desk answered for the first time: it runs on its machine, and desk_seconds count from timings.started_at. The session as run.session@1 has it. Envelope: subject { type: session, id: <session id> }, visibility internal, priority low, actor service:run.

schema.title: RunSessionEndedPayload
schema.description: run.session.ended v1 (OpenVibe.Run; the Desks plan's D6). A session ended (end.reason ended, ttl, idle, host_lost, unplaceable or failed), its desk stopped and its lease given back; usage.desk_seconds is final. The session as run.session@1 has it. Envelope: subject { type: session, id: <session id> }, visibility internal, priority low, actor service:run.

schema.title: BotDeskLease
schema.description: bot.desk-lease@1 (the Desks plan's D6): one desk OpenVibe.Bot holds for one OpenVibe.Run session, as POST /api/v1/machines/{id}/desk-leases answers it (201, capability bot.desk.session, a Run service token acting for the session's person in X-OV-Subject) and GET /api/v1/machines/{id}/desk-leases/{desk} reads it. The request is bot.desk-lease-create-request@1. Bot leases a desk only on the person's own machine where they turned on 'Let my agent use this computer' (shared false), or on a desk host whose owner offers its desks to other people and whose OpenVibe.Node runs each desk in its own sandbox (describe desk.isolation sandbox; shared true). The lease starts the desk (bot.command@1 kind desk, start, kind browser, the lease's size) and from then on only the lease's person, through Run, may act on that desk, with screen, input and browser at POST /api/v1/machines/{id}/desk-leases/{desk}/commands (bot.command@1 without desk, answered by bot.command-result@1): never another desk, never the machine's own screen, files, programs or network, and on a shared host not even its owner's own commands reach a leased desk. DELETE /api/v1/machines/{id}/desk-leases/{desk} stops the desk and ends the lease; so does the machine going away (Run sees the lease gone, 404, and ends the session host_lost).

owner.description: The session's person, the only one whose commands reach the desk.

shared.description: true on a desk host that serves other people (the desk runs in its own sandbox there); false on the person's own machine.

schema.title: BotDeskLeaseCreateRequest
schema.description: bot.desk-lease-create-request@1 (the Desks plan's D6): the body of POST /api/v1/machines/{id}/desk-leases on OpenVibe.Bot (capability bot.desk.session), answered 201 with bot.desk-lease@1. DESK is the name Run chose for the session (unique per session); a desk already leased to another session, or running for the machine's owner, is refused 409 bot.desk_busy, and a repeat for the same session answers its lease (200). A machine with no room (its max_desks) is refused 409 bot.machine_busy, one that is offline 409 bot.device_offline, and one the person may not use 404 bot.device_not_found.

schema.title: ActionItem
schema.description: One piece of a person's agent work in the Action Center (plan 2026-10-28 §3.10): an agent task, a coding task, an AI run, or an approval waiting on them. Each authority answers its own items in this shape (common.action-list-result@1); OpenVibe.Network merges them into buckets (network.me-actions-result@1). Text is plain (no markup); a cost is what the person was charged in USD, null when unknown or free; href is a page on the authority's own public site.

service.description: The authority that owns the item.

id.description: The authority's own id (tsk_…, a Codes task id, run_…, a confirmation id, dpr_…).

kind.description: What the item is.

title.description: A short plain-text name: the start of the task text, the workflow, or what the approval is for.

summary.description: The last step, the outcome, or what will happen on approval.

bucket.description: Where the Action Center shows it: running (queued or working), waiting (needs the person), scheduled (will run later), done, failed (failed, cancelled or expired).

state.description: The authority's own state word (queued, running, needs_you, succeeded, failed, cancelled, pending…).

agent.description: The agent, model or workflow doing it, when known.

cost_usd.description: What it cost the person, in US dollars; null when unknown or free.

steps.description: Tool calls or steps so far, when counted.

error.description: Why it failed, in words a person can act on.

next_run_at.description: When a scheduled item runs next.

href.description: The item's page: its live steps, receipt or approval.

actions.description: What the person can do from the list. approve/decline/cancel/retry go through OpenVibe.Network (POST /api/v1/me/actions/:service/:id/:action); open is a link.

schema.title: ActionListResult
schema.description: One authority's Action Center items for a person (capabilities actor.actions.read, codes.actions.read, ai.actions.read, domains.actions.read): GET /api/v1/actions?subject=usr_… with the caller's service token. Everything running, waiting or scheduled, then done and failed items from the last 30 days, newest first, at most 50.

schema.title: MeActionsResult
schema.description: The Action Center for the signed-in person (capability network.actions.read, GET /api/v1/me/actions): every authority's items merged into five buckets, newest first in each. sources says how each authority answered; a slow or failing one is left out (partial true), never fails the answer.

schema.title: NetworkDockState
schema.description: network.dock-state@1 (the Dock plan 2026-10-30, K-D1): the state of one person's Dock — the little floating surface every OpenVibe site draws. It lives in the Network, not in the browser, because localStorage is per site and the Dock follows the person across every domain. GET /api/v1/me/dock and PUT /api/v1/me/dock on OpenVibe.Network.

open.description: Whether the Dock is open (a sheet on a phone, a floating card on a desktop) or collapsed to its pill.

tab.description: Which of the Dock's three tabs shows: the agent's screen, the chats, the activity.

pinned.description: Keep the pill on screen even when nothing runs and nothing waits.

agent.description: The agent the Agent tab follows, or null when it follows none.

chat.description: The conversation the Chats tab has open, or null.

phone.description: Where the Dock sits on a phone.

desktop.description: Where the Dock sits on a desktop, and how big it is (null: the site's own default size).

updated_at.description: When the state was last written.

schema.title: NetworkDockResult
schema.description: network.dock-result@1 (the Dock plan 2026-10-30, K-D1): what GET /api/v1/me/dock answers on OpenVibe.Network — the person's Dock state, the counts the pill's status dot is drawn from, and whether those counts are complete.

state.description: The person's Dock state: the stored one, or the default when they have never opened the Dock.

running.description: How many of the person's agents are running.

unread.description: How many notifications the person has not read.

sources_partial.description: True when an authority behind the counts did not answer, so the counts are lower than the truth.

schema.title: NetworkConsent
schema.description: network.consent@1 (L24, data and AI by consent, 2026-10-31): one person's choice for one purpose. Nothing a person makes is off-limits to AI or data use by design; each use is off until that person turns it on, here. The record is the proof of what was allowed, by whom, under which wording and when: a choice is turned off by setting revoked_at, never by deleting the row. Stored by OpenVibe.Network (consents, with every change in consent_events), read by a person at GET /api/v1/me/consent and by services through POST /internal/consent/check (capability network.consent.read). A service that cannot reach Network treats every purpose as off.

id.description: The choice's own id (cns_<ULID>). A choice changed later (other kinds, another licence) is a new record; the old one is revoked.

subject.description: Whose choice it is. Only that person (or an account merge or deletion) changes it.

purpose.description: What turning it on allows. ai.train: OpenVibe trains or fine-tunes models on the person's content. data.public: the person's content goes into OpenVibe's open dataset under the licence in options. face.recognize: the person's face is recognised (the features in options; OpenVibe.Vision keeps the encrypted templates). ai.looks is retired (0.256.0): the owner removed the rule that AI text never describes people (2026-10-31), so describing how someone looks needs no opt-in; it stays in the list so older readers still validate, and nothing writes it. app.data: one named app (client) may use the person's content for the purposes in options.

on.description: Whether the purpose is allowed now: true while the record is active (revoked_at null and expires_at not passed). A service never decides from this field alone; it asks the check.

kinds.description: Which of the person's content it covers. Empty means every kind the purpose applies to. face.recognize and ai.looks take no kinds (they are about the person, not a piece of content).

client.description: The app the choice is for: null means OpenVibe itself; otherwise the OAuth client id of an app the person granted (required for app.data, and only there).

licence.description: data.public only: the licence the person's content is published under.

features.description: face.recognize only: which recognition the person allows (OpenVibe.Vision's features). Empty means none yet.

purposes.description: app.data only: what the app may do with the person's content, as the consent screen showed it.

options.description: What the purpose needs beyond on and kinds. An empty object for ai.train and ai.looks.

text_version.description: The exact wording the person saw when choosing (YYYY-MM-DD.n). A new wording never turns an existing choice on; it may only ask again.

source.description: Where the choice was made: the account page, an app's consent screen, the person's own API call, or OpenVibe.Vision's older face consents moved into Network.

granted_at.description: When the person turned it on.

revoked_at.description: When it was turned off (by the person, by revoking the app, by a merge or by deleting the account), or null while it holds. Use stops on the next check; a model already trained keeps what it learned, and the next dataset release leaves the person's content out.

expires_at.description: When the choice ends by itself (a time-limited grant, or the end of a face purpose), or null for no end.

schema.title: NetworkConsentChoice
schema.description: network.consent-choice@1 (L24): the body of PUT /api/v1/me/consent/:purpose on OpenVibe.Network — the signed-in person turns a purpose on or off. Turning on records the wording they saw (text_version, which must be the current one) and, for the adults-only purposes, that they confirmed they are 18 or older. Turning off revokes the active choice. An app's choice (app.data) is made on its consent screen, not here.

text_version.description: The wording the page showed. Required to turn on; a stale one is refused (consent.stale_text) so the page shows the new words first.

adult.description: The person confirmed they are 18 or older. Required (true) to turn on face.recognize, ai.looks, ai.train or data.public.

schema.title: NetworkMeConsentResult
schema.description: network.me-consent-result@1 (L24): "Your data choices" for the signed-in person. GET /api/v1/me/consent (and the answer to PUT /api/v1/me/consent/:purpose and DELETE /api/v1/me/consent/:purpose/:client) on OpenVibe.Network. Every purpose is listed with the words the account page shows, whether the person has turned it on, and the history of their changes. Off is the default for every purpose.

allows.description: What turning it on allows, in one plain line.

cannot_undo.description: What turning it off cannot undo (empty when nothing).

adults_only.description: Turning it on asks the person to confirm they are 18 or older.

kinds.description: The kinds of content the person may narrow it to (empty: the purpose takes none).

consents.description: The person's active choices (network.consent@1), one per purpose and app.

by.description: Who made the change: the person, the app being revoked, an account merge, an account deletion, or the move of an older record.

schema.title: NetworkConsentCheckRequest
schema.description: network.consent-check-request@1 (L24): may this purpose be used for these people? POST /internal/consent/check on OpenVibe.Network with a service token holding network.consent.read. One purpose per call, up to 500 subjects (a dataset build or a chat log checks its authors in batches).

kind.description: The kind of content the use is about. A choice limited to other kinds answers false.

client.description: app.data only: the app asking. Required for app.data.

feature.description: face.recognize only: the recognition about to run.

subjects.description: The people the use would be about.

schema.title: NetworkConsentCheckResult
schema.description: network.consent-check-result@1 (L24): the answer to network.consent-check-request@1. Every subject asked about is in allowed: true only for an active choice that covers the purpose, the kind, the app and the feature asked about. An unknown or deleted subject is false, the same as a person who never chose (the answer never says whether an account exists). A service caches an answer for at most 60 s and drops it on network.consent.changed; when Network cannot answer, every subject is false.

allowed.description: Each subject asked about, and whether the use is allowed for them.

licence.description: data.public only: the licence each allowed subject chose.

schema.title: NetworkConsentChangedPayload
schema.description: network.consent.changed v1 (OpenVibe.Network, L24): a person turned a purpose on or off, an app's grant was revoked, or a choice expired. A service that caches consent answers drops that subject's answers for the purpose at once; one that is running a use for the subject (a dataset build, a recognition, an AI text) checks again before it goes on. The payload names the change and never the content it covers.

on.description: Whether the purpose is allowed after the change.

schema.title: TodayEventScheduledPayload
schema.description: today.event.scheduled v1 (OpenVibe.Today server/events/store.js, written to its outbox in the same transaction as the change and published once per evt_ id). A person put a stream or an event on OpenVibe.Today's calendar (POST /api/v1/events or the schedule form). Envelope: source today, subject and actor { type: user, id: <owner usr_> }, visibility internal, priority important. OpenVibe.Network tells a streamer's followers about a scheduled public or followers-only stream (STREAM_SCHEDULED) and clears those notices on cancel (server/notifications/events-consumer.js).

event_id.description: Today's id for the calendar entry (not the envelope's evt_ id).

channel.description: The owner's Live username for a stream; null for an event.

tz.description: The IANA zone it was scheduled in.

url.description: Where it happens (a stream: its Live channel page).

seq.description: The calendar SEQUENCE: up by one with every change.

schema.title: TodayEventUpdatedPayload
schema.description: today.event.updated v1 (OpenVibe.Today server/events/store.js, written to its outbox in the same transaction as the change and published once per evt_ id). Its title, times, zone, description or visibility changed (seq went up), or it went live or ended (live.stream.started / ended). Envelope: source today, subject and actor { type: user, id: <owner usr_> }, visibility internal, priority important. OpenVibe.Network tells a streamer's followers about a scheduled public or followers-only stream (STREAM_SCHEDULED) and clears those notices on cancel (server/notifications/events-consumer.js).

event_id.description: Today's id for the calendar entry (not the envelope's evt_ id).

channel.description: The owner's Live username for a stream; null for an event.

tz.description: The IANA zone it was scheduled in.

url.description: Where it happens (a stream: its Live channel page).

seq.description: The calendar SEQUENCE: up by one with every change.

schema.title: TodayEventCancelledPayload
schema.description: today.event.cancelled v1 (OpenVibe.Today server/events/store.js, written to its outbox in the same transaction as the change and published once per evt_ id). Its owner cancelled it: calendars that subscribe drop it (STATUS:CANCELLED), and OpenVibe.Network clears the followers' notices. Envelope: source today, subject and actor { type: user, id: <owner usr_> }, visibility internal, priority important. OpenVibe.Network tells a streamer's followers about a scheduled public or followers-only stream (STREAM_SCHEDULED) and clears those notices on cancel (server/notifications/events-consumer.js).

event_id.description: Today's id for the calendar entry (not the envelope's evt_ id).

channel.description: The owner's Live username for a stream; null for an event.

tz.description: The IANA zone it was scheduled in.

url.description: Where it happens (a stream: its Live channel page).

seq.description: The calendar SEQUENCE: up by one with every change.

schema.title: CodesTaskQueuedPayload
schema.description: codes.task.queued v1 (OpenVibe.Codes): a coding task was stored and handed to OpenVibe.Run; the person's machine has not started it. Envelope: source codes, subject { type: user, id: <owner usr_> }, visibility internal.

repo.description: owner/name from the task's repository URL, or null when it is not a repository path.

schema.title: CodesTaskRunningPayload
schema.description: codes.task.running v1 (OpenVibe.Codes): Run placed or started the task on the person's machine (both task states placed and running announce as running). Envelope: source codes, subject { type: user, id: <owner usr_> }, visibility internal.

repo.description: owner/name from the task's repository URL, or null when it is not a repository path.

schema.title: CodesTaskSucceededPayload
schema.description: codes.task.succeeded v1 (OpenVibe.Codes): the task ended and its result is stored on the task page. cost_usd and files_changed are the machine's result (null when it returned neither). Envelope: source codes, subject { type: user, id: <owner usr_> }, visibility internal.

repo.description: owner/name from the task's repository URL, or null when it is not a repository path.

schema.title: CodesTaskFailedPayload
schema.description: codes.task.failed v1 (OpenVibe.Codes): the task ended failed, or expired because no machine took it in time (Run's expired state is announced on the failed topic). Envelope: source codes, subject { type: user, id: <owner usr_> }, visibility internal.

repo.description: owner/name from the task's repository URL, or null when it is not a repository path.

schema.title: CodesTaskCancelledPayload
schema.description: codes.task.cancelled v1 (OpenVibe.Codes): the task ended cancelled, by its owner or by a service holding codes.task.cancel. Envelope: source codes, subject { type: user, id: <owner usr_> }, visibility internal.

repo.description: owner/name from the task's repository URL, or null when it is not a repository path.

schema.title: DomainsProposal
schema.description: A change to a person's DNS on OpenVibe.Domains (plan 2026-10-28 §5.1): nothing an agent, a bulk edit or the person's own edit asks for touches DNS until the person approves it. A proposal holds the record diff, why, what could break, and its rollback; approving it applies the changes in order through the provider's API with the person's connected credential (a Network project secret, ADR-056, never part of this document). A change whose record moved since the proposal was made is refused as stale; rolling back applies the inverse changes.

risk.description: What could break, in plain words.

record_id.description: The provider's record id (update, delete; a create's after it is applied).

name.description: The full record name (example.com, www.example.com).

ttl.description: Seconds; 1 is the provider's automatic TTL.

proxied.description: Cloudflare's proxy, for A, AAAA and CNAME; null elsewhere.

name.description: The full record name (example.com, www.example.com).

ttl.description: Seconds; 1 is the provider's automatic TTL.

proxied.description: Cloudflare's proxy, for A, AAAA and CNAME; null elsewhere.

type.description: A registrar change: the domain's nameservers at the registry. op is update only; before and after are the lists.

schema.title: VisionUiCheckRequest
schema.description: vision.ui-check-request@1: the JSON body of POST /api/v1/ui-check on OpenVibe.Vision (Design's Arena and signed-in people; HTML, URL and screenshot checks also work anonymously). Send exactly one source: `html` with the markup, `url` with a public http(s) page, `image` with a data URL, or `image_url` with a public image URL. The multipart form field `image` is the same screenshot source. `viewport` defaults to 1280x800 and is clamped to 160..10000; the check executes no JavaScript and fetches only a public URL through the SSRF guard.

html.description: The HTML to check, including any inline CSS.

url.description: A public page to fetch and check.

image.description: A screenshot as an image data URL.

schema.title: VisionUiCheckResult
schema.description: vision.ui-check-result@1: the answer of POST /api/v1/ui-check and GET /api/v1/ui-checks/:id on OpenVibe.Vision. `check` names the engine that ran (static HTML/CSS or a screenshot through OCR boxes and pixels), the viewport, every finding with its stable kind and severity, and the summary the saved row keeps. No image bytes are returned; a screenshot is identified only by its sha256.

schema.title: VisionImageRequest
schema.description: vision.image-request@1: one image for OpenVibe.Vision's one-shot tools, as a data URL or a public URL. The multipart form field `image` carries the same bytes. Private tools (find, index, watch, moments) accept only uploaded bytes or a data URL, never an unverified source URL.

image.description: The image as a data URL (base64).

image_url.description: A public image URL, fetched through Vision's private-address guard.

schema.title: VisionAskRequest
schema.description: vision.ask-request@1: the body of POST /api/v1/ask and /api/v1/describe on OpenVibe.Vision. `task` is what the caller wants (ask, describe, identify, count, translate, ocr); `mode` is auto (local OCR first, then OpenVibe.AI), local (never a model) or ai. A read question (text, sign, receipt, label) is answered by the local OCR reader first in auto mode. `lang` is the Tesseract language and `model` is a provider:model hint AI may ignore.

image.description: The image as a data URL (base64).

image_url.description: A public image URL, fetched through Vision's private-address guard.

schema.title: VisionOcrRequest
schema.description: vision.ocr-request@1: the body of POST /api/v1/ocr. The local Tesseract 5 reader runs on Vision's host and costs nothing; `fallback` asks OpenVibe.AI only when the local pass found no usable text, which needs a signed-in person or a service token holding vision.ocr.

image.description: The image as a data URL (base64).

image_url.description: A public image URL, fetched through Vision's private-address guard.

schema.title: VisionCompareRequest
schema.description: vision.compare-request@1: the body of POST /api/v1/compare. One image runs through the local reader and up to three AI hints; the requested model is a hint only, and each row reports the provider and model OpenVibe.AI says answered.

image.description: The image as a data URL (base64).

image_url.description: A public image URL, fetched through Vision's private-address guard.

schema.title: VisionFindRequest
schema.description: vision.find-request@1: the body of POST /api/v1/index and of GET or POST /api/v1/find. `index` stores a scoped CLIP embedding for one of the caller's own items (`item_id`, optional `result_url`); `find` searches only the caller's own private index, by words (`q`) or by an example image. No public image index is ever built.

image.description: The image as a data URL (base64).

image_url.description: A public image URL, fetched through Vision's private-address guard.

schema.title: VisionReceiptRequest
schema.description: vision.receipt-request@1: the body of POST /api/v1/receipt. The local OCR reader extracts line items and a total; `fallback` asks OpenVibe.AI only when the local pass could not produce both.

image.description: The image as a data URL (base64).

image_url.description: A public image URL, fetched through Vision's private-address guard.

schema.title: VisionProductRequest
schema.description: vision.product-request@1: the body of POST /api/v1/product. The image is embedded locally with CLIP; `allow_rerank` lets one routed model reorder the candidate offers. Candidates come from OpenVibe.Deals and open.shoes; Vision never invents a price.

image.description: The image as a data URL (base64).

image_url.description: A public image URL, fetched through Vision's private-address guard.

schema.title: VisionWatchRequest
schema.description: vision.watch-request@1: the body of POST /api/v1/watch (owner-granted camera alerts). `classes` names 1–20 things to look for (snow, delivery, package, a DETR label, or "scene change"); `previous_image` is required for a scene change and is compared by histogram.

image.description: The image as a data URL (base64).

image_url.description: A public image URL, fetched through Vision's private-address guard.

schema.title: VisionMomentsRequest
schema.description: vision.moments-request@1: the body of POST /api/v1/moments. Up to 30 timestamped frames are compared with CLIP prompt embeddings; a histogram jump marks a scene change. VOD and stream chapters come from this.

schema.title: VisionAnswer
schema.description: vision.answer@1: one saved answer on OpenVibe.Vision. It names the engine, model, provider and route that actually answered (never a model hint), the reason it was chosen, the cost OpenVibe.AI reported, the measured latency and the confidence. No image bytes are stored: only a sha256 and the declared media type.

answer.description: Engine details, OCR words, provenance and any compare rows; never an image.

schema.title: VisionAnswerResult
schema.description: vision.answer-result@1: what POST /api/v1/ask, /describe and /ocr answer (`{ answer }`), and POST /api/v1/compare answers with `compare` rows and the local reader's summary added. Every AI-written text has passed noLooks: a look-naming answer is replaced, never repaired word by word.

schema.title: VisionAltResult
schema.description: vision.alt-result@1: POST /api/v1/alt answers one short, editable alt-text sentence about the scene, objects and action, never about a person. The text has passed noLooks; the receipt says which engine answered and at what cost.

schema.title: VisionFindResult
schema.description: vision.find-result@1: POST /api/v1/index and GET/POST /api/v1/find answer a scoped private search over the caller's own indexed items: `results` (item_id, result_url, score) only, no one else's rows and no public index.

schema.title: VisionReceiptResult
schema.description: vision.receipt-result@1: POST /api/v1/receipt answers the store, the line items and the total the local OCR reader read (or the routed fallback read), with `raw_text` when the local pass produced it. OpenVibe.Food decides what enters a pantry; Vision returns the reading.

schema.title: VisionProductResult
schema.description: vision.product-result@1: POST /api/v1/product answers a description of the product only (never a person), the CLIP embedding, and candidate offers from OpenVibe.Deals and open.shoes with their score, price and URL. A room must not treat a candidate as a price it verified.

schema.title: VisionWatchResult
schema.description: vision.watch-result@1: POST /api/v1/watch answers the requested classes found in a camera still (DETR labels, snow/delivery/package through CLIP, or a histogram scene change), each with a confidence and, for an object, a box.

schema.title: VisionMomentsResult
schema.description: vision.moments-result@1: POST /api/v1/moments answers scene changes and candidate moments (timestamp, matching prompt, score) for up to 30 frames. A moment is a suggestion: the room decides whether it becomes a clip or a chapter.

schema.title: VisionFaceDetection
schema.description: vision.face-detection@1: POST /api/v1/faces/detect, an identity-free YuNet privacy tool. It counts faces and returns their boxes and scores; it stores no template, names no one and needs no consent. Anyone may use it.

schema.title: VisionFaceBlur
schema.description: vision.face-blur@1: POST /api/v1/faces/blur answers a redacted PNG derivative and the number of faces blurred in X-Faces-Blur. Identity-free, no template, and the original is never stored.

schema.title: VisionFaceEnrolRequest
schema.description: vision.face-enrol-request@1: POST /api/v1/faces/enrol/:feature. `feature` is verify (1:1 verification of yourself), find (search your own uploads) or cast (an adult tagging named streams); each needs its own signed consent first, and cast also names the channel scope.

image.description: The image as a data URL (base64).

image_url.description: A public image URL, fetched through Vision's private-address guard.

schema.title: VisionFaceVerify
schema.description: vision.face-verify@1: POST /api/v1/faces/verify compares this person's own verification attempt with their enrolled template. It always requires that person's verify consent; without it the answer is faces.consent_required whether or not a template exists. A match alone never unlocks anything: liveness and a second factor are separate.

schema.title: VisionFaceFindResult
schema.description: vision.face-find-result@1: POST /api/v1/faces/find lists the caller's own private uploads that match their enrolled self-search template, as private links and scores. It requires find consent; without it the answer is faces.consent_required whether or not any media exists.

schema.title: VisionFaceCastMatchRequest
schema.description: vision.face-cast-match-request@1: POST /api/v1/faces/cast/match, called by OpenVibe.Live with a service token scoped to one channel (vision.face.cast.match). It matches only that channel's opted-in adult roster; a person who has not enrolled for this channel cannot appear, and the answer does not say whether they exist.

image.description: The image as a data URL (base64).

image_url.description: A public image URL, fetched through Vision's private-address guard.

schema.title: VisionFaceCastMatch
schema.description: vision.face-cast-match@1: the matches inside one channel's consented roster, each with a score and box. No other subject is named and no non-roster face is described.

schema.title: VisionFaceTag
schema.description: vision.face-tag@1: one cast tag on a stream: which subject, which channel, which private media reference and when. GET /api/v1/faces/cast/tags lists the caller's own tags; revoking the cast consent removes them.

schema.title: VisionFaceTagList
schema.description: vision.face-tag-list@1: GET /api/v1/faces/cast/tags answers the caller's own cast tags, newest first, as a bare array. Empty when they have not consented to cast matching.

schema.title: VisionFaceLibraryRequest
schema.description: vision.face-library-request@1: POST /api/v1/faces/library/cluster (region-gated), GET /library/groups and POST /library/correct. `action` is cluster (default), exclude, merge or split; `ids` names up to 100 of the caller's own clusters; `region` is a jurisdiction code the host allows. Unknown faces stay unlabelled.

schema.title: VisionFaceLibraryResult
schema.description: vision.face-library-result@1: clustering and group reads answer the caller's own private face groups as an array; a correction answers the action and how many clusters it updated.

schema.title: VisionFaceLibraryGroup
schema.description: vision.face-library-group@1: one private face cluster in a person's own Vision library: the media it came from, the group it was merged into, an optional label and whether the person excluded it. It never leaves that person's library.

schema.title: VisionConsent
schema.description: vision.consent@1: one consent record on OpenVibe.Vision. It says whose face or voice it is (`subject`), the modality, the purpose-scoped feature and scope (a channel or a library), who signed which text version, when it was granted, when it expires, and how and when it was revoked. Face matching tools refuse without an active record for that person, with the same answer whether or not the person exists. Templates are deleted when the purpose ends and at the latest three years after the last use (BIPA); a revoked audit record is deleted one year after the purpose ends (CUBI).

subject.description: The person whose face or voice this consent covers.

scope.description: Empty means the person's own account; a cast grant names one channel, a library grant the library it applies to.

granted_by.description: The person who signed; the subject themself, or a guardian where the law allows.

expires_at.description: When the consent stops applying on its own; null when it lasts until revoked.

revoked_by.description: How it was revoked: by the person, by the retention job, or with the account.

retention_until.description: The outer limit the record and derived data may exist: three years after last use, or one year after the purpose ended.

erased.description: True once the template and derived results this consent covered are gone.

schema.title: VisionConsentRequest
schema.description: vision.consent-request@1: POST /api/v1/faces/consents/:feature. The caller signs the current text (`text_version` must match this server's), names themself (`signed_name`), and for cast must confirm they are an adult; library grouping is refused outside the host's allowed regions. A repeat of an active consent changes nothing.

schema.title: VisionConsentRevocation
schema.description: vision.consent-revocation@1: DELETE /api/v1/faces/consents/:feature answers with the revoked feature and scope, when, and that the template and derived data were erased in the same transaction. Revocation removes past cast tags and cannot be undone by reusing an old text version.

schema.title: VisionModels
schema.description: vision.models@1: GET /api/v1/models names the AI route's offered provider:model hints, the configured hints and the local engines present, without any subject data. OpenVibe.AI's router remains the authority: this is a menu, not a promise.

schema.title: VisionBenchmarks
schema.description: vision.benchmarks@1: GET /api/v1/benchmarks aggregates compare samples per task, engine, provider and model with sample counts and mean latency and cost. No subject, image or answer text is included.

schema.title: VisionResultReadyPayload
schema.description: vision.result.ready v1 (OpenVibe.Vision): a visual result is ready for its owner or caller. Envelope: source vision, subject { type: user, id: <requester> } (or { type: service, id: <caller> } when no person asked), visibility subject for a person and internal otherwise. The payload carries the identifiers, the engine and provenance, cost, latency and retention, never an image, a template or an answer text.

schema.title: VisionAlertPayload
schema.description: vision.alert v1 (OpenVibe.Vision): an owner-granted camera alert. Envelope: source vision, subject { type: user, id: <source owner> }, visibility subject. The payload names the watched source reference and the classes found with their confidence; it carries no image bytes and no person's identity.

schema.title: BenchKind
schema.description: bench.kind@1: a benchmark kind on OpenVibe.Bench. ROOM is the room that owns the kind, ENTRY the shape a submitted entry takes, JUDGE the default judge (pair, rubric, automatic_grader, test_suite or game_outcome), NAME the display name, SCHEMA the entry JSON Schema, and METRICS the board metrics (elo, pareto, cost, or a room's own).

schema.title: BenchTask
schema.description: bench.task@1: a benchmark task on OpenVibe.Bench. KIND_ID names the kind; PROMPT is the task; TASK_CLASS is an optional classifier for grouping; PUBLIC says whether the task may appear in the open dataset.

schema.title: BenchRound
schema.description: bench.round@1: a pinned, reproducible benchmark round on OpenVibe.Bench. TASK_ID names the task; OFFERS are the exact offers (provider, model, route) the round runs; STATUS follows queued, running, ready, finished or failed; SEED and RECEIPT make the round reproducible.

schema.title: BenchEntry
schema.description: bench.entry@1: one submitted entry in a benchmark round on OpenVibe.Bench. PROVIDER and MODEL name the offer; ROUTE is the exact route taken; PAYLOAD is the entry's output; COST_USD, MS and TOKENS are the measured use.

schema.title: BenchJudgement
schema.description: bench.judgement@1: a blind judgement cast on a benchmark round on OpenVibe.Bench. JUDGE names the judge (pair, rubric, automatic_grader, test_suite, game_outcome); METHOD is how the pair was decided; PAIR is the two entry ids; OUTCOME and SCORE are the result.

schema.title: BenchRating
schema.description: bench.rating@1: a rating on a benchmark board on OpenVibe.Bench. CATEGORY and SUBJECT identify what is rated (a model, a route or a room's own subject); ELO, GAMES, WINS, LOSSES, TIES and WIN_RATE are the score; CI_LOWER and CI_UPPER bound the estimate.

schema.title: BenchRoundFinishedPayload
schema.description: bench.round.finished v1 (OpenVibe.Bench): a pinned round reached finished with at least two usable entries and is ready for judgements. Envelope: source bench, subject { type: user, id: <created_by> }, visibility first-party.

schema.title: BenchJudgementRecordedPayload
schema.description: bench.judgement.recorded v1 (OpenVibe.Bench): a judgement was cast on a round. Envelope: source bench, subject { type: user, id: <judge> } or { type: service, id: <judge> }, visibility first-party.

schema.title: BenchRatingChangedPayload
schema.description: bench.rating.changed v1 (OpenVibe.Bench): a rating moved on a benchmark board. Envelope: source bench, subject { type: service, id: bench }, visibility first-party.

schema.title: GraphLink
schema.description: graph.link@1: a directed, typed relation between canonical OpenVibe object names (plan 2026-10-28 section 4.1). The owning service supplies the OVRNs and relation; no graph producer is live yet.

rel.description: Typed relation, for example derivedFrom, on, soldBy or cites.

schema.title: ReportMetric
schema.description: report.metric@1: one count computed or ingested by Report, with a UTC day or a window. Money values come from Billing's API; Report does not derive them. Mirrors OpenVibe.Report docs/report.metric.v1.json on origin/main.

schema.title: BenchBenchmark
schema.description: bench.benchmark@1: a versioned, forkable benchmark on OpenVibe.Bench (spec 2026-10-30, stage B1). It holds the tasks, the judges, how they combine into one score, the limits a run may not pass, the default model and harness matrix, and the visibility of the set. A version is immutable once a run names it; a fork records its parent. Holdout tasks are hidden from everyone but the executor.

id.description: The benchmark id; the same id carries every version.

owner.description: Who owns the set: a person (usr_…), a project (prj_…) or a service.

kind.description: One of Bench's kinds; the kind sets the renderer.

visibility.description: public appears in the registry; unlisted is reachable by id only.

version.description: The version number this document is.

parent.description: The benchmark id@version this one was forked from, or null.

expected.description: What a correct answer looks like; the judge reads it.

holdout.description: A hidden task: it is withheld from everyone but the executor, against tuning to the set.

type.description: human_pairwise | rubric | automatic_grader | test_suite | game_outcome

version.description: The pinned judge version; a run names the judge it used.

ms.description: The time one task may take.

usd.description: The money one run may spend.

schema.title: BenchRun
schema.description: bench.run@1: one result on OpenVibe.Bench (spec 2026-10-30, stage B1): a benchmark version × a model × a harness × settings × who ran it. It records the environment, the per-task scores, cost, time and tokens, the rendered artifacts, and the provenance: verified (executed by openvibe.codes or a Run worker) or submitted (posted through the API with no executor). Submitted runs are badged and kept out of the default rankings.

benchmark.description: The benchmark id@version the run names. The version is immutable once a run names it.

route.description: The route that produced the run.

hardware.description: The machine for a local model: GPU, CPU, RAM, quantization.

score.description: The benchmark's one score for this run, 0-100.

provenance.description: verified: an executor ran it. submitted: posted with no executor, badged and out of the default rankings.

kind.description: codes: an openvibe.codes task. run: a Run worker. node: the person's own machine. submitted: nobody ran it.

schema.title: BenchRunV2
schema.description: bench.run@2: scores may be null while human judges have not scored verified outputs yet.

benchmark.description: The benchmark id@version the run names. The version is immutable once a run names it.

route.description: The route that produced the run.

hardware.description: The machine for a local model: GPU, CPU, RAM, quantization.

score.description: The benchmark's score for this run, or null while human judges have not scored it yet.

provenance.description: verified: an executor ran it. submitted: posted with no executor, badged and out of the default rankings.

kind.description: codes: an openvibe.codes task. run: a Run worker. node: the person's own machine. submitted: nobody ran it.

score.description: The task score, or null while human judges have not scored it yet.

schema.title: AiMemoryItem
schema.description: ai.memory-item@1 (OpenVibe.AI; Memory M2): one memory item as the person's own API reads it. Tenant is the owner (`user:usr_…`); the text is decrypted only inside AI's process and never logged, never in an error, a span or an event. `source_ref` is the file path relative to the scanned root and the heading, when the item came from a file.

scope.description: `user` for the person's own notes, or `project:<slug>` for a repo or folder they chose. Never an absolute path.

text.description: The item text after the server-side redaction. Only the person's own routes and a granted agent search see it.

source.description: The adapter id (claude-code, cursor, …) or the service (actor, vibe, know, person).

source_ref.description: The path relative to the scanned root and the heading, when the item came from a file.

machine.description: The Node machine id it came from, when it came from one.

no_looks.description: True when the item was produced by an AI: the server ran noLooks on it (Memory M2 rule 5).

schema.title: AiMemoryResult
schema.description: ai.memory-result@1 (OpenVibe.AI; Memory M2): what the memory API answers: a list of items (GET /items, the batch import), one item (GET or PATCH /items/{id}), the cached profile (GET /profile), a count of deleted rows (DELETE) or the agent search's items (GET /search, at most 8, active only). The text is the person's own and is never logged.

text.description: The cached summary of the person's own notes for this scope. It passed noLooks before it was stored.

items_hash.description: sha256 of the sorted item MACs the profile was built from.

schema.title: AiMemoryWriteRequest
schema.description: ai.memory-write-request@1 (OpenVibe.AI; Memory M2): the body of POST /api/v1/memory/items:batch (up to 200 items), PATCH /api/v1/memory/items/{id} (text, kind, scope or status) and DELETE /api/v1/memory/items?source= (the source to delete). Secret shapes are redacted again on the server, and an item that is only a secret is refused. AI-produced items are suggestions until the person accepts them.

schema.title: AiMeCredentialV1
schema.description: ai.me-credential@1 (OpenVibe.AI; L36 Y1): one of the person's own provider keys as the person reads it from GET /api/v1/me/credentials. It is never the key: `hint` is the last four characters, and `last_error` is a redacted line that never carries the key. `status` is what the last save-time or run-time check found: ok, failing or untested. `models_count` is how many models the provider listed when it was last tested. Own keys are free to their owner: no fee, no cap and no network budget.

hint.description: The key's last four characters, so the person can tell two keys apart. Never more.

base_url.description: The endpoint the person chose, or null for the provider's own (taken from the console presets).

budget_usd_per_day.description: The person's own daily cap on this key; null or 0 means no cap. The network's budgets never apply to their own key.

last_error.description: Why the key last failed, with the key and any other secret redacted. Never the key itself.

schema.title: AiMeCredentialPutV1
schema.description: ai.me-credential-put@1 (OpenVibe.AI; L36 Y1): the person stores or replaces their own provider key at PUT /api/v1/me/credentials/{provider}. Only the person's own Network token or their AI site session may send it. `key` is required the first time and whenever `base_url` changes; a later save may leave it out to keep the stored key. The key is sealed at rest, tested on save and never returned, logged or put in an error.

provider.description: The provider. The route names it too; when both are present they must agree. A custom provider must name its endpoint in base_url.

key.description: The provider key. Required the first time and whenever base_url changes; optional afterwards, when the stored key is kept. Never returned.

base_url.description: The endpoint, for a custom provider or to override the provider's own. https only, no credentials, query or fragment; reached through the guarded fetcher's egress rules.

budget_usd_per_day.description: The person's own daily cap on this key; 0 or absent means no cap.

models.description: The model this key should use per kind of work. `auto` is not a model: absent means the provider's default, and the person's ai.me-preferences choose between keys.

schema.title: AiMeCredentialTestV1
schema.description: ai.me-credential-test@1 (OpenVibe.AI; L36 Y1/Y8): the answer to POST /api/v1/me/credentials/{provider}/test and to the test that runs on save. It lists the provider's models (up to five samples), or, when it lists none, makes a one-token request to its cheapest model. `ok` is false for a refused key, an empty endpoint or a timeout (10 s). `error` is a redacted line that never carries the key. `balance` is present only when the provider reports one.

schema.title: AiMeCredentialListV1
schema.description: ai.me-credential-list@1 (OpenVibe.AI; L36 Y1): GET /api/v1/me/credentials — every provider key the person holds themselves, without any key. Ordered by provider so a page can render it steadily.

schema.title: AiMePreferencesV1
schema.description: ai.me-preferences@1 (OpenVibe.AI; L36 Y1/Y3): how one person's AI runs route, stored per person under GET/PUT /api/v1/me/ai/preferences. `only_my_keys` means exactly that: a failed or missing key is never quietly replaced by a paid route. `free_first` puts free tiers ahead of paid ones. `price_ceiling_usd_per_mtok` caps the network's paid fallback per million tokens; the person's own keys are never capped. Each default is a model id or `auto`.

modelChoice.description: A model id, or `auto` to let placement choose.

schema.title: AiCredentialFailedPayload
schema.description: ai.credential.failed v1 (OpenVibe.AI; L36 Y8): a provider refused one of a person's own keys with 401 or 403 during a run. The key's status becomes failing and this event tells the products that may show it. `error` is a redacted line that never carries the key. Envelope: on_behalf_of the person, subject { type: credential, id: <subject>:<provider> }, visibility internal, priority important, actor service:ai.

error.description: The redacted reason. Never the key.
